\textbf{Sporophyte} & \hyperref[gl:diploid]{\textbf{Diploid (2n)}}
generation; produces spores by meiosis; dominant in vascular plants \\
\textbf{Gametophyte} & Haploid (n) generation; produces gametes by
mitosis; dominant in bryophytes \\
\textbf{Sporopollenin} & Highly resistant polymer of pollen exine;
survives millions of years in sediment \\
\textbf{Tube cell} & Vegetative cell of pollen grain; forms the pollen

\textbf{Generative cell} & Cell of pollen grain that divides to produce

\textbf{Microsporogenesis} & Meiotic + mitotic divisions producing
pollen grain from microspore mother cell \\
\textbf{Megasporogenesis} & Meiotic divisions producing functional
megaspore from megaspore mother cell \\
\textbf{Synergid} & Two cells flanking the egg in the embryo sac;
secrete LURE peptides; regulate sperm release \\
\textbf{Filiform apparatus} & Cell-wall labyrinth at the synergid
micropylar pole; secretes LURE peptides \\
\textbf{Central cell} & Large embryo sac cell containing two polar
nuclei; gives rise to endosperm (3n; 2m:1p) \\
\textbf{Antipodal cells} & Three cells at the chalazal end of embryo
sac; nutritive function \\
\textbf{Double fertilisation} & Unique to angiosperms: sperm 1 + egg =
embryo (2n); sperm 2 + polar nuclei = endosperm (3n) \\
\textbf{LURE peptides} & Cysteine-rich defensin-like peptides from
synergids; species-specific pollen tube attractants \\
\textbf{FERONIA-LORELEI} & Receptor complex on synergid surface;
required for pollen tube rupture \\
\textbf{ABCDE model} & Model of floral organ identity; combinatorial
MADS-box TF activity specifies each whorl \\
\textbf{MADS-box} & DNA-binding domain in floral organ identity
transcription factors; binds CArG-box motifs \\
\textbf{AP1, AP3, PI, AG, SEP} & MADS-box gene families: A, B, B, C, E
classes respectively \\
\textbf{Floral quartet} & Tetrameric MADS-box complex specifying organ
identity by binding two CArG boxes \\
\textbf{Sporophytic SI} & Self-incompatibility where pollen
\hyperref[gl:phenotype]{\textbf{phenotype}} determined by diploid
tapetum; SRK-SCR system \\
\textbf{Gametophytic SI} & Self-incompatibility where pollen phenotype
determined by its own haploid genotype; S-RNase/SLF \\
\textbf{Polyploidy} & Whole-genome duplication; about 70\% of
angiosperms are paleopolyploids \\
\textbf{Autopolyploid} & Polyploid arising within a single species \\
\textbf{Allopolyploid} & Polyploid arising from interspecific
hybridisation followed by chromosome doubling \\
\textbf{Phyllotaxis} & Arrangement of leaves/organs on stem; golden
angle 137.5 degrees; Fibonacci spirals \\
\textbf{WUS-CLV3 circuit} & Negative feedback loop maintaining stem cell
population in the SAM \\
\textbf{Karrikins} & Smoke-derived butenolides; activate KAI2 receptor;
break seed dormancy after fire \\
\textbf{Apomixis} & Asexual reproduction through seed without
fertilisation; produces maternal clones \\
\textbf{Adventive embryony} & Sporophytic apomixis: embryos from
nucellar/integument cells \\
\textbf{Apospory} & Gametophytic apomixis with embryo sac from somatic
cell \\
\textbf{Diplospory} & Gametophytic apomixis with embryo sac from
modified meiosis \\
\textbf{MiMe} & Mitosis-instead-of-Meiosis triple knockout (OSD1, PAIR1,
REC8); basis of synthetic apomixis \\
\textbf{Endosperm} & Triploid (3n; 2m:1p) nutritive tissue in angiosperm
seeds; stores starch, protein, oils \\
\textbf{Free-nuclear endosperm} & Endosperm form with multiple nuclei in
shared cytoplasm before cellularisation \\
\textbf{PEG (Paternally Expressed Gene)} & Gene expressed primarily from
paternal allele in endosperm \\
\textbf{MEG (Maternally Expressed Gene)} & Gene expressed primarily from
maternal allele in endosperm \\
\textbf{FIS-PRC2} & Polycomb complex (MEA-FIS2-FIE-MSI1) regulating
endosperm imprinting \\
\textbf{Heterospory} & Production of two different spore sizes (micro-
and megaspores); precursor to seed habit \\
\textbf{Pericarp} & Mature ovary wall comprising exocarp, mesocarp, and
endocarp; forms the fruit \\
\textbf{Parthenocarpy} & Fruit development without fertilisation; can be
natural or induced by auxin/GA \\
\textbf{Climacteric fruit} & Fruit type with autocatalytic ethylene
burst at ripening (banana, tomato, apple) \\
\textbf{System 1/System 2 ethylene} & Basal vs auto-catalytic ripening
ethylene biosynthesis \\
\textbf{1-MCP} & Synthetic ethylene perception inhibitor used
commercially to delay fruit ripening \\
\textbf{Stratification} & Cold-moist treatment that breaks seed
dormancy; simulates winter \\
\textbf{Scarification} & Physical or chemical disruption of seed coat
enabling water uptake \\
\textbf{DOG1} & Master regulator of seed dormancy; QTL in
\emph{Arabidopsis} \\
\textbf{\hyperref[gl:totipotency]{Totipotency}} & Ability of a single
plant cell to regenerate an entire organism \\

\subsection{Review Questions}\label{review-questions-28}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\item
  Compare the male gametophyte of a \emph{Pinus} tree to that of a
  \emph{Solanum lycopersicum} (tomato). How many cells in each? Where is
  mitosis 2 completed? How is sperm delivered to the egg? What is the
  evolutionary significance of the reduction in gametophyte size?
\item
  An \emph{Arabidopsis} triple mutant lacks functional A, B, and C
  domain transcription factors (abc mutant). Predict the identity of
  organs in each floral whorl. Then predict what would happen if, in the
  same mutant, you ectopically expressed B-class genes in whorls 1 and 2
  during flower development. Reference
  \cref{eq:unit_VIII_floral_quartet} in your answer.
\item
  Explain the mechanism of gametophytic self-incompatibility in
  Solanaceae. A researcher crosses two plants with S-genotypes
  \(S_1S_2\) and \(S_1S_3\). What fraction of pollen will be accepted?
  Which S-\hyperref[gl:allele]{\textbf{allele}} combinations appear in
  the viable offspring? Compare with the same scheme under sporophytic
  SI in \emph{Brassica}.
\item
  Compare primary and secondary seed dormancy. For a temperate tree
  species requiring both stratification and light for germination, trace
  the environmental cues from autumn seed fall through spring
  germination, linking each cue to its molecular mechanism (DOG1, ABA/GA
  balance, phytochrome). Identify the dormancy class (PD, PY, MD, MPD,
  combinational).
\item
  The goal of introducing synthetic apomixis into hybrid rice is to
  allow subsistence farmers to save F1 hybrid seed. (a) What genetic
  modifications are needed to create apomictic seed (cite Wang \emph{et
  al.} 2022)? (b) What risks might apomictic crops pose to wild
  relatives via gene flow? (c) Compare the genetic diversity
  implications of apomixis vs vegetative propagation.
\item
  Explain why double fertilisation \citep{nawaschin1898} is considered a
  key evolutionary innovation. What advantage does the triploid
  endosperm provide over the gymnosperm approach where the female
  gametophyte tissue serves as the nutritive tissue? Discuss the
  parental conflict implications via the PEG/MEG mechanism. Why is the
  canonical 2m:1p genome dosage common, and what kinds of exceptions
  would challenge an over-simple rule?
\item
  A fruit biologist examines a mystery fruit and finds: fleshy mesocarp,
  hard endocarp containing a single seed, and thin exocarp. Classify
  this fruit type. Name three plants that produce this type of fruit and
  describe the most likely dispersal mechanism. Is this likely a
  climacteric or non-climacteric fruit?
\item
  Describe the WUS-CLV3 feedback loop. Predict the phenotype of: (a) a
  loss-of-function \emph{clv3} mutant, (b) a gain-of-function \emph{WUS}
  overexpression line, and (c) a double mutant lacking both WUS and
  CLV3.
\item
  Run \breaktt{plant\_biomass\_growth} from 1 g to 40 g capacity over 60
  days. How does the curve differ from unrestricted exponential growth?
\item
  Why might \textbf{endosperm ploidy} (3n) stabilise parent-offspring
  conflict compared with purely maternal provisioning? Use the FIS-PRC2
  mechanism in your answer.
\item
  A breeder wants to create double-flowered carnations (extra petals).
  Which class of MADS-box gene should be partially inactivated and why?
  Cite the relevant Coen and Meyerowitz framework \citep{coen1991} and
  the molecular identity of the gene (AG).
\item
  Explain the commercial pre-harvest treatment with 1-MCP for apples in
  long-distance export. Which step of the ethylene pathway shown in
  \cref{eq:unit_VIII_ethylene_pathway} does 1-MCP block, and how does
  this preserve fruit firmness during shipping? Distinguish System 1 and
  System 2 ethylene biosynthesis.
\item
  A plant exhibits adventive embryony (sporophytic apomixis) in some
  seeds and zygotic embryos in others. From a single cross, predict the
  genotypic distribution of offspring and the agricultural value of this
  dual-mode reproduction.
\end{enumerate}

\subsection{Summary}\label{summary-28}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{Alternation of generations:} Sporophyte (2n) produces spores
  by meiosis; gametophyte (n) produces gametes by mitosis. Evolutionary
  trend: sporophyte dominant, gametophyte reduced.
\item
  \textbf{Plant group diversity:} Bryophytes (gametophyte dominant,
  water-dependent fertilisation) through gymnosperms (pollen, seeds,
  wind pollination) to angiosperms (flowers, double fertilisation,
  fruits, animal pollination).
\item
  \textbf{Floral ABCDE model \citep{coen1991}:} A+E = sepal; A+B+E =
  petal; B+C+E = stamen; C+E = carpel; D+E = ovule. MADS-box TFs (AP1,
  AP3-PI heterodimer, AG, SEP1-4) form floral quartets binding two CArG
  boxes simultaneously.
\item
  \textbf{Gametophytes:} Male = 3-cell pollen grain (tube cell + 2
  sperm) inside sporopollenin exine; female = 7-cell, 8-nucleate
  Polygonum-type embryo sac (egg + 2 synergids + central cell with 2
  polar nuclei + 3 antipodals). Microsporogenesis: MMC \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} meiosis \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} 4
  microspores \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} asymmetric mitosis I \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} 2-cell pollen; mitosis II yields
  2 sperm. Megasporogenesis: MMC \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} meiosis \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} 1 functional + 3
  degenerating megaspores \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} 3 free nuclear divisions \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} 8 nuclei \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
  cellularisation \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} 7-cell embryo sac.
\item
  \textbf{Double fertilisation \citep{nawaschin1898}:} LURE-LRE-FER
  signalling triggers pollen tube rupture in synergid; sperm 1 + egg =
  2n zygote \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} embryo; sperm 2 + 2 polar nuclei = 3n primary endosperm.
  Pollen tube guidance: tip-focused Ca\(^{2+}\) gradient + LURE
  chemotropism; spermatogenesis during tube elongation in bicellular
  pollen species.
\item
  \textbf{Endosperm (typically 3n; 2m:1p):} Free-nuclear \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} cellular
  development; PEG/MEG imprinting via FIS-PRC2 drives parent-of-origin
  expression and parental-conflict regulation. Dosage is canonically
  2m:1p but varies in some lineages and developmental contexts.
\item
  \textbf{Self-incompatibility:} Sporophytic SI (SRK-SCR-ARC1;
  \emph{Brassica}) acts at stigma surface; gametophytic SI (S-RNase/SLF;
  Solanaceae, Rosaceae) acts in style by collaborative non-self
  recognition.
\item
  \textbf{Polyploidy:} Auto- vs allopolyploids; 70\% of angiosperms have
  paleopolyploid history; major crop genomes (wheat, cotton, strawberry)
  are polyploid.
\item
  \textbf{Fruit types:} Diverse adaptations for dispersal (endozoochory,
  anemochory, explosive dehiscence, epizoochory). Climacteric fruits
  (banana, tomato, apple) ripen via System 2 autocatalytic ethylene
  burst --- controlled commercially with 1-MCP. Parthenocarpy can be
  induced by auxin/GA (seedless grapes, watermelons).
\item
  \textbf{Seed dormancy:} Five classes (PD, PY, MD, MPD, combinational);
  broken by stratification, scarification, light (Pfr), smoke-karrikins
  (KAI2), or temperature fluctuation. Germination: GA degrades DELLA,
  releasing \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\alpha}}{alpha}-amylase transcription; ABA-DOG1-PP2C-SnRK2 axis maintains
  dormancy.
\item
  \textbf{Vegetative reproduction:} Stolons, rhizomes, bulbs, corms,
  tubers, adventitious roots/plantlets, fragmentation, layering,
  grafting. Foundation of clonal crop production (banana, potato,
  garlic, grape).
\item
  \textbf{Apomixis:} Sporophytic (adventive embryony, e.g., citrus
  nucellar) vs gametophytic (apospory in \emph{Hieracium}, diplospory in
  \emph{Taraxacum}; pseudogamous vs autonomous endosperm). Wang \emph{et
  al.} 2022 synthetic apomixis in rice via MiMe + MTL/BBML.
\item
  \textbf{Meristems:} SAM (WUS-CLV3 feedback, PIN1-auxin phyllotaxis at
  golden angle); RAM (QC + initials). Both maintain lifelong growth.
\item
  \textbf{Biotechnology:} Tissue culture exploits totipotency;
  \emph{Agrobacterium} Ti plasmid enables genetic transformation; Bt
  crops, golden rice.
\item
  \textbf{Connections:} See Unit IV for meiosis and life cycle,
  \cref{sec:unit_VIII_plant_structure_and_water} for water and growth,
  and \cref{sec:unit_III_photosynthesis} for photosynthate partitioning.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Learning Objectives}\label{learning-objectives-29}

By the end of this chapter, you should be able to:

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  Describe tropisms and how plants sense and respond to directional
  stimuli, including the molecular pathway for phototropism
  \citep{went1926}.
\item
  Explain the major plant \hyperref[gl:hormone]{\textbf{hormone}}s
  (auxin, gibberellin, cytokinin, ABA, ethylene, brassinosteroids,
  jasmonates, salicylate, strigolactones) and their signalling pathways.
\item
  Describe photomorphogenesis: phytochrome biochemistry (Pr/Pfr
  photoconversion), cryptochrome FAD signalling, and shade avoidance.
\item
  Explain gravitropism in roots and shoots, including amyloplast
  settling and PIN \hyperref[gl:protein]{\textbf{protein}}
  relocalisation.
\item
  Describe \hyperref[gl:photoperiodism]{\textbf{photoperiodism}}, the
  role of \hyperref[gl:phytochrome]{\textbf{phytochrome}}, florigen
  (FT), and the molecular basis of flowering time control via
  vernalisation (FLC silencing).
\item
  Explain the plant circadian clock molecular architecture (morning loop
  CCA1/LHY/TOC1; evening loop PRR5/7/9) and how it gates growth,
  flowering, and \hyperref[gl:photosynthesis]{\textbf{photosynthesis}}.
\item
  Describe drought (ABA pathway), cold (CBF-COR pathway), heat (HSP
  response), salt, flooding, and
  \hyperref[gl:herbivory]{\textbf{herbivory}} (jasmonate) stress
  responses.
\item
  Describe plant immunity (PTI, ETI), the hypersensitive response,
  systemic acquired resistance (SAR), and JA/SA antagonism.
\item
  Evaluate agricultural applications of plant hormone biology: ethylene
  inhibitors, gibberellin dwarfing genes, and auxin herbicides.
\end{enumerate}
