\subsection*{Paper-Based
Investigation}\label{paper-based-investigation-37}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Paper-Based Investigation}

\textbf{Part A --- Biome Classification}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  For each of 10 climate data cards (MAT in °C, MAP in mm), plot the
  location on the Whittaker diagram. Identify the biome for each
  location.
\end{enumerate}

\textbf{Part B --- Species-Area Relationship}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{1}
\tightlist
\item
  Plot log(S) vs log(A) for the 6 habitat fragments on log-log paper.
  Fit a line; calculate the slope (z exponent) and the y-intercept (log
  c).
\item
  Using \(S = cA^z\), predict species richness in a fragment one-tenth
  the area of the largest.
\item
  If a deforestation event reduces a forest from 10,000 ha to 100 ha,
  predict the percentage of species lost using the same equation.
\end{enumerate}

\textbf{Part C --- MVP Analysis}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{4}
\tightlist
\item
  Given MVP data for the provided species: 50/500 rule (N\_e
  \textgreater{} 50 for short-term genetic viability; N\_e
  \textgreater{} 500 for long-term). Current population: 35 individuals.
  Is the population below the short-term MVP? Design a 10-year recovery
  plan with specific targets.
\end{enumerate}

\textbf{Part D --- IUCN Classification}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{5}
\tightlist
\item
  Apply IUCN criteria to the species profile (population decline 80\% in
  10 years; \textless{} 250 mature individuals; geographic range
  \textless{} 100 km\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{2}}{2}). Determine IUCN status.
\item
  Use the reserve-design matrix to compare a single large reserve,
  several small reserves, and a connected-corridor plan. Score each
  option for extinction risk, climate refugia, ecosystem services, and
  governance tradeoffs.
\end{enumerate}

\textbf{Part E --- Coral and Food-System Decision Cards}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{7}
\tightlist
\item
  Classify coral scenarios by degree-heating-week exposure, recovery
  interval, and local stressors. Decide whether the evidence supports
  likely recovery, repeated bleaching risk, or high mortality risk.
\item
  Use the symbiont-response cards to distinguish symbiont shuffling,
  assisted gene flow, selective breeding, and microbiome conditioning.
  State one benefit, one tradeoff, and one missing validation step for
  each.
\item
  Use the IPBES/food-security card to compare two conservation plans:
  one maximizing protected area alone and one combining habitat
  protection with agroecological transition, pollinator corridors, and
  food-waste reduction. Score biodiversity, nutrition, equity, and
  feasibility separately.
\end{enumerate}

\subsection*{Evidence and Reproducibility
Checklist}\label{evidence-and-reproducibility-checklist-37}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Evidence and Reproducibility
Checklist}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{Primary evidence goal:} Compare biome patterns and
  conservation tradeoffs.
\item
  \textbf{Data skill to practice:} Use maps, trend data, and threat
  categories to justify conservation priorities.
\item
  \textbf{BioSkills emphasis:} Modeling and simulation, Science and
  society, Communication and collaboration.
\item
  \textbf{Control logic:} identify at least one positive control, one
  negative control, or one baseline comparison before interpreting
  results.
\item
  \textbf{Measurement discipline:} record units, uncertainty, sample
  size, and any discarded observation with a reason.
\item
  \textbf{Mechanistic link:} connect one result directly to the parent
  chapter's big idea before writing the conclusion.
\item
  \textbf{Reproducibility check:} state one procedural detail that
  another group would need in order to reproduce the result.
\end{itemize}

Focus note: for this conservation lab, separate the ecological signal in
the printed dataset (a biodiversity index, range map, or protected-area
comparison) from the value judgement and the feasibility constraint, and
name explicitly which counterfactual or unprotected reference the
decision is being measured against. Keep required work paper-based; any
material-handling or equipment version belongs only in an optional
extension.

\subsection*{Analysis Questions}\label{analysis-questions-37}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Analysis Questions}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  Two locations had the same MAT but very different biomes because of
  different MAP values. What does this demonstrate about the relative
  importance of temperature vs precipitation in biome determination?
  Name an example pair from the Whittaker diagram where this contrast is
  striking.
\item
  Your log-log plot of the species-area relationship should be linear.
  What does the slope (z) represent ecologically? Why do oceanic islands
  have higher z values (about 0.35) than mainland habitat
  patches (about 0.12)?
\item
  Predicted species loss from deforestation assumes equilibrium. Explain
  the concept of ``extinction debt'' --- why the full extinction toll of
  habitat reduction is primarily realised decades after the habitat
  loss, and what this implies for urgency in conservation action.
\item
  The 50/500 rule gives threshold population sizes for genetic
  viability. Explain: (a) why populations below N\_e = 50 suffer
  inbreeding depression; (b) why populations below N\_e = 500 lose the
  variation needed to adapt to future environmental change. What is the
  difference between census population size (N\_c) and effective
  population size (N\_e)?
\item
  Design a conservation reserve for a large mammal (e.g., tiger, Amur
  leopard) with a home range of 200 km\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{2}}{2} that requires a minimum viable
  population of 100 individuals. Calculate the minimum reserve area,
  explain whether a single large reserve (SLOSS debate: Single Large or
  Several Small) is preferable in this case, and identify two human
  activities outside the reserve boundary that would most threaten
  population persistence.
\item
  A reef has high DHW exposure but a recovery window long enough for
  partial symbiont reshuffling, while a nearby watershed continues to
  deliver nutrient pollution. Which intervention should be treated as
  climate adaptation, which as local-stressor reduction, and why would
  assisted evolution alone be insufficient?
\item
  A food-security policy increases short-term yield by removing
  hedgerows and reducing crop diversity. Use the IPBES/food-system
  tradeoff card to evaluate why yield, pollination, soil stability,
  nutrition, and equity must be scored separately rather than collapsed
  into one ``more food'' metric.
\end{enumerate}

\subsection*{Safety and Ethics Notes}\label{safety-and-ethics-notes-37}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Safety and Ethics Notes}

No hazardous materials. Conservation discussions involving indigenous
land rights and protected area design should be approached with cultural
sensitivity and recognition of land sovereignty principles. IUCN
assessments require reliable species data --- discuss uncertainty and
the precautionary principle.

\subsection*{Debrief and Reflection}\label{debrief-and-reflection-34}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Debrief and Reflection}

After you finish the practical work, spend 5--10 minutes in your small
group comparing results and discussing the following prompts. Each
member should contribute at least one observation before moving to the
next prompt:

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{What did your measurements show} --- compare the group's
  results to the textbook's predictions. Where they diverge, suggest at
  least one mechanistic explanation before concluding ``experimental
  error.''
\item
  \textbf{What would change the outcome} --- propose one modification to
  the procedure that would sharpen the measurement or extend the result
  to a new biological context, and predict what you would observe.
\item
  \textbf{One-sentence headline} --- each student composes a single
  sentence summarising the lab's take-home message, suitable for a
  tweet. Compare sentences across groups; good headlines are short,
  quantitative, and mechanistic.
\item
  \textbf{Connection back to the textbook} --- identify one section of
  \cref{sec:unit_X_biomes_and_conservation} that your data either
  confirmed or complicated. Cite the specific passage.
\end{enumerate}

\subsection*{Recall Questions (1 mark
each)}\label{recall-questions-1-mark-each}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Recall Questions (1 mark each)}

\subsection*{Instructor Use and Coverage
Notes}\label{instructor-use-and-coverage-notes}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Instructor Use and Coverage Notes}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{Coverage target:} Given a biological scenario, identify the
  system boundary, feedback loop, and missing measurement.
\item
  \textbf{Model/data emphasis:} Box-and-arrow causal models with
  explicit inputs, outputs, and feedback signs.
\item
  \textbf{Assessment alignment:} Questions and Methods, Representing and
  Describing Data, Argumentation.
\item
  \textbf{Misconception probe:} A system is not just a list of parts;
  the interactions are part of the explanation.
\item
  \textbf{Transfer product:} Apply the same feedback map to a cell,
  organism, and ecosystem, then name what changes at each scale.
\item
  \textbf{Grading focus:} award full credit for mechanism, evidence,
  boundary conditions, and units when a calculation is required.
\item
  \textbf{Suggested use:} draw one recall item, one application item,
  and one synthesis item when building a short quiz from this bank.
\end{itemize}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  Define `systems science' in your own words and provide a biological
  example.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{1}
\tightlist

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{3}
\tightlist

  Describe one biological example of negative feedback and one of

\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{4}

\subsection*{Synthesis Questions (4 marks
each)}\label{synthesis-questions-4-marks-each}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Synthesis Questions (4 marks each)}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{10}
\tightlist
\item
  Compare and contrast the immune system and an evolving tumour as
  complex adaptive systems. In each case, identify (a) the agents, (b)
  the selection pressures, (c) an emergent property, and (d) a critical
  vulnerability.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{11}
\tightlist
\item
  A patient with chronic anxiety has persistent overactivation of the
  sympathetic nervous system even in the absence of objective threat.
  Using predictive coding and active inference, construct a mechanistic
  account of how prior beliefs about threat might drive this pattern.
  How might therapeutic interventions (CBT, interoceptive exposure)
  alter the generative model?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{12}
\tightlist
\item
  Describe how ecosystem collapse (e.g., coral bleaching, fishery
  collapse) can be framed as a phase transition in a complex adaptive
  system. What warning signals might precede the transition? Why is
  recovery often much harder than the original decline?
\end{enumerate}

\subsection*{Data and Model Interpretation Questions (3 marks
each)}\label{data-and-model-interpretation-questions-3-marks-each}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Data and Model Interpretation
Questions (3 marks each)}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{13}
\tightlist
\item
  A homeostatic variable is measured at 98, 101, 105, 112, and 130 units
  after a perturbation. Identify whether the response appears damped,
  amplified, or unstable, and name one missing measurement needed before
  drawing a systems-level conclusion.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{14}
\tightlist
\item
  Draw a signed feedback diagram for blood glucose regulation that
  includes glucose, insulin, glucagon, liver glycogen breakdown, and
  muscle glucose uptake. Which links are negative feedback links?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{15}
\tightlist
\item
  In a predator-prey system, prey abundance rises first, predator
  abundance rises after a delay, and prey then falls. Explain why the
  delay matters for oscillation rather than immediate stabilization.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{16}
\tightlist
\item
  A pathway has two parallel routes from receptor activation to
  transcription. Blocking one route reduces output by 20\%. What systems
  property explains this robustness, and what experiment would test it?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{17}
\tightlist
\item
  A network diagram has many nodes with two links and three nodes with
  hundreds of links. What kind of network does this suggest, and why is
  it robust to random node loss but vulnerable to targeted hub loss?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{18}
\tightlist
\item
  A cell-fate model has two stable attractors, A and B. A weak transient
  signal moves the cell partway toward B, but it returns to A; a
  stronger signal switches it to B permanently. Explain this in terms of
  basins of attraction.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{19}
\tightlist
\item
  A researcher reports that deleting one enzyme in a pathway has no
  phenotype, so the enzyme is unimportant. Critique this conclusion
  using compensation and context dependence.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{20}
\tightlist
\item
  A negative feedback loop has a sensor that saturates at high input
  values. Predict what happens when the input exceeds the sensor's
  dynamic range.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{21}
\tightlist
\item
  Explain how modularity can make a system both more evolvable and more
  fragile.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{22}
\tightlist
\item
  Compare a thermostat, blood calcium regulation, and quorum sensing.
  Which parts of the analogy are useful, and where does the analogy
  break down?
\end{enumerate}

each)}\label{evaluation-and-design-questions-4-marks-each}

marks each)}

\setcounter{enumi}{13}
\tightlist
\item
  In an agent-based simulation, changing one local rule from ``align
  with three neighbours'' to ``align with six neighbours'' causes global
  order to appear faster. Explain why this is an emergent result rather
  than a command from a central controller.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{14}
\tightlist
\item
  A microbial biofilm becomes resistant to an antibiotic even though
  many isolated cells from the same biofilm remain sensitive. Give two
  complex-adaptive explanations.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{15}
\tightlist
\item
  A fitness landscape has one tall narrow peak and one lower broad peak.
  Which peak is easier for a population to maintain under mutation and
  environmental noise, and why?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{16}
\tightlist
\item
  Explain how a phase transition differs from a gradual linear change.
  Use one biological example.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{17}
\tightlist
\item
  A population repeatedly evolves the same resistance mutation in
  separate cultures. Does this prove evolution is deterministic? Give a
  careful answer.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{18}
\tightlist
\item
  Compare self-organization in embryonic patterning and in ant foraging.
  What is shared, and what differs?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{19}
\tightlist
\item
  A complex system model reproduces one observed pattern but fails under
  a new perturbation. What does this tell you about model validation?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{20}
\tightlist
\item
  Explain why heterogeneity among agents can make a population more
  resilient.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{21}
\tightlist
\item
  A cancer therapy kills 99\% of tumour cells but leaves a small
  resistant subpopulation. Explain why this can select for relapse.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{22}
\tightlist
\item
  Distinguish adaptation by natural selection from adaptation by
  learning within an organism. Why can both be described as adaptive
  processes?
\end{enumerate}

marks each)}

Principle}\label{questions-ch-0.3-active-inference-and-the-free-energy-principle}
\addcontentsline{toc}{section}{Questions --- Ch 0.3: Active Inference
and the Free Energy Principle}

the textbook --- review that chapter before attempting the exercises
below.}

\subsection*{Recall Questions (1 mark
each)}\label{recall-questions-1-mark-each-2}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Recall Questions (1 mark each)}

\subsection*{Instructor Use and Coverage
Notes}\label{instructor-use-and-coverage-notes-2}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Instructor Use and Coverage Notes}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{Coverage target:} Calculate a posterior belief and explain
  what action would reduce uncertainty or restore a set point.
\item
  \textbf{Model/data emphasis:} Bayesian belief updating and
  expected-free-energy-style policy comparison.
\item
  \textbf{Assessment alignment:} Questions and Methods, Representing and
  Describing Data, Argumentation.
\item
  \textbf{Misconception probe:} Active inference is not passive
  prediction; action changes the sensory data that arrive next.
\item
  \textbf{Transfer product:} Map prediction-error reasoning onto
  chemotaxis, thermoregulation, and attention.
\item
  \textbf{Grading focus:} award full credit for mechanism, evidence,
  boundary conditions, and units when a calculation is required.
\item
  \textbf{Suggested use:} draw one recall item, one application item,
  and one synthesis item when building a short quiz from this bank.
\end{itemize}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  Define `active inference' in your own words and provide a biological
  example.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{1}
\tightlist
\item
  What distinguishes a complex adaptive system from a simple system?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{2}
\tightlist
\item
  What is the free energy principle? What does free energy measure?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{3}
\tightlist
\item
  Describe one biological example of negative feedback and one of
  positive feedback.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{4}
\tightlist
\item
  What is the difference between homeostasis and allostasis?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{center}\rule{0.5\linewidth}{0.5pt}\end{center}

each)}\label{application-questions-2-marks-each-2}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{5}
\tightlist
\item
  A drug blocks a key kinase in a signalling cascade, but the tumour
  eventually regrows. Explain this outcome using the concept of feedback
  compensation.

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{6}
\tightlist

  Explain why the lac operon switch is described as bistable. What
  advantage does bistability provide over a graded (linear) response?

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{7}
\tightlist

  How does the concept of attractors in phase space relate to cell fate?

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{8}
\tightlist

  Apply the active inference framework to explain how a fever might be
  adaptive rather than merely a pathological response.

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{9}

  In evolutionary terms, what is niche construction, and how does it

\subsection*{Synthesis Questions (4 marks
each)}\label{synthesis-questions-4-marks-each-2}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Synthesis Questions (4 marks each)}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{10}
\tightlist
\item
  Compare and contrast the immune system and an evolving tumour as
  complex adaptive systems. In each case, identify (a) the agents, (b)
  the selection pressures, (c) an emergent property, and (d) a critical
  vulnerability.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{11}
\tightlist
\item
  A patient with chronic anxiety has persistent overactivation of the
  sympathetic nervous system even in the absence of objective threat.
  Using predictive coding and active inference, construct a mechanistic
  account of how prior beliefs about threat might drive this pattern.
  How might therapeutic interventions (CBT, interoceptive exposure)
  alter the generative model?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{12}
\tightlist
\item
  Describe how ecosystem collapse (e.g., coral bleaching, fishery
  collapse) can be framed as a phase transition in a complex adaptive
  system. What warning signals might precede the transition? Why is
  recovery often much harder than the original decline?
\end{enumerate}

each)}\label{data-and-model-interpretation-questions-3-marks-each-2}

Questions (3 marks each)}

  A prior predicts body temperature should be 37.0 degrees C, but

\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{15}

  A patient with panic disorder interprets benign heart-rate increases

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}

\tightlist

  Compare homeostasis and allostasis from an active-inference

\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}

\tightlist

  A chemotactic bacterium tumbles more often when attractant

\begin{enumerate}

  Explain why active inference is not the same as reinforcement

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{21}

  Use active inference to explain why inflammation can be both

\begin{enumerate}

\section*{Questions --- Ch 1: Atoms, Molecules, and Chemical
Bonds}\label{questions-ch-1-atoms-molecules-and-chemical-bonds}
\addcontentsline{toc}{section}{Questions --- Ch 1: Atoms, Molecules, and
Chemical Bonds}

\subsection*{Instructor Use and Coverage
Notes}\label{instructor-use-and-coverage-notes-3}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Instructor Use and Coverage Notes}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{Coverage target:} Predict bond polarity, formal charge, or
  isotope behaviour and connect it to a biological consequence.
\item
  \textbf{Model/data emphasis:} Formal charge and
  electronegativity-difference reasoning.
\item
  \textbf{Assessment alignment:} Concept Explanation, Statistical Tests
  and Data Analysis, Argumentation.
\item
  \textbf{Misconception probe:} Weak interactions are not unimportant;
  many weak interactions together dominate structure and specificity.
\item
  \textbf{Transfer product:} Use atomic reasoning to explain a medical
  tracer, enzyme cofactor, or membrane-solubility problem.
\item
  \textbf{Grading focus:} award full credit for mechanism, evidence,
  boundary conditions, and units when a calculation is required.
\item
  \textbf{Suggested use:} draw one recall item, one application item,
  and one synthesis item when building a short quiz from this bank.
\end{itemize}

\subsection*{Questions 1--10: Recall and
Comprehension}\label{questions-110-recall-and-comprehension}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Questions 1--10: Recall and
Comprehension}

\emph{This activity accompanies \cref{sec:unit_I_atoms_molecules} of the
textbook --- review that chapter before attempting the exercises below.}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  Define an atom and identify its three subatomic particles. Which
  determines the element's identity?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{1}
\tightlist
\item
  What is the atomic number of carbon? How many valence electrons does
  carbon have?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{2}
\tightlist
\item
  Distinguish between covalent and ionic bonds. Give one biological
  example of each.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{3}
\tightlist
\item
  Define electronegativity. Which element has the highest
  electronegativity?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{4}
\tightlist
\item
  What makes a covalent bond polar? What partial charges (\texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\delta}}{delta}+ and \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\delta}}{delta}\texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{-}}{-})
  arise in an O--H bond?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{5}
\tightlist
\item
  Define a hydrogen bond. Which atoms typically act as hydrogen bond
  donors and acceptors?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{6}
\tightlist
\item
  What is a van der Waals interaction? In which large molecules are van
  der Waals forces collectively significant?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{7}
\tightlist
\item
  List four properties of water that arise directly from hydrogen
  bonding.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{8}
\tightlist
\item
  What is pH? What hydrogen ion concentration corresponds to pH 7 and pH
  4?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{9}
\tightlist
\item
  Define an acid and a base using the Brønsted-Lowry definition. Give
  one biological example of each.
\end{enumerate}

\subsection*{Questions 11--20: Application and
Analysis}\label{questions-1120-application-and-analysis}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Questions 11--20: Application and
Analysis}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{10}
\tightlist
\item
  Carbon forms four covalent bonds. Explain how this tetravalency allows
  carbon to form diverse structures including chains, branches, and
  rings. Why is carbon the basis of biological molecules rather than
  silicon?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{11}
\tightlist
\item
  The electronegativity difference for O--H is 1.4, for N--H is 0.9, and
  for C--H is 0.4. Rank these bonds from most to least polar and predict
  which can form hydrogen bonds.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{12}
\tightlist
\item
  A buffer solution contains equal concentrations of carbonic acid
  (H\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{2}}{2}CO\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{3}}{3}) and bicarbonate (HCO\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{3}}{3}\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{-}}{-}). At what pH does the buffer have
  maximum capacity? Express this using the Henderson-Hasselbalch
  equation (pKa of carbonic acid = 6.1).
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{13}
\tightlist
\item
  Explain why non-polar molecules such as cholesterol are insoluble in
  water but soluble in lipids. What thermodynamic principle governs this
  behaviour (hint: entropy of hydrophobic interactions)?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{14}
\tightlist
\item
  A molecule has the formula C\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{1}}{1}\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{8}}{8}H\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{3}}{3}\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{6}}{6}O\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{2}}{2}. Predict whether it is saturated
  or unsaturated based on the degree-of-unsaturation (DoU) formula.
  Identify it as a likely carbohydrate, lipid, or protein monomer.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{15}
\tightlist
\item
  Compare the properties of strong acids (e.g., HCl) vs weak acids
  (e.g., acetic acid, pKa = 4.76) at the same initial concentration. At
  pH 5, what fraction of acetic acid molecules are dissociated? (Use
  Henderson-Hasselbalch.)
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{16}
\tightlist
\item
  A cell's cytoplasmic pH drops from 7.4 to 6.9 during intense exercise.
  By what factor does {[}H\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{+}}{+}{]} increase? What buffers in the cytoplasm
  resist this pH change?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{17}
\tightlist
\item
  Explain why CO\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{2}}{2} dissolved in blood lowers pH. Write the relevant
  chemical equations, naming each species formed.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{18}
\tightlist
\item
  The peptide bond in proteins involves C--N with partial double-bond
  character due to resonance. Explain how this resonance prevents
  rotation around the peptide bond and what structural constraint this
  places on protein backbone geometry.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{19}
\tightlist
\item
  Magnesium (Mg\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{2}}{2}\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{+}}{+}) is a common enzyme cofactor. Using your understanding
  of atomic structure, explain why Mg\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{2}}{2}\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{+}}{+} can stabilise negatively charged
  phosphate groups in ATP. What orbital property of Mg\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{2}}{2}\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{+}}{+} makes it a
  Lewis acid?
\end{enumerate}

\subsection*{Questions 21--30: Synthesis and
Evaluation}\label{questions-2130-synthesis-and-evaluation}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Questions 21--30: Synthesis and
Evaluation}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{20}
\tightlist
\item
  Evaluate the statement: ``Life could have evolved using silicon
  instead of carbon as its molecular backbone.'' Using comparative
  chemistry, identify at least two key chemical differences between the
  bonding properties of C and Si that make carbon uniquely suited for
  biological macromolecules.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{21}
\tightlist
\item
  Design an experiment to test whether the hydrophobic effect is
  entropy-driven. Describe what measurements you would take, what
  temperature you would vary, and what thermodynamic parameters you
  would calculate. Predict the outcome.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{22}
\tightlist
\item
  A drug molecule must cross the blood-brain barrier (which is composed
  of lipid bilayer membranes). Using the structure-activity relationship
  principle, explain what molecular properties (MW, logP, H-bond
  donors/acceptors) favour CNS penetration. How would you modify a
  highly polar drug to improve CNS penetration?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{23}
\tightlist
\item
  Carbonic anhydrase catalyses CO\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{2}}{2} + H\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{2}}{2}O \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\rightleftharpoons}}{<=>} H\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{2}}{2}CO\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{3}}{3} with a rate constant
  about 10\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{6}}{6}\texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\times}}{x} faster than the uncatalysed reaction. The active
  site uses a Zn\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{2}}{2}\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{+}}{+} ion to polarise the O--H bond of a water molecule.
  Explain the mechanistic logic: why does metal coordination of water
  make it a better nucleophile in this context?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{24}
\tightlist
\item
  Compare the evolutionary origins of the genetic code (DNA/RNA using N-
  and O-containing bases) with a hypothetical alternative code using
  entirely non-polar building blocks. What biochemical properties would
  be lost or gained? Evaluate why polarity and hydrogen bonding in
  nucleobases are essential for genetic fidelity.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{25}
\tightlist
\item
  A newly discovered antibiotic (X) functions by chelating Mg\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{2}}{2}\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{+}}{+} ions in
  bacterial ribosomes. Predict: (a) which step of protein synthesis
  would be disrupted; (b) whether X would be active vs gram-positive or
  gram-negative bacteria; (c) possible mechanisms of resistance the
  bacterium might evolve.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{26}
\tightlist
\item
  The Henderson-Hasselbalch equation assumes that pKa is constant.
  However, the pKa of His residues in proteins is strongly
  context-dependent (ranging from 4.0 to 8.0). Explain how protein
  microenvironment (electrostatics, hydrophobicity, hydrogen bonding)
  shifts the pKa of an ionisable side chain, and why this is
  functionally important for enzyme catalysis.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{27}
\tightlist
\item
  Bohr effect: CO\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{2}}{2} and H\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{+}}{+} reduce haemoglobin's O\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{2}}{2} affinity by
  stabilising the T-state (deoxy form). Using atomic-level reasoning:
  (a) which specific residues of haemoglobin are protonated at low pH;
  (b) how does protonation alter quaternary structure; (c) why is this
  physiologically beneficial in exercising tissues?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{28}
\tightlist
\item
  A patient presents with severe metabolic acidosis (blood pH 7.1, HCO\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{3}}{3}\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{-}}{-}
  = 12 mEq/L, pCO\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{2}}{2} = 30 mmHg). Using Henderson-Hasselbalch (pH = 6.1 +
  log{[}HCO\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{3}}{3}\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{-}}{-}{]}/{[}0.03 \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\times}}{x} pCO\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{2}}{2}{]}), verify the expected pH vs measured.
  Is there respiratory compensation? What primary disorder is this
  (metabolic or respiratory) and how would you distinguish a primary
  from a compensatory change?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{29}
\tightlist
\item
  Propose a molecular mechanism by which a histone deacetylase (HDAC)
  inhibitor (e.g., vorinostat) could be used to treat cancer. Trace from
  HDAC inhibition \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} altered histone acetylation state \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} chromatin
  opening \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} transcription of tumour suppressor genes \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} reduced tumour
  cell survival. Identify the specific bond type removed/restored at
  each step.
\end{enumerate}

\section*{Questions --- Ch 2: Water --- The Molecule of
Life}\label{questions-ch-2-water-the-molecule-of-life}
\addcontentsline{toc}{section}{Questions --- Ch 2: Water --- The
Molecule of Life}

\label{sec:q_unit_I_water_and_life}

\subsection*{Instructor Use and Coverage
Notes}\label{instructor-use-and-coverage-notes-4}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Instructor Use and Coverage Notes}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{Coverage target:} Calculate a pH or buffer ratio and interpret
  what it means for a biological system.
\item
  \textbf{Model/data emphasis:} Henderson-Hasselbalch and pH-scale
  calculations.
\item
  \textbf{Assessment alignment:} Concept Explanation, Statistical Tests
  and Data Analysis, Argumentation.
\item
  \textbf{Misconception probe:} Water is not an inert background; it is
  an active participant in structure and reaction chemistry.
\item
  \textbf{Transfer product:} Transfer water-property reasoning to blood
  buffering, plant transport, or protein folding.
\item
  \textbf{Grading focus:} award full credit for mechanism, evidence,
  boundary conditions, and units when a calculation is required.
\item
  \textbf{Suggested use:} draw one recall item, one application item,
  and one synthesis item when building a short quiz from this bank.

\subsection*{Questions 1--10: Recall and
Comprehension}\label{questions-110-recall-and-comprehension-1}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Questions 1--10: Recall and
Comprehension}

\emph{This activity accompanies \cref{sec:unit_I_water_and_life} of the
textbook --- review that chapter before attempting the exercises below.}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  Draw the water molecule; label the bond angle (104.5°), partial
  charges, and hydrogen bonds with adjacent molecules.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{1}
\tightlist
\item
  Define specific heat capacity. Why does water have a high specific
  heat compared to most liquids?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{2}
\tightlist
\item
  What is the heat of vaporisation of water (cal/g) and what biological
  process exploits this?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{3}
\tightlist
\item
  Define cohesion and adhesion. Which property allows water to form a
  meniscus in a glass tube?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{4}
\tightlist
\item
  What is osmosis? In which direction does water move --- toward higher
  or lower solute concentration?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{5}
\tightlist
\item
  Define water potential (\texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\Psi}}{Psi}). Write the equation \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\Psi}}{Psi} = \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\Psi}}{Psi}\_s + \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\Psi}}{Psi}\_p and
  define each term.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{6}
\tightlist
\item
  What is tonicity? Distinguish hypertonic, hypotonic, and isotonic
  solutions relative to a red blood cell.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{7}
\tightlist
\item
  Define capillarity. Name two forces responsible for capillary rise in
  a tube.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{8}
\tightlist
\item
  What is the pH of pure water at 25°C? What is the Kw of water at this
  temperature?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{9}
\tightlist
\item
  Describe what happens to a freshwater fish placed in seawater
  (hypertonic solution) in terms of osmosis.
\end{enumerate}

\subsection*{Questions 11--20: Application and
Analysis}\label{questions-1120-application-and-analysis-1}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Questions 11--20: Application and
Analysis}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{10}
\tightlist
\item
  Calculate: if the osmotic potential of a plant cell is \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{-}}{-}0.8 MPa and
  pressure potential is +0.3 MPa, what is the water potential? Will
  water enter or leave the cell if it is placed in a solution with \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\Psi}}{Psi} =
  \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{-}}{-}0.4 MPa?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{11}
\tightlist
\item
  During sweating, 1 litre of sweat evaporated removes approximately 580
  kcal of heat from the body. Calculate: if a marathon runner produces 2
  L/h of sweat, how many watts of heat are removed? (1 watt = 1 J/s)
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{12}
\tightlist
\item
  Sea ice insulates frigid arctic waters and protects aquatic organisms.
  Explain, at the molecular level, why ice is less dense than liquid
  water and why this unusual property has profound ecological
  consequences.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{13}
\tightlist
\item
  An onion cell with osmotic potential \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{-}}{-}0.6 MPa is placed in a 0.3 M
  NaCl solution. The NaCl solution has \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\Psi}}{Psi}\_s = \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{-}}{-}0.75 MPa. Predict the
  direction of water movement and whether the cell will plasmolyse or
  swell.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{14}
\tightlist
\item
  Compare the water requirements of a plant using C\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{4}}{4} photosynthesis
  (e.g., maize) vs C\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{3}}{3} photosynthesis (e.g., wheat) in a hot, dry
  environment. Explain in terms of stomatal conductance and water-use
  efficiency.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{15}
\tightlist
\item
  Describe three specific properties of water that make it essential for
  the cohesion-tension mechanism of xylem transport. What evidence
  refutes the alternative ``root pressure'' hypothesis as the primary
  force driving water to the tops of tall trees?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{16}
\tightlist
\item
  A student proposes using ethanol instead of water as a biological
  solvent. Identify three properties of water (not of ethanol) that
  would be lost, and predict the consequences for enzyme function, ion
  transport, and pH buffering.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{17}
\tightlist
\item
  During hypothermia, core body temperature drops to 32°C. Using
  specific heat capacity principles, calculate the heat (kJ) that must
  be extracted from a 70 kg person (composed of about 60\%
  water) to lower their temperature from 37°C to 32°C (specific heat of
  the body \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\approx}}{~} 3.47 kJ/kg\texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\cdot}}{.}°C).
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{18}
\tightlist
\item
  Explain the role of aquaporins in transmembrane water movement. How
  does the selectivity filter exclude protons (H\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{3}}{3}O\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{+}}{+}) despite water
  molecules sharing similar size? What disease results from aquaporin-2
  deficiency?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{19}
\tightlist
\item
  The mangrove tree lives in salty seawater. Its roots must extract
  fresh water against an extremely negative osmotic potential. Explain
  what root structure adaptations mangroves have developed, and
  calculate the minimum root pressure required if external seawater has
  \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\Psi}}{Psi}\_s = \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{-}}{-}2.5 MPa and leaf water loss creates \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\Psi}}{Psi}\_p = \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{-}}{-}1.0 MPa.
\end{enumerate}

\subsection*{Questions 21--30: Synthesis and
Evaluation}\label{questions-2130-synthesis-and-evaluation-1}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Questions 21--30: Synthesis and
Evaluation}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{20}
\tightlist
\item
  Water is simultaneously the product and reactant of countless
  biochemical reactions (hydrolysis, condensation, and hydration).
  Evaluate whether increasing intracellular water concentration would
  shift equilibrium toward condensation reactions (protein synthesis) or
  hydrolysis reactions. What does Le Chatelier's principle predict?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{21}
\tightlist
\item
  Propose an experiment to test whether the anomalous expansion of water
  upon freezing is due to hydrogen bond structure. What control
  conditions and measurements would you use? What would falsify the
  hydrogen bond hypothesis?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{22}
\tightlist
\item
  The blood-brain barrier restricts water flux into the CNS. Cerebral
  oedema (excess water accumulation in brain tissue) can be fatal. Using
  water potential principles, explain: (a) why hyponatraemia (low blood
  {[}Na\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{+}}{+}{]}) causes cerebral oedema; (b) why mannitol infusion reduces
  oedema; (c) how AQP4 water channels contribute to normal fluid
  homeostasis.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{23}
\tightlist
\item
  Compare the water potential of: (a) pure water; (b) 0.1 M sucrose
  solution; (c) wilted plant cell (\texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{-}}{-}1.2 MPa osmotic, +0.1 MPa pressure);
  (d) turgid plant cell (\texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{-}}{-}1.2 MPa osmotic, +0.9 MPa pressure). Rank them
  from highest to lowest \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\Psi}}{Psi} and predict the direction of water flux
  between each pair.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{24}
\tightlist
\item
  Desiccation-tolerant (resurrection) plants can survive to \textless{}
  5\% water content and revive when rehydrated. Propose two cellular
  mechanisms that allow membranes and proteins to remain functional in
  the nearly anhydrous state. Consider the role of trehalose as a
  vitrifying agent.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{25}
\tightlist
\item
  Reverse osmosis (RO) desalination uses high pressure to push seawater
  through semi-permeable membranes. Calculate: if seawater has an
  osmotic pressure of approximately 27 atm (2.7 MPa), what minimum
  external pressure must the RO system exert to produce fresh water?
  What energy (kJ) is required per litre, given 1 atm \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\approx}}{~} 101.3 kPa and
  volume = 1 L?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{26}
\tightlist
\item
  During ischemia (reduced blood flow), intracellular Na\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{+}}{+} rises due to
  Na/K-ATPase failure. Predict the effect of rising intracellular Na\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{+}}{+}
  on: (a) intracellular osmotic potential; (b) water flux across the
  plasma membrane; (c) cell volume. How does this contribute to
  ischaemic cell death?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{27}
\tightlist
\item
  Antarctic ice fish have no haemoglobin and survive at \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{-}}{-}1.9°C seawater
  by relying on the unusual fluidity of water at low temperatures.
  Explain: (a) how antifreeze proteins (AFPs) prevent ice crystal
  formation at subzero temperatures (using the concepts of ice crystal
  growth inhibition); (b) how AFP ice binding differs from osmotic
  freezing protection (as in glycerol).
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{28}
\tightlist
\item
  Water's high surface tension (72 mN/m at 20°C) is biologically
  critical. Describe two specific biological examples of surface tension
  exploitation (one arthropod, one mammalian respiratory) and explain
  the molecular basis of surface tension in each, and what would happen
  if surface tension were reduced by half in each case.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{29}
\tightlist
\item
  Critique the role of water activity (a\_w) vs water potential in
  determining microbial growth. Explain why halophilic bacteria can grow
  at a\_w = 0.75 (equivalent to about 5 M NaCl), while most
  bacteria cannot survive below a\_w = 0.95. How does reduced water
  activity inhibit cellular processes even when cells are fully
  hydrated? What field of food science exploits this principle and how?
\end{enumerate}

Comprehension}\label{questions-110-recall-and-comprehension-2}

\subsection*{Questions 11--20: Application and
Analysis}\label{questions-1120-application-and-analysis-2}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Questions 11--20: Application and
Analysis}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{10}
\tightlist
\item
  Cellulose and starch are both glucose polymers, yet starch is
  digestible by humans and cellulose is not. Explain this difference in
  terms of glycosidic bond type (\texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\alpha}}{alpha}-1,4 vs \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\beta}}{beta}-1,4), three-dimensional
  structure, and the specific enzyme (cellulase) that humans lack.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{11}
\tightlist
\item
  A protein has Tm (melting temperature) of 55°C in the presence of 8 M
  urea and 70°C in the absence of denaturant. Identify which types of
  bonds are disrupted by urea (that are absent from primary structure),
  and predict whether a disulphide-bonded protein would be denatured by
  urea alone.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{12}
\tightlist
\item
  Collagen is a fibrous protein with a repeating Gly-X-Y motif (X =
  often Pro; Y = often Hyp). Explain: (a) why Gly must occur every third
  residue; (b) what modification produces hydroxyproline (Hyp) and which
  vitamin is required; (c) what disease results from Hyp deficiency.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{13}
\tightlist
\item
  Phospholipids form bilayers in water. Explain: (a) the thermodynamic
  basis for bilayer formation (hydrophobic effect); (b) why cholesterol
  increases membrane rigidity at high temperatures but increases
  fluidity at low temperatures; (c) how membrane asymmetry (different
  inner vs outer leaflet composition) is maintained.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{14}
\tightlist
\item
  Compare the structures of DNA and RNA --- list at least four
  differences (sugar, bases, strand number, stability). Explain why RNA
  is less stable than DNA chemically (relate to the 2'-hydroxyl group).
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{15}
\tightlist
\item
  Calculate the number of possible distinct dipeptides from 20 standard
  amino acids. Then calculate the number of different 100-residue
  proteins possible. What does this astronomical number imply for
  protein sequence space and directed evolution?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{16}
\tightlist
\item
  Haemoglobin (quaternary structure, four subunits) loses cooperative O\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{2}}{2}
  binding when disaggregated into monomers. Explain how quaternary
  structure enables cooperativity (Hill coefficient n \textgreater{} 1),
  and why this is physiologically advantageous.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{17}
\tightlist
\item
  A glycoprotein has oligosaccharide chains attached to Asn residues
  (N-linked glycosylation). Describe: (a) where in the cell
  N-glycosylation occurs; (b) what enzyme adds the glycan; (c) three
  functions of glycosylation on cell-surface proteins.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{18}
\tightlist
\item
  Lipoproteins (LDL, HDL) are macromolecular complexes of lipid and
  protein. Explain how their amphipathic structure allows transport of
  hydrophobic lipids in the aqueous bloodstream. Why does elevated LDL
  cholesterol increase atherosclerosis risk while elevated HDL is
  protective?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{19}
\tightlist
\item
  A 10-residue peptide contains one disulphide bond between Cys
  residues. How many possible disulphide bond arrangements are there?
  Under what cellular conditions do disulphide bonds form (redox
  potential), and why are they rare in intracellular proteins?
\end{enumerate}

\subsection*{Questions 21--30: Synthesis and
Evaluation}\label{questions-2130-synthesis-and-evaluation-2}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Questions 21--30: Synthesis and
Evaluation}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{20}
\tightlist
\item
  Prions are infectious proteins (misfolded PrP\^{}Sc) that propagate by
  templating the misfolding of normal PrP\^{}C. Evaluate the hypothesis
  that protein conformation can carry infectivity without nucleic acid:
  what evidence supports it, and what challenges remain for explaining
  how a protein can act as an infectious agent?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{21}
\tightlist
\item
  Intrinsically disordered proteins (IDPs) lack stable tertiary
  structure under physiological conditions but are biologically
  functional. Evaluate the traditional sequence-structure-function
  paradigm in light of IDPs. What advantages might disorder confer for
  signalling and regulatory proteins?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{22}
\tightlist
\item
  Silk fibroin is a \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\beta}}{beta}-sheet-rich protein with extraordinary material
  strength (tensile strength 0.5 GPa). Explain, at the inter-molecular
  level, why \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\beta}}{beta}-sheet stacking produces this strength. Compare to
  collagen's triple helix and synthetic Kevlar (also a \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\beta}}{beta}-sheet polymer).
  Design a biotechnology experiment to engineer silk with improved
  elasticity by incorporating glycine-rich loops.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{23}
\tightlist
\item
  Deep-sea bacteria living at 110°C require heat-stable enzymes
  (thermozymes). Propose three molecular-level strategies these
  organisms use to maintain enzyme structure at extreme temperatures
  (consider ion pairs, proline residues, hydrophobic packing, and
  disulphide bonds). How might you engineer a mesophilic enzyme for
  thermostability using directed evolution?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{24}
\tightlist
\item
  Glycolipids in the outer leaflet of the plasma membrane act as
  cell-surface recognition molecules (blood type antigens, pathogen
  receptors). Evaluate the claim that carbohydrate diversity makes
  carbohydrates better suited than proteins for cell-surface diversity.
  Consider information content per unit mass (number of possible
  trisaccharides vs tripeptides from their respective monomer sets).
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{25}
\tightlist
\item
  Amyloid plaques (\texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\beta}}{beta}-sheet-rich aggregates of A\texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\beta}}{beta} peptide) are associated
  with Alzheimer's disease. Evaluate the ``amyloid cascade hypothesis''
  citing: (a) the evidence for A\texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\beta}}{beta} oligomers (not fibrils) as the toxic
  species; (b) why therapeutic targeting of A\texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\beta}}{beta} aggregation has largely
  failed clinically; (c) an alternative hypothesis involving tau
  protein.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{26}
\tightlist
\item
  Design a protein engineering strategy to convert an enzyme that uses
  NADH as cofactor to one that uses NADPH. Identify the specific
  residues in the coenzyme-binding pocket that differ between
  NADH-specific and NADPH-specific enzymes, and describe what mutations
  you would introduce. What selection pressure would you use in directed
  evolution?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{27}
\tightlist
\item
  RNA aptamers can fold into three-dimensional structures that
  specifically bind proteins (like antibodies but made of RNA). Compare
  RNA and protein as molecular recognition scaffolds: evaluate the
  structural repertoire (functional groups available, backbone rigidity,
  available secondary structures) of each, and explain why protein
  antibodies have been preferred over RNA aptamers clinically, and what
  advantages aptamers offer in terms of synthesis and immunogenicity.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{28}
\tightlist
\item
  Polyhydroxyalkanoates (PHAs) are bacterial polyesters (biological
  plastics). Compare their biosynthesis pathway and polymer chemistry to
  triacylglycerides (TAGs) --- which also function as carbon storage
  molecules in animals. Evaluate whether PHAs could replace
  petroleum-derived plastics industrially, considering degradation
  rates, production cost, and material properties.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{29}
\tightlist
\item
  The hydrophobic core of most globular proteins contains residues with
  about 15--30\% exposed surface area. Propose and critically evaluate
  three evolutionary forces that have driven the formation of the
  hydrophobic core: (a) thermodynamic stability; (b) protection of
  reactive centres; (c) evolutionary constraint on folding kinetics. Use
  a specific example (e.g., cytochrome c, lysozyme) to ground your
  argument.
\end{enumerate}

\section*{Questions --- Ch 4: Enzymes and the Kinetics of
Catalysis}\label{questions-ch-4-enzymes-and-the-kinetics-of-catalysis}
\addcontentsline{toc}{section}{Questions --- Ch 4: Enzymes and the
Kinetics of Catalysis}

\label{sec:q_unit_I_enzymes_and_kinetics}

\subsection*{Instructor Use and Coverage
Notes}\label{instructor-use-and-coverage-notes-6}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Instructor Use and Coverage Notes}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{Coverage target:} Infer Vmax, Km, or inhibition type from data
  and justify the mechanistic interpretation.
\item
  \textbf{Model/data emphasis:} Michaelis-Menten, Lineweaver-Burk, and
  inhibition-pattern calculations.
\item
  \textbf{Assessment alignment:} Concept Explanation, Statistical Tests
  and Data Analysis, Argumentation.
\item
  \textbf{Misconception probe:} A catalyst changes rate, not the
  equilibrium constant or the sign of delta G.
\item
  \textbf{Transfer product:} Apply enzyme-kinetic reasoning to drug
  dosing, metabolic control, or diagnostic assays.
\item
  \textbf{Grading focus:} award full credit for mechanism, evidence,
  boundary conditions, and units when a calculation is required.
\item
  \textbf{Suggested use:} draw one recall item, one application item,
  and one synthesis item when building a short quiz from this bank.
\end{itemize}

\subsection*{Questions 1--10: Recall and
Comprehension}\label{questions-110-recall-and-comprehension-3}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Questions 1--10: Recall and
Comprehension}

\emph{This activity accompanies \cref{sec:unit_I_enzymes_and_kinetics}
of the textbook --- review that chapter before attempting the exercises
below.}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  Define an enzyme. What type of macromolecule are most enzymes? Name
  one exception.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{1}
\tightlist
\item
  What is the active site? Explain the induced fit model.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{2}
\tightlist
\item
  Define activation energy (Ea). How does an enzyme reduce Ea without
  altering \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\Delta}}{Delta}G of the reaction?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{3}
\tightlist
\item
  What are Michaelis-Menten kinetics? Define Km and Vmax.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{4}
\tightlist
\item
  Write the Michaelis-Menten equation. At \hyperref[s]{S} = Km, what
  fraction of Vmax is achieved?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{5}
\tightlist
\item
  Distinguish competitive, non-competitive, and uncompetitive
  inhibition. Which type changes Km? Which changes Vmax?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{6}
\tightlist
\item
  What is a coenzyme? Name two vitamins that serve as coenzymes.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{7}
\tightlist
\item
  What is an allosteric enzyme? How does cooperativity affect the v vs
  \hyperref[s]{S} curve shape?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{8}
\tightlist
\item
  Define feedback inhibition (product inhibition) and give one example
  from a metabolic pathway.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{9}
\tightlist
\item
  How does temperature affect enzyme activity? Name two effects of
  extreme temperatures on enzyme function.
\end{enumerate}

\subsection*{Questions 11--20: Application and
Analysis}\label{questions-1120-application-and-analysis-3}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Questions 11--20: Application and
Analysis}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{10}
\tightlist
\item
  An enzyme has Km = 2 mM and Vmax = 10 \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\mu}}{mu}mol/min. Calculate the reaction
  rate at \hyperref[s]{S} = 1 mM, 2 mM, and 10 mM. What does the
  saturation behaviour tell you about enzyme kinetics?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{11}
\tightlist
\item
  In a competitive inhibition experiment, Km increases from 2 mM to 8
  mM, but Vmax is unchanged (10 \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\mu}}{mu}mol/min). Calculate the inhibitor
  constant Ki if \hyperref[i]{I} = 50 \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\mu}}{mu}M (use the relationship
  K\_m\^{}app = Km(1 + \hyperref[i]{I}/Ki)).
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{12}
\tightlist
\item
  ATCase (aspartate transcarbamoylase) shows sigmoidal kinetics (Hill
  coefficient n = 2) rather than hyperbolic Michaelis-Menten kinetics.
  Explain what the Hill coefficient indicates about subunit
  cooperativity and how CTP (the end product) acts as a heterotropic
  allosteric inhibitor.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{13}
\tightlist
\item
  Temperature doubles reaction rates approximately every 10°C (Q\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{1}}{1}\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{0}}{0} \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\approx}}{~} 2).
  However, above an optimal temperature, enzyme rate drops sharply.
  Explain: (a) why the Arrhenius relationship predicts increasing rate
  with temperature; (b) why denaturation overrides this above Topt; (c)
  how thermophilic enzymes (Tm \textgreater{} 80°C) avoid denaturation.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{14}
\tightlist
\item
  A Lineweaver-Burk (double-reciprocal) plot for enzyme X gives a
  y-intercept of 0.1 \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\mu}}{mu}mol\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{-}}{-}\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{1}}{1}\texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\cdot}}{.}min and x-intercept of \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{-}}{-}0.5 mM\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{-}}{-}\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{1}}{1}. Calculate
  Vmax and Km. If an inhibitor shifts the x-intercept to \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{-}}{-}0.25 mM\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{-}}{-}\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{1}}{1}
  without changing the y-intercept, what type of inhibition is this?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{15}
\tightlist
\item
  Aconitase, an enzyme in the TCA cycle, uses Fe\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{2}}{2}\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{+}}{+} as a cofactor. When
  \emph{E. coli} is iron-starved, aconitase activity is abolished.
  Explain: (a) the likely role of Fe\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{2}}{2}\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{+}}{+} in the active site mechanism; (b)
  why iron starvation globally affects energy metabolism; (c) how some
  bacteria produce iron-chelating siderophores to restore enzyme
  function.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{16}
\tightlist
\item
  Isoenzymes (isozymes) are distinct enzymes that catalyse the same
  reaction but have different kinetic properties. Hexokinase
  (Km\_glucose = 0.1 mM) and glucokinase/hexokinase IV (Km\_glucose = 10
  mM) both catalyse glucose phosphorylation. Explain why the liver
  expresses high-Km glucokinase rather than low-Km hexokinase and how
  this enables hepatic glucose buffering post-meal.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{17}
\tightlist
\item
  Serine proteases (trypsin, chymotrypsin, elastase) use the catalytic
  triad Ser-His-Asp. Explain the mechanism: how does the His residue act
  as a proton acceptor/donor, how does Ser become a nucleophile, and how
  does the oxyanion hole stabilise the tetrahedral intermediate?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{18}
\tightlist
\item
  Ribozymes are RNA enzymes that catalyse phosphodiester bond cleavage.
  Compare ribozyme catalytic mechanisms to protein enzyme mechanisms:
  what functional group strategies can RNA use that proteins cannot (and
  vice versa)? What does the existence of ribozymes tell us about the
  origin of life?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{19}
\tightlist
\item
  Suicide (mechanism-based) inhibitors permanently inactivate enzymes by
  forming covalent bonds after being processed by the enzyme's active
  site. Give a specific clinical example of a suicide inhibitor and
  explain, step-by-step, how it inactivates the target enzyme. Why are
  suicide inhibitors more selective than reversible inhibitors?
\end{enumerate}

\subsection*{Questions 21--30: Synthesis and
Evaluation}\label{questions-2130-synthesis-and-evaluation-3}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Questions 21--30: Synthesis and
Evaluation}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{20}
\tightlist
\item
  Aspirin (acetylsalicylate) irreversibly inhibits COX-1 and COX-2 by
  acetylating Ser530 in the active site. Evaluate: (a) why aspirin's
  anti-platelet effect lasts 7--10 days (the lifetime of a platelet);
  (b) how selective COX-2 inhibitors (celecoxib) were designed to reduce
  GI side effects; (c) the unexpected cardiovascular risk of COX-2
  inhibitors detected primarily after clinical deployment.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{21}
\tightlist
\item
  Design an enzyme engineering experiment to improve the Km of an
  industrial enzyme for a non-natural substrate. Describe: the rational
  design approach using structural data; the directed evolution
  approach; how you would screen large variant libraries; and how you
  would verify that the improved Km reflects genuine active-site
  affinity changes vs changes in protein stability.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{22}
\tightlist
\item
  Enzyme kinetics assumes a well-mixed, dilute environment. However,
  intracellular enzymes operate in a crowded, compartmentalised
  environment with local \hyperref[s]{S} quite different from bulk
  cytoplasm. Evaluate three ways that molecular crowding alters
  effective Km and Vmax in vivo vs in vitro measurements, and propose an
  experimental strategy to measure kinetics in a crowded environment.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{23}
\tightlist
\item
  Zymogen activation (e.g., pepsinogen \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} pepsin) is a mechanism for
  controlling enzyme activity. Evaluate the physiological logic of
  synthesising inactive proenzymes, using three specific examples from
  digestion and blood coagulation. What happens when zymogen activation
  goes wrong (e.g., pancreatitis)?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{24}
\tightlist
\item
  Methotrexate inhibits dihydrofolate reductase (DHFR) by competitive
  inhibition. In cancer chemotherapy, it exploits rapidly dividing
  cells' high demand for folate-derived nucleotides. Evaluate: (a) why
  cancer cells cannot simply overcome competitive inhibition by
  upregulating substrate concentration; (b) why resistance to
  methotrexate often involves DHFR gene amplification; (c) the trade-off
  between therapeutic index and resistance evolution.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{25}
\tightlist
\item
  PCSK9 (proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9) is a serine
  protease that degrades LDL receptors, raising LDL cholesterol.
  Monoclonal antibody inhibitors of PCSK9 dramatically lower LDL.
  Evaluate why an enzyme inhibitor (rather than a simple receptor
  agonist) is necessary here, and explain how the
  enzyme-substrate-inhibitor kinetics differ from conventional
  small-molecule competitive inhibitors targeting PCSK9's active site.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{26}
\tightlist
\item
  Enzymes that catalyse the same reaction in different organisms often
  have different optimal pH values (e.g., pepsin pH 2 vs trypsin pH 8).
  Propose three molecular reasons why the optimal pH of an enzyme is
  tuned to its cellular compartment, and describe how you would
  experimentally shift the pH optimum of pepsin toward neutral pH by
  rational mutation.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{27}
\tightlist
\item
  Single-molecule enzyme kinetics (SMEK) experiments reveal that
  individual enzyme molecules show fluctuating activity --- some are
  momentarily fast, some slow --- a phenomenon called ``dynamic
  disorder.'' Evaluate what SMEK data reveals about the assumptions
  underlying the traditional Michaelis-Menten model, and propose what
  these fluctuations imply for drug design targeting enzymes in disease.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{28}
\tightlist
\item
  Metabolic channelling occurs when the product of enzyme A is directly
  transferred to enzyme B without diffusing into the bulk solution
  (e.g., tryptophan synthase, CAD complex, purinosome). Evaluate the
  advantages of metabolic channelling over free diffusion for: (a)
  reaction efficiency; (b) protection of unstable intermediates; (c)
  prevention of inhibitory product accumulation. Describe one
  experimental test that distinguishes channelling from free diffusion.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{29}
\tightlist
\item
  Criticise the following hypothesis: ``The optimal enzyme evolves to
  have a Km equal to the in vivo substrate concentration.'' Using
  evolutionary arguments, real enzyme kinetic data, and the concept of
  ``catalytic perfection'' (kcat/Km approaching the diffusion limit
  about 10\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{8}}{8}--10\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{9}}{9} M\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{-}}{-}\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{1}}{1}s\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{-}}{-}\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{1}}{1}), evaluate whether enzymes are actually
  at evolutionary optimum, or whether constraints (protein stability,
  pleiotropic effects) prevent optimisation. Cite specific examples.
\end{enumerate}

\newpage

\subsection*{Questions 11--20: Application and

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{10}
\tightlist
\item
  Calculate the surface area-to-volume ratio (SA:V) for spherical cells
  with radii of 1 \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\mu}}{mu}m, 5 \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\mu}}{mu}m, and 10 \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\mu}}{mu}m. Explain why SA:V limits the

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{11}
\tightlist

  (b) vesicle trafficking; (c) cilia; (d) cell shape.

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{12}
\tightlist
\item
  \emph{Thiomargarita namibiensis} is a bacterium \textgreater750 \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\mu}}{mu}m in

  problem?

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{13}
\tightlist
\item
  Describe the experimental basis for the discovery that cells arise
  from pre-existing cells (Pasteur's swan-neck flask experiment).
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{14}
\tightlist
\item
  Explain five lines of molecular evidence supporting the endosymbiotic
  origin of mitochondria.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{15}
\tightlist
\item
  A secretory cell is treated with brefeldin A (disrupts the Golgi).
  Predict the consequences for enzyme secretion.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{16}
\tightlist
\item
  Explain why red blood cells lack a nucleus and mitochondria. What
  metabolic consequences does this create?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{17}
\tightlist
\item
  A mutation eliminates the peroxisomal targeting signal (PTS1) from
  catalase. Where will catalase end up? What biochemical consequence
  results?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{18}
\tightlist
\item
  Ribosome composition differs between prokaryotes (70S = 50S + 30S) and
  eukaryotes (80S = 60S + 40S). How are antibiotics exploited to target
  primarily bacterial ribosomes?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{19}
\tightlist
\item
  A student uses STED super-resolution microscopy and finds that nuclear
  pore complexes are distributed non-randomly on the nuclear envelope,
  clustering near transcriptionally active chromatin. Interpret this
  finding in terms of mRNA export and nuclear architecture.
\end{enumerate}

\subsection*{Questions 21--30: Synthesis and
Evaluation}\label{questions-2130-synthesis-and-evaluation-4}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Questions 21--30: Synthesis and
Evaluation}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{20}
\tightlist
\item
  Evaluate the claim: ``Most life evolved from a single comprehensive
  common ancestor (LUCA).'' What molecular evidence supports LUCA, and
  what evidence (e.g., horizontal gene transfer) complicates the simple
  tree-of-life narrative?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{21}
\tightlist
\item
  Synthetic biology aims to build minimal artificial cells (protocells).
  Evaluate three fundamental hurdles: (a) stable lipid encapsulation;
  (b) genetic self-replication; (c) energy supply. At what stage are
  current (2024--2025) efforts?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{22}
\tightlist
\item
  Organelles proliferate or contract depending on cellular demand.
  Design an experiment to determine whether smooth ER proliferation in
  response to lipid overload is controlled by transcriptional
  upregulation of ER resident proteins or by a different mechanism
  (e.g., membrane lipid incorporation itself driving ER expansion).
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{23}
\tightlist
\item
  Ageing cells accumulate dysfunctional mitochondria. Evaluate the
  ``mitochondrial theory of ageing'': does mitochondrial dysfunction
  cause ageing, or result from it? Cite evidence from caloric
  restriction and NAD+ supplementation studies.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{24}
\tightlist
\item
  Some unicellular organisms (e.g., \emph{Euglena}) contain both
  mitochondria and chloroplasts. Evaluate how a single cell coordinates
  two endosymbiotic organelles with conflicting demands on the cell's
  redox state.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{25}
\tightlist
\item
  Evaluate the role of the centrosome as a signalling hub beyond its
  microtubule-organising function. What kinases localise to the
  centrosome, and how does centrosome duplication failure contribute to
  cancer?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{26}
\tightlist
\item
  Apicoplasts in malaria parasites (\emph{Plasmodium}) are
  non-photosynthetic plastids derived from a secondary endosymbiosis.
  Evaluate them as drug targets --- what essential biosynthetic pathways
  occur exclusively in the apicoplast, and why does targeting apicoplast
  translation (e.g., with doxycycline) kill the parasite but spare human
  cells?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{27}
\tightlist
\item
  Liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS) creates membraneless organelles
  (stress granules, P-bodies). Evaluate the evidence that these
  condensates are functionally equivalent to membrane-bounded organelles
  in concentrating reaction components.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{28}
\tightlist
\item
  Compare the evolutionary trajectories of a symbiotic bacterium
  becoming a mitochondrion vs becoming a lysosome. What structural and
  genomic changes would you expect in each pathway?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{29}
\tightlist
\item
  Critically assess the hypothesis that cancer is a disease of cell
  identity --- a reversion to a primordial unicellular state where
  individual cell fitness (unlimited proliferation, resistance to death)
  overrides multicellular cooperation. What evidence from cancer
  evolutionary biology supports or contradicts this view?
\end{enumerate}
