\section*{Questions --- Ch 6: Cell Structure and
Organelles}\label{questions-ch-6-cell-structure-and-organelles}
\addcontentsline{toc}{section}{Questions --- Ch 6: Cell Structure and
Organelles}

\label{sec:q_unit_II_cell_structure}

\subsection*{Instructor Use and Coverage
Notes}\label{instructor-use-and-coverage-notes-8}

\begin{itemize}

  \textbf{Coverage target:} Predict which organelle or cytoskeletal

  apoptosis, infection, or cell division.

  \textbf{Grading focus:} award full credit for mechanism, evidence,
  boundary conditions, and units when a calculation is required.
\item
  \textbf{Suggested use:} draw one recall item, one application item,
  and one synthesis item when building a short quiz from this bank.

\subsection*{Questions 1--10: Recall and
Comprehension}\label{questions-110-recall-and-comprehension-5}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Questions 1--10: Recall and

\emph{This activity accompanies \cref{sec:unit_II_cell_structure} of the
textbook --- review that chapter before attempting the exercises below.}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}

  Which organelle is responsible for: (a) protein synthesis; (b) lipid
  synthesis; (c) protein glycosylation; (d) intracellular digestion; (e)

\begin{enumerate}

  What is the difference between rough ER and smooth ER in structure and

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{2}
\tightlist

  Describe the cis-to-trans polarity of the Golgi apparatus and the

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{3}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}

\tightlist

  Name the three components of the cytoskeleton and one function of

\begin{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}

\subsection*{Questions 11--20: Application and
Analysis}\label{questions-1120-application-and-analysis-5}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Questions 11--20: Application and
Analysis}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{10}
\tightlist
\item
  Trace the complete path of a secretory protein from its gene to the
  extracellular space, naming every organelle and vesicle type it passes
  through.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{11}
\tightlist
\item
  A mutation disables the signal recognition particle (SRP). Predict the
  fate of a lysosomal enzyme without functional SRP.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{12}
\tightlist
\item
  Colchicine prevents microtubule polymerisation. Would it disrupt: (a)
  chromosome segregation; (b) ER-Golgi trafficking; (c) cell migration;
  (d) axonal transport? Justify each.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{13}
\tightlist
\item
  Gaucher disease results from a deficiency of the lysosomal enzyme
  glucocerebrosidase. What accumulates, in which cells, and why does
  this cause splenomegaly and bone marrow infiltration?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{14}
\tightlist
\item
  If a cell's mitochondria were removed, which metabolic pathways would
  be abolished and which would remain functional? Calculate the maximum
  ATP yield from 1 glucose in a cell without mitochondria.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{15}
\tightlist
\item
  Clathrin-coated vesicles mediate receptor-mediated endocytosis.
  Describe the sequence from receptor-ligand binding to delivery of
  cargo to endosomes. Name two other coat protein systems and their
  functions.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{16}
\tightlist
\item
  Motor proteins kinesin (moves to + end) and dynein (moves to \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{-}}{-} end)
  both use microtubule tracks. How does a cell ensure organelles are
  delivered to the correct destination --- axon terminal vs cell body?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{17}
\tightlist
\item
  The rough ER membrane is studded with ribosomes, while the smooth ER
  is ribosome-free. A mutation eliminates the ribosome-binding site on
  the ER translocon (Sec61). Predict the consequence for: (a) membrane
  protein insertion; (b) secretory protein signal peptide cleavage.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{18}
\tightlist
\item
  Zellweger syndrome (peroxisome biogenesis disorder) causes progressive
  neurological deterioration. Identify two specific metabolic functions
  of peroxisomes in neurons that would be disrupted, and explain the
  mechanism of neural damage.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{19}
\tightlist
\item
  A researcher fuses a nuclear localisation signal (NLS) to a
  cytoplasmic protein (GFP). Describe the molecular events leading to
  the protein's nuclear import, including the roles of importin-\texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\alpha}}{alpha},
  importin-\texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\beta}}{beta}, RanGTP, and the nuclear pore complex.
\end{enumerate}

\subsection*{Questions 21--30: Synthesis and
Evaluation}\label{questions-2130-synthesis-and-evaluation-5}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Questions 21--30: Synthesis and
Evaluation}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{20}
\tightlist
\item
  Primary cilia are now recognised as signalling organelles for
  Hedgehog, Wnt, and PDGFR pathways. Evaluate why concentrating
  receptors in a small ciliary compartment (0.1\% of total cell surface)
  enhances signalling sensitivity compared to distributing receptors
  over the entire plasma membrane.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{21}
\tightlist
\item
  Design an experiment to determine whether a newly discovered organelle
  in a marine protist is related to the peroxisome or the lysosome,
  using: (a) proteomic analysis; (b) membrane lipid analysis; (c)
  fluorescent marker trafficking; (d) inhibitor sensitivity.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{22}
\tightlist
\item
  Autophagy (macro, micro, chaperone-mediated) degrades cytosolic
  material. Evaluate the selective vs non-selective aspects of each
  type, and propose why cells might preferentially use CMA
  (chaperone-mediated autophagy) rather than macroautophagy for
  long-lived soluble proteins.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{23}
\tightlist
\item
  Reticulophagy (selective ER autophagy) is triggered by ER stress.
  Trace the molecular pathway from misfolded protein accumulation \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
  IRE1\texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\alpha}}{alpha}/PERK/ATF6 activation \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} reticulophagy receptor induction \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
  ER-phagy. What would happen if reticulophagy were completely blocked?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{24}
\tightlist
\item
  The Golgi apparatus disperses into ministacks during mitosis and
  reassembles in each daughter cell after division. Evaluate the
  mechanism of Golgi fragmentation (role of mitotic kinases) and
  reassembly (role of p97 ATPase), and explain why Golgi inheritance
  must be coordinated with chromosome segregation.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{25}
\tightlist
\item
  Compare endocytosis mechanisms: clathrin-mediated endocytosis,
  caveolae-mediated endocytosis, macropinocytosis, and phagocytosis. For
  each: what cargo is internalised, what signalling events initiate it,
  and how is cargo processed after internalisation?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{26}
\tightlist
\item
  COPI-coated vesicles mediate retrograde transport from Golgi back to
  ER (retrieval of escaped ER-resident proteins). How do KDEL-bearing
  ER-resident proteins get retrieved? What is the KDEL receptor, and
  what happens to its affinity for KDEL at Golgi pH vs ER pH?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{27}
\tightlist
\item
  The nuclear lamina (lamin intermediate filaments) underlies the inner
  nuclear membrane. Mutations in lamin A cause laminopathies including
  Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome (HGPS) --- a premature ageing
  disease. Evaluate how nuclear structural failure leads to an
  accelerated-ageing phenotype at the cellular level.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{28}
\tightlist
\item
  Cells in developing lungs must convert from secreting surfactant
  (lipid-rich, packaged in lamellar bodies --- lysosome-related
  organelles) to absorbing alveolar fluid at birth. Evaluate the
  signalling mechanisms controlling this switch and what organelle
  remodelling is required.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{29}
\tightlist
\item
  Evaluate the concept of ``organelle crosstalk'': mitochondria-ER
  contact sites (MAM --- mitochondria-associated membranes) facilitate
  Ca\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{2}}{2}\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{+}}{+} and lipid exchange. How does disruption of MAM contact alter: (a)
  mitochondrial Ca\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{2}}{2}\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{+}}{+} buffering; (b) phosphatidylserine transfer; (c)
  mitochondrial morphology? Cite evidence from neurodegenerative disease
  models.
\end{enumerate}

\section*{Questions --- Ch 7: Membrane Structure and
Transport}\label{questions-ch-7-membrane-structure-and-transport}
\addcontentsline{toc}{section}{Questions --- Ch 7: Membrane Structure
and Transport}

\label{sec:q_unit_II_membrane_transport}

\subsection*{Instructor Use and Coverage
Notes}\label{instructor-use-and-coverage-notes-9}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Instructor Use and Coverage Notes}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist

  \textbf{Coverage target:} Calculate or predict ion movement and
  explain which force dominates.

  \textbf{Model/data emphasis:} Nernst, Goldman, osmotic, and
  facilitated-transport calculations.

  Methods, Argumentation.

  \textbf{Misconception probe:} Equilibrium does not mean equal
  concentration; charge and permeability matter.

  \textbf{Transfer product:} Transfer gradient logic to neurons,
  kidneys, roots, and mitochondrial membranes.
\item
  \textbf{Grading focus:} award full credit for mechanism, evidence,
  boundary conditions, and units when a calculation is required.
\item
  \textbf{Suggested use:} draw one recall item, one application item,
  and one synthesis item when building a short quiz from this bank.
\end{itemize}

\subsection*{Questions 1--10: Recall and
Comprehension}\label{questions-110-recall-and-comprehension-6}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Questions 1--10: Recall and
Comprehension}

\emph{This activity accompanies \cref{sec:unit_II_membrane_transport} of
the textbook --- review that chapter before attempting the exercises
below.}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  Describe the fluid-mosaic model of the plasma membrane
  (Singer-Nicolson, 1972). What are the two major components?

\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{1}
\tightlist

  What is a phospholipid bilayer? Explain why it forms spontaneously in
  an aqueous environment.

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{2}
\tightlist

  Define selective permeability. Which types of molecules cross

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{3}
\tightlist

  Distinguish simple diffusion, facilitated diffusion, and active
  transport.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{4}
\tightlist

  What is the sodium-potassium ATPase (Na\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{+}}{+}/K\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{+}}{+}-ATPase)? How many ions
  does it move per ATP?

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{5}
\tightlist

  Define osmosis. In which direction does water move --- toward high or

\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{6}
\tightlist

  What is a membrane potential? What is the typical resting membrane

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{7}
\tightlist

  Distinguish primary from secondary active transport. Give one example

\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{8}
\tightlist
\item
  What is endocytosis? Distinguish phagocytosis, pinocytosis, and
  receptor-mediated endocytosis.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{9}
\tightlist
\item
  What is the role of cholesterol in membrane structure? How does it
  affect fluidity at high and low temperatures?
\end{enumerate}

\subsection*{Questions 11--20: Application and
Analysis}\label{questions-1120-application-and-analysis-6}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Questions 11--20: Application and
Analysis}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{10}
\tightlist
\item
  A cell is placed in a hypertonic solution. Describe, at the molecular
  level, what happens to: (a) the direction of water movement; (b) cell
  volume; (c) the cytoskeleton if shrinkage is severe; (d) membrane
  potential due to increased ion concentration.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{11}
\tightlist
\item
  The Na\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{+}}{+}/K\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{+}}{+}-ATPase pumps 3 Na\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{+}}{+} out and 2 K\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{+}}{+} in per ATP hydrolysed.
  Explain why this creates an electrogenic current. Calculate the charge
  moved per pump cycle and predict how ouabain (a pump inhibitor) would
  affect membrane potential.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{12}
\tightlist
\item
  Glucose enters intestinal epithelial cells via SGLT1 (Na\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{+}}{+}-glucose
  co-transporter) on the apical membrane and exits via GLUT2 (passive
  facilitated diffusion) on the basolateral membrane. Explain: (a) which
  transport is primary active and which is secondary active; (b) why
  this arrangement allows glucose to be absorbed against its
  concentration gradient.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{13}
\tightlist
\item
  CFTR is a Cl\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{-}}{-} channel mutated in cystic fibrosis. The \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\Delta}}{Delta}F508 deletion
  causes CFTR misfolding and ER retention. Explain how this affects: (a)
  epithelial Cl\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{-}}{-} secretion; (b) mucus viscosity; (c) bacterial
  colonisation of airways.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{14}
\tightlist
\item
  A cell biologist measures the fluorescence recovery after
  photobleaching (FRAP) of a fluorescently labelled membrane protein.
  Recovery takes 30 seconds in normal cells but 5 minutes in cells with
  disrupted actin cortex. Interpret this result using the fluid-mosaic
  model and the concept of membrane protein diffusion constraints.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{15}
\tightlist
\item
  Explain how the membrane potential arises from differences in ion
  permeability (Goldman equation). If a cell becomes 10\texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\times}}{x} more permeable
  to Na\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{+}}{+} (e.g., during an action potential), predict the direction of
  change in membrane potential and apply the Nernst equation to estimate
  the equilibrium potential for Na\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{+}}{+}.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{16}
\tightlist
\item
  Vesicle fusion requires SNARE proteins. Explain the zipper model of
  SNARE complex assembly and how this drives membrane fusion. Why does
  botulinum toxin (which cleaves SNARE proteins) block neurotransmitter
  release?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{17}
\tightlist
\item
  Aquaporin-1 (AQP1) is absent in red blood cells from certain
  individuals, yet these individuals are healthy. AQP1 knockout mice
  have impaired urinary concentrating ability. Explain this discrepancy
  --- what does it reveal about the relative importance of aquaporin vs
  lipid bilayer water permeability in different tissues?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{18}
\tightlist
\item
  LDL receptor-mediated endocytosis concentrates LDL receptors in
  clathrin-coated pits. FH (familial hypercholesterolaemia) patients
  lack functional LDL receptors. Explain: (a) why plasma LDL rises
  dramatically; (b) why heterozygous FH is less severe than homozygous;
  (c) why statins partially compensate for LDL receptor deficiency.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{19}
\tightlist
\item
  Membrane asymmetry: phosphatidylserine (PS) is normally on the inner
  leaflet but is exposed on the outer leaflet of apoptotic cells.
  Explain: (a) the enzyme (flippase) that normally maintains PS on the
  inner leaflet; (b) the enzyme (scramblase) that destroys asymmetry
  during apoptosis; (c) the physiological consequence of outer-leaflet
  PS exposure (phagocyte recognition).
\end{enumerate}

\subsection*{Questions 21--30: Synthesis and
Evaluation}\label{questions-2130-synthesis-and-evaluation-6}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Questions 21--30: Synthesis and
Evaluation}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{20}
\tightlist
\item
  Evaluate the thermodynamic basis of lipid raft formation. What causes
  certain lipids (sphingomyelin, cholesterol, saturated phospholipids)
  to phase-separate into liquid-ordered domains? Evaluate the evidence
  that lipid rafts are real functional domains vs artefacts of cold
  detergent extraction.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{21}
\tightlist
\item
  The membrane potential (typically \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{-}}{-}70 mV, inside negative) represents
  stored electrochemical energy. Calculate the energy available per mole
  of Na\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{+}}{+} flowing inward across a neuron membrane using \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\Delta}}{Delta}G = zF\texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\Delta}}{Delta}\texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\Psi}}{Psi} + RT
  ln({[}Na\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{+}}{+}{]}\_in/{[}Na\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{+}}{+}{]}\_out). How does this compare to the energy
  of ATP hydrolysis (about \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{-}}{-}57 kJ/mol at physiological
  concentrations)?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{22}
\tightlist
\item
  Ionophores are small molecules that carry specific ions across lipid
  bilayers. Valinomycin is a K\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{+}}{+}-selective ionophore; gramicidin is a
  non-selective cation channel. Compare their effects on: (a) membrane
  potential; (b) mitochondrial function; (c) cell viability at
  therapeutic vs toxic concentrations. How are they used experimentally
  as tools?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{23}
\tightlist
\item
  Membrane curvature is actively generated during endocytosis, vesicle
  budding, and tubule formation. Evaluate the mechanisms: (a) BAR domain
  protein scaffolding; (b) asymmetric lipid composition; (c) protein
  insertion into the cytoplasmic leaflet. Which mechanism is most
  critical for clathrin-mediated endocytosis at the cell's flat plasma
  membrane?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{24}
\tightlist
\item
  Osmotic stress responses in bacteria involve membrane sensors (e.g.,
  EnvZ osmosensor) that activate two-component signalling systems.
  Compare bacterial osmosensing to mammalian cell osmosensing via
  volume-sensitive ion channels (VSOR). Which system responds faster and
  why?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{25}
\tightlist
\item
  Fatty acid composition of membrane phospholipids changes with
  temperature (homeoviscous adaptation). Design an experiment to
  determine whether \emph{E. coli} adjusts membrane fluidity in response
  to temperature via: (a) transcriptional regulation of fatty acid
  desaturases; (b) selective incorporation of exogenous fatty acids; or
  (c) lipid flip-flop remodelling. What lipid analysis technique would
  you use?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{26}
\tightlist
\item
  P-glycoprotein (MDR1) is an ABC transporter that pumps hydrophobic
  drugs out of cancer cells, causing multidrug resistance. Evaluate: (a)
  why hydrophobic drugs are its substrates; (b) why inhibiting MDR1 has
  largely failed clinically; (c) an alternative strategy (e.g., prodrug
  activation inside the cell) that bypasses MDR1.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{27}
\tightlist
\item
  The mitochondrial inner membrane maintains a proton gradient (\texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\Delta}}{Delta}\texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\mu}}{mu}H\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{+}}{+} =
  \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{-}}{-}200 mV, \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\Delta}}{Delta}pH = 1 unit = \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{-}}{-}59 mV, electrical = \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{-}}{-}141 mV). Using the
  chemiosmotic equation \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\Delta}}{Delta}G = nF\texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\Delta}}{Delta}\texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\Psi}}{Psi} + 2.303RT\texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\Delta}}{Delta}pH, calculate the total
  proton-motive force. How does this compare to the energy needed to
  synthesise ATP from ADP + Pi (about +37 kJ/mol at
  physiological {[}ATP{]}/{[}ADP{]})? Assume 3 H\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{+}}{+} per ATP (c-ring H\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{+}}{+}/ATP
  coupling ratio).
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{28}
\tightlist
\item
  Nanoparticle drug delivery systems exploit endocytosis for
  intracellular drug delivery. Evaluate the barriers nanoparticles face:
  (a) being taken up via endocytosis rather than direct membrane fusion;
  (b) endosomal escape before lysosomal degradation; (c) targeting
  specificity via surface ligands. What design features address each
  barrier?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{29}
\tightlist
\item
  Stretch-activated ion channels (SACs) open when the plasma membrane is
  mechanically deformed. Design a complete research programme to: (a)
  identify the molecular identity of a SAC in cardiac myocytes; (b)
  determine its role in cardiac arrhythmia during myocardial stretch;
  (c) develop a selective SAC inhibitor and evaluate its anti-arrhythmic
  potential in a relevant animal model.
\end{enumerate}

\subsection*{Questions 1--10: Recall and
Comprehension}\label{questions-110-recall-and-comprehension-7}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Questions 1--10: Recall and

textbook --- review that chapter before attempting the exercises below.}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  List the three stages of cell signalling. Give a brief description of
  each stage.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{1}
\tightlist
\item
  Name four chemical classes of signalling molecules. Give one
  biological example of each.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{2}
\tightlist
\item
  Distinguish autocrine, paracrine, endocrine, and contact-dependent
  signalling.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{3}
\tightlist
\item
  What is a G protein-coupled receptor (GPCR)? Name the three subunits
  of the heterotrimeric G protein.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{4}
\tightlist

  Describe the second messengers cAMP and IP\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{3}}{3}/DAG and name the enzymes
  that produce each.

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}

\tightlist

  What is a receptor tyrosine kinase (RTK)? Name two growth factor
  receptors of this type.

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{6}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{7}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{8}
\tightlist

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{9}
\tightlist

  What is the role of protein phosphatases in signal termination?
\end{enumerate}

\subsection*{Questions 11--20: Application and
Analysis}\label{questions-1120-application-and-analysis-7}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Questions 11--20: Application and
Analysis}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{10}
\tightlist
\item
  Adrenaline binds \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\beta}}{beta}-adrenergic receptors (Gs-coupled). Trace the
  complete signalling cascade from ligand binding to glycogen
  phosphorylase activation, naming every molecule. How many molecules of
  glycogen phosphorylase are activated per initial adrenaline molecule?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{11}
\tightlist
\item
  Steroid hormones (e.g., cortisol) exert their effects via
  intracellular receptors that act as transcription factors. Compare the
  timescale, reversibility, and specificity of steroid signalling vs
  adrenaline signalling via GPCR. Which is more suitable for rapid
  physiological responses, and why?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{12}
\tightlist
\item
  Explain how Ca\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{2}}{2}\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{+}}{+} acts as a second messenger. What keeps resting
  cytoplasmic {[}Ca\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{2}}{2}\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{+}}{+}{]} so low (about 100 nM)? What is the
  role of calmodulin as a Ca\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{2}}{2}\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{+}}{+} sensor, and which kinase does
  Ca\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{2}}{2}\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{+}}{+}-calmodulin activate?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{13}
\tightlist
\item
  Trastuzumab (Herceptin) is a monoclonal antibody that targets HER2 (an
  RTK overexpressed in about 25\% of breast cancers). Explain
  its mechanism of action: how does receptor blockade inhibit downstream
  MAPK and PI3K-Akt signalling, and why does HER2 dimerisation (with
  HER3) make it particularly potent?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{14}
\tightlist
\item
  An inhibitor blocks PLC-\texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\beta}}{beta} (phospholipase C-\texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\beta}}{beta}). Predict the effects on:
  (a) IP\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{3}}{3} production; (b) DAG levels; (c) PKC activation; (d)
  intracellular Ca\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{2}}{2}\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{+}}{+} release from the ER; (e) smooth muscle contraction
  downstream of M3 muscarinic receptor activation.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{15}
\tightlist
\item
  Cross-talk between signal pathways allows integration of multiple
  inputs. Describe two specific examples where activation of one
  signalling pathway inhibits or potentiates the response of another
  pathway. How might this cross-talk produce distinct cellular outcomes
  depending on context?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{16}
\tightlist
\item
  Wnt signalling inhibits the destruction complex (APC/Axin/CK1/GSK3\texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\beta}}{beta}),
  allowing \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\beta}}{beta}-catenin to accumulate and enter the nucleus. Explain how
  mutations in APC (found in \textgreater80\% of colorectal cancers)
  constitutively activate Wnt signalling and promote cell proliferation.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{17}
\tightlist
\item
  Nitric oxide (NO) is produced by nitric oxide synthase (NOS) and
  diffuses freely across membranes to activate soluble guanylate cyclase
  (sGC) in smooth muscle cells, producing cGMP. Explain: (a) why NO is
  unusual as a paracrine signal; (b) how sildenafil (Viagra) potentiates
  the NO-cGMP pathway; (c) what happens to cGMP without PDE5 inhibition.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{18}
\tightlist
\item
  Notch signalling requires direct cell-cell contact (juxtacrine). When
  Notch receptor (on receiving cell) binds Delta ligand (on sending
  cell), \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\gamma}}{gamma}-secretase cleaves the Notch intracellular domain (NICD),
  which enters the nucleus. Explain: (a) why this signalling cannot be
  mediated by a diffusible messenger; (b) the role of Notch in lateral
  inhibition during development.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{19}
\tightlist
\item
  TGF-\texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\beta}}{beta} receptors (type I and type II serine/threonine kinase receptors)
  signal via SMAD proteins. Explain: (a) how receptor dimerisation
  activates SMAD2/3 phosphorylation; (b) how SMAD4 forms a complex with
  phospho-SMAD2/3; (c) how this complex regulates target gene
  transcription in the context of tumour suppression vs EMT
  (epithelial-mesenchymal transition).
\end{enumerate}

\subsection*{Questions 21--30: Synthesis and
Evaluation}\label{questions-2130-synthesis-and-evaluation-7}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Questions 21--30: Synthesis and
Evaluation}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{20}
\tightlist
\item
  Evaluate the concept of ``signal integration'': a cell simultaneously
  receives growth factor (MAPK activation), anchorage signals
  (integrin-FAK signalling), and survival signals (insulin \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} PI3K-Akt).
  How does the cell integrate these three pathways to make a
  proliferation vs death decision? Name at least one molecular node
  where most three signals converge.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{21}
\tightlist
\item
  Design a CRISPR screen to identify novel negative regulators of the
  EGFR-MAPK pathway in non-small-cell lung cancer cells. Describe the
  library design, the cellular readout, and how you would validate the
  top hits as therapeutically relevant targets.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{22}
\tightlist
\item
  Receptor endocytosis and downregulation reduce cell sensitivity to a
  signal. However, some endosomal signalling (e.g., from
  endosome-localised EGFR) is qualitatively different from plasma
  membrane signalling. Evaluate the concept of ``spatial encoding'' of
  signal quality by receptor location. What specific downstream
  effectors are activated preferentially from endosomal vs surface
  receptors?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{23}
\tightlist
\item
  Intracellular Ca\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{2}}{2}\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{+}}{+} oscillations are widely used for signal encoding.
  Evaluate how the frequency and amplitude of Ca\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{2}}{2}\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{+}}{+} oscillations can
  encode different cellular responses (NF-\texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\kappa}}{kappa}B vs NFAT activation). What
  molecular mechanism (IP\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{3}}{3}R sensitivity to Ca\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{2}}{2}\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{+}}{+} and inhibition by Ca\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{2}}{2}\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{+}}{+})
  generates oscillations?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{24}
\tightlist
\item
  Synaptic signalling relies on glutamate receptor subtypes (AMPA, NMDA,
  mGluR) with vastly different ion conductances, Ca\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{2}}{2}\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{+}}{+} permeabilities,
  and kinetics. Evaluate how the combination of fast ionotropic (AMPA)
  and slow modulatory (NMDA, mGluR) signalling enables both rapid
  synaptic transmission and long-term plasticity at the same synapse.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{25}
\tightlist
\item
  Drug resistance in targeted therapy often results from mutations that
  reactivate downstream signalling. In BRAF\^{}V600E melanoma treated
  with vemurafenib (BRAF inhibitor), resistance arises via: (a) RAS
  mutation bypassing BRAF; (b) MEK1 mutation making it insensitive; (c)
  RAF1 dimerisation activating MEK. Evaluate why combination therapy
  (BRAF + MEK inhibition) reduces resistance emergence.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{26}
\tightlist
\item
  The PI3K-Akt-mTOR pathway is a master regulator of cell growth and
  metabolism. Evaluate the consequences of complete mTOR inhibition in
  cancer vs healthy cells: why do rapalogs (mTORC1 inhibitors) produce
  cytostatic rather than cytotoxic effects in most cancers, and what
  feedback mechanisms restore Akt activity?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{27}
\tightlist
\item
  Feedback loops in signalling networks can generate bistability
  (switch-like most-or-none responses) or oscillations (e.g., NF-\texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\kappa}}{kappa}B
  oscillations). Evaluate the mathematical conditions (using a two-state
  model) under which positive feedback creates bistability vs
  oscillations. Give one biological example of each.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{28}
\tightlist
\item
  Exosomes (30--150 nm extracellular vesicles) carry signalling
  molecules (proteins, miRNAs, lipids) between cells over long
  distances. Evaluate the evidence that exosomes constitute a bona fide
  signalling mechanism distinct from classical paracrine signalling, and
  propose experimental criteria to distinguish ``exosomal'' from
  conventional secreted-protein-mediated communication.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{29}
\tightlist
\item
  Critically evaluate the ``oncogene addiction'' hypothesis: cancer
  cells become ``addicted'' to a single dominant oncogene signal (e.g.,
  BCR-ABL in CML), making targeted inhibition highly effective. Under
  what conditions does addiction arise, and why do multiple oncogenic
  mutations (e.g., in pancreatic cancer) prevent effective single-agent
  targeted therapy?
\end{enumerate}

\subsection*{Questions 11--20: Application and

Analysis}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{10}
\tightlist
\item
  Calculate the theoretical maximum ATP yield from one glucose molecule
  in aerobic respiration. How does the actual yield (about 30
  ATP) differ from the textbook maximum (about 38), and why?

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{11}
\tightlist
\item
  In anaerobic fermentation, yeast converts pyruvate to ethanol + CO\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{2}}{2}.
  Explain why this regeneration of NAD\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{+}}{+} is essential for continued
  glycolysis, even though no ATP is produced in the process.

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{12}
\tightlist
\item
  Cyanide (CN\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{-}}{-}) blocks Complex IV (cytochrome c oxidase). Predict the
  consequences for: (a) proton gradient; (b) NADH/NAD\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{+}}{+} ratio; (c) ATP
  production; (d) O\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{2}}{2} consumption; (e) lactic acid production.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{13}
\tightlist
\item
  Uncoupling proteins (UCPs) such as thermogenin in brown adipose tissue
  dissipate the proton gradient as heat rather than driving ATP
  synthesis. Explain the physiological role of this process and
  calculate: if 50\% of the proton gradient is uncoupled, what happens
  to O\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{2}}{2} consumption vs ATP output?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{14}
\tightlist
\item
  Glycolysis includes an irreversible phosphofructokinase-1 (PFK-1)
  step. PFK-1 is allosterically activated by AMP. ADP, and F-2,6-BP, and
  inhibited by ATP and citrate. Explain how this regulation matches
  glycolytic rate to cellular energy status.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{15}
\tightlist
\item
  Brown adipose tissue (BAT) is thermogenic. Compare the metabolic
  activity of BAT vs white adipose tissue (WAT): what substrate do they
  preferentially oxidise, how do they regulate UCP1 expression
  (adrenergic \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} cAMP \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} PKA \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} lipolysis \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} FA activation of UCP1), and
  what clinical interest does BAT activation generate?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{16}
\tightlist
\item
  The proton-motive force (pmf) has two components: electrical (\texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\Delta}}{Delta}\texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\Psi}}{Psi} \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\approx}}{~}
  \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{-}}{-}140 mV) and chemical (\texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\Delta}}{Delta}pH \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\approx}}{~} 1 unit = \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{-}}{-}59 mV at 37°C; note sign
  convention for force driving H\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{+}}{+} into the matrix). Calculate the total
  pmf in mV and the Gibbs energy per mole of protons entering the matrix
  (\texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\Delta}}{Delta}G = F\texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\Delta}}{Delta}\texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\Psi}}{Psi} + 2.303RT\texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\cdot}}{.}\texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\Delta}}{Delta}pH).
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{17}
\tightlist
\item
  The malate-aspartate shuttle transfers NADH electrons from the
  cytoplasm into the mitochondrial matrix. Why is this shuttle needed,
  and why does a cell using the glycerol-3-phosphate shuttle instead
  produce slightly less ATP? (Hint: which NADH-equivalent is delivered
  to which complex?)
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{18}
\tightlist
\item
  Cancer cells preferentially use aerobic glycolysis (Warburg effect)
  even when oxygen is available. Propose three mechanistic explanations
  for why rapidly proliferating cells would benefit from this apparently
  inefficient strategy.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{19}
\tightlist
\item
  Chloramphenicol inhibits bacterial 50S ribosomes and mitochondrial
  ribosomes. Explain why chloramphenicol can cause myelosuppression
  (bone marrow failure) after prolonged use, and why it is still used
  clinically when other antibiotics fail.
\end{enumerate}

\subsection*{Questions 21--30: Synthesis and
Evaluation}\label{questions-2130-synthesis-and-evaluation-8}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Questions 21--30: Synthesis and
Evaluation}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{20}
\tightlist
\item
  Evaluate the ATP synthase as a molecular motor. Describe the rotary
  mechanism (F\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{0}}{0} rotation driven by H\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{+}}{+} flux \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} F\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{1}}{1} conformational change \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
  alternating binding-change mechanism). Calculate the torque generated
  if F\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{0}}{0} rotates at 100 rpm with a step size of 120° per ATP.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{21}
\tightlist
\item
  Evaluate the efficiency of oxidative phosphorylation: how close is the
  actual ATP/O ratio to the theoretical maximum, and what factors cause
  inefficiency (proton leak, incomplete coupling)? What impact does
  membrane composition (cardiolipin content) have on coupling
  efficiency?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{22}
\tightlist
\item
  Design an experiment to test whether a newly discovered
  mitochondrially targeted compound acts as an uncoupler, a chain
  blocker, or an ATP synthase inhibitor. What measurements (O\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{2}}{2}
  consumption rate, membrane potential, ATP levels, pH) would you take,
  and in what order?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{23}
\tightlist
\item
  Cells can switch between aerobic respiration, fermentation, and fatty
  acid oxidation. Design a metabolic flux experiment using \texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{1}}{1}\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{3}}{3}C-labelled
  glucose and isotope mass spectrometry (metabolomics) to map which
  pathways are active under normoxia, hypoxia, and caloric restriction.
  What isotopomer patterns would distinguish glycolytic from TCA-derived
  carbon?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{24}
\tightlist
\item
  The pentose phosphate pathway (PPP) branches from glycolysis at G6P
  and produces NADPH and ribose-5-phosphate. Evaluate the relative
  importance of PPP in: (a) red blood cells (where NADPH protects
  against oxidative damage via glutathione); (b) rapidly proliferating
  cancer cells (where ribose is needed for nucleotide synthesis). Design
  a therapeutic strategy targeting the PPP specifically in cancer cells.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{25}
\tightlist
\item
  Mitochondria-derived reactive oxygen species (ROS) cause oxidative
  stress. Evaluate the paradox that low ROS function in redox signalling
  (activating NF-\texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\kappa}}{kappa}B, Nrf2, and HIF-1\texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\alpha}}{alpha}) while high ROS cause
  macromolecular damage. What antioxidant systems exist in mitochondria
  (SOD2, thioredoxin, peroxiredoxin), and how might targeted
  mitochondrial antioxidants (MitoQ, SS-31) prevent disease?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{26}
\tightlist
\item
  Metabolic reprogramming in hypoxia (HIF-1\texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\alpha}}{alpha} pathway) switches cells
  from oxidative phosphorylation to anaerobic glycolysis. Evaluate the
  molecular logic: why would a cell transcriptionally upregulate
  glycolytic enzymes AND simultaneously downregulate Complex IV (via
  COX4-2 subunit switch) AND activate BNIP3-mediated mitophagy
  (selective mitochondrial degradation) in response to O\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{2}}{2} lack?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{27}
\tightlist
\item
  The ketone bodies (\texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\beta}}{beta}-hydroxybutyrate, acetoacetate) produced during
  fasting and ketogenic diets are increasingly recognised as signalling
  molecules (not just fuel). Evaluate the evidence that
  \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\beta}}{beta}-hydroxybutyrate inhibits histone deacetylases (HDACs), thereby
  acting as an epigenetic regulator. What genes are induced, and how
  might this explain the neuroprotective and anti-inflammatory
  properties attributed to ketogenic diets?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{28}
\tightlist
\item
  Thermodynamic coupling in oxidative phosphorylation can be described
  by non-equilibrium thermodynamics. Evaluate: when the ATP/ADP ratio is
  very high, does flow of H\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{+}}{+} through ATP synthase reverse (ATP \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} ADP +
  Pi, using pmf to rotate in reverse)? Under what physiological
  conditions does this reverse mode actually occur, and what is its role
  in maintaining mitochondrial membrane potential when Complex I/III
  activity is inhibited?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{29}
\tightlist
\item
  Critically evaluate the ``two-hit'' model of mitochondrial disease:
  patients with heteroplasmic mtDNA mutations are often asymptomatic
  until a critical threshold (often about 80\% mutated mtDNA)
  is exceeded. What cellular mechanisms (quality control,
  complementation in fused networks) maintain function below the
  threshold? At what threshold does bioenergetic failure occur, and how
  does tissue-specific metabolism (brain vs muscle vs liver) determine
  which tissue is most sensitive?
\end{enumerate}

\section*{Questions --- Ch 10:
Photosynthesis}\label{questions-ch-10-photosynthesis}
\addcontentsline{toc}{section}{Questions --- Ch 10: Photosynthesis}

\label{sec:q_unit_III_photosynthesis}

\subsection*{Instructor Use and Coverage
Notes}\label{instructor-use-and-coverage-notes-12}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Instructor Use and Coverage Notes}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{Coverage target:} Compute carbon-fixation requirements and
  explain a limiting factor.
\item
  \textbf{Model/data emphasis:} Photon, ATP/NADPH, and Calvin-cycle
  stoichiometry.
\item
  \textbf{Assessment alignment:} Representing and Describing Data,
  Statistical Tests and Data Analysis.
\item
  \textbf{Misconception probe:} Plants do not eat sunlight; they use
  light energy to reduce carbon using electrons and enzymes.
\item
  \textbf{Transfer product:} Transfer photosynthetic constraints to
  crops, algae, climate, or ecosystem productivity.
\item
  \textbf{Grading focus:} award full credit for mechanism, evidence,
  boundary conditions, and units when a calculation is required.
\item
  \textbf{Suggested use:} draw one recall item, one application item,
  and one synthesis item when building a short quiz from this bank.
\end{itemize}

\subsection*{Questions 1--10: Recall and
Comprehension}\label{questions-110-recall-and-comprehension-9}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Questions 1--10: Recall and
Comprehension}

\emph{This activity accompanies \cref{sec:unit_III_photosynthesis} of
the textbook --- review that chapter before attempting the exercises
below.}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  Write the overall equation for photosynthesis. Which reactant provides
  O\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{2}}{2}?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{1}
\tightlist
\item
  Locate photosynthesis: in which organelle and in which specific
  membrane compartment do the light reactions occur?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{2}
\tightlist
\item
  What are photosystems I and II? What is the primary electron donor in
  each?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{3}
\tightlist
\item
  Define the Z-scheme. Trace the path of electrons from water to NADP\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{+}}{+}.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{4}
\tightlist
\item
  What are the products of the light reactions passed to the Calvin
  cycle?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{5}
\tightlist
\item
  Name the three stages of the Calvin cycle (also called the C3 cycle or
  light-independent reactions).
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{6}
\tightlist
\item
  What is RuBisCO? What reaction does it catalyse and what is its
  substrate?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{7}
\tightlist
\item
  Distinguish C\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{3}}{3}, C\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{4}}{4}, and CAM plants. Give one example species of each.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{8}
\tightlist
\item
  What is photorespiration? Under what conditions is it maximised?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{9}
\tightlist
\item
  What is the wavelength absorbed by chlorophyll a and chlorophyll b?
\end{enumerate}

\subsection*{Questions 11--20: Application and
Analysis}\label{questions-1120-application-and-analysis-9}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Questions 11--20: Application and
Analysis}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{10}
\tightlist
\item
  DCMU (herbicide, kills plants) blocks the electron acceptor site of
  Photosystem II. Predict its effects on: (a) O\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{2}}{2} evolution; (b) NADPH
  production; (c) ATP (photophosphorylation); (d) the Calvin cycle.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{11}
\tightlist
\item
  Non-cyclic photophosphorylation produces both ATP and NADPH. Cyclic
  photophosphorylation produces primarily ATP. Explain the mechanism of
  cyclic flow (electron recirculates through Fd \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} PQ \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} Cyt b\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{6}}{6}f \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} PSI)
  and when a cell uses cyclic vs non-cyclic flow.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{12}
\tightlist
\item
  A student growing \emph{Arabidopsis thaliana} increases light
  intensity 10-fold. Initially photosynthetic rate rises, then plateaus.
  Explain the two-phase response: which reaction limits at low light
  (light reactions) and which limits at high light (Calvin cycle enzyme
  capacity)?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{13}
\tightlist
\item
  C\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{4}}{4} plants (e.g., maize) separate initial CO\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{2}}{2} fixation (HCO\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{3}}{3}\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{-}}{-} \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
  oxaloacetate, in mesophyll) from RuBisCO (in bundle sheath). Explain:
  (a) how this concentrates CO\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{2}}{2} around RuBisCO; (b) why it reduces
  photorespiration; (c) why C\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{4}}{4} plants outcompete C\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{3}}{3} plants in hot, sunny
  conditions.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{14}
\tightlist
\item
  The quantum yield of O\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{2}}{2} production is about 1 O\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{2}}{2} per 8
  photons absorbed (theoretical: 1 O\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{2}}{2} per 8 photons absorbed). Why is
  this the minimum, and how does the Z-scheme energetically justify why
  4 photons per PSII and 4 per PSI are needed to produce 1 O\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{2}}{2} and 2
  NADPH?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{15}
\tightlist
\item
  Photorespiration occurs when RuBisCO oxygenates RuBP (instead of
  carboxylating it), producing phosphoglycolate, which must be recycled
  through the glycolate pathway. Calculate: if 25\% of RuBisCO reactions
  are oxygenation rather than carboxylation, what fraction of carbon
  fixed is immediately lost? How does this affect net carbon gain?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{16}
\tightlist
\item
  Antenna complexes (LHCI, LHCII) harvest photons and funnel excitation
  energy to reaction centres by resonance energy transfer (Förster
  transfer). Explain: (a) why antenna complexes increase efficiency; (b)
  why there is a risk of photodamage (singlet O\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{2}}{2} production) at high
  light; (c) what non-photochemical quenching (NPQ) does to protect the
  reaction centres.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{17}
\tightlist
\item
  Rubisco activase unfolds the tight inhibitory conformation of RuBisCO
  when CO\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{2}}{2} is absent. Explain: (a) why RuBisCO requires activation
  before catalysis; (b) how activase uses ATP hydrolysis to open the
  active site; (c) why rubisco activase is itself heat-sensitive and
  limits photosynthesis at high temperatures.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{18}
\tightlist
\item
  CAM (Crassulacean acid metabolism) plants open stomata primarily at
  night. Trace: (a) nocturnal CO\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{2}}{2} fixation into malate (by PEPC); (b)
  daytime malate decarboxylation to CO\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{2}}{2}; (c) CO\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{2}}{2} fixation by RuBisCO;
  (d) the advantage in arid environments. Compare water-use efficiency
  (WUE) of CAM vs C\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{3}}{3} plants.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{19}
\tightlist
\item
  The chloroplast ATP synthase (CF\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{1}}{1}F\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{0}}{0}) is structurally similar to the
  mitochondrial ATP synthase. Compare: the direction of proton gradient
  (lumen to stroma vs IMS to matrix); whether CF\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{1}}{1}F\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{0}}{0} can run in reverse
  (hydrolyse ATP to pump H\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{+}}{+}); and the regulatory role of the
  thiol-regulated \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\gamma}}{gamma}-subunit in the dark vs light.
\end{enumerate}

\subsection*{Questions 21--30: Synthesis and
Evaluation}\label{questions-2130-synthesis-and-evaluation-9}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Questions 21--30: Synthesis and
Evaluation}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{20}
\tightlist
\item
  Evaluate the artificial leaf as a technology for solar fuel
  production: splitting water to produce H\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{2}}{2} photochemically. What
  catalysts mimic the Mn cluster of the oxygen-evolving complex (OEC)?
  What are the current efficiency limits, and how do they compare to
  photosynthetic efficiency (about 3\% vs photovoltaic
  about 25\%)?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{21}
\tightlist
\item
  Rising CO\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{2}}{2} atmospheric concentrations (currently about 420
  ppm) should theoretically increase C\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{3}}{3} photosynthesis (CO\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{2}}{2}
  fertilisation effect) but FACE (Free Air CO\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{2}}{2} Enrichment) experiments
  show attenuated responses. Evaluate three mechanisms of
  ``photosynthetic downregulation'' under elevated CO\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{2}}{2} and assess the
  net impact on crop yields.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{22}
\tightlist
\item
  RuBisCO is notoriously inefficient (kcat about 3 s\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{-}}{-}\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{1}}{1},
  compared to \textgreater1,000 s\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{-}}{-}\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{1}}{1} for most enzymes). Evaluate why
  evolution has not improved RuBisCO, and assess recent synthetic
  biology approaches to engineer an improved RuBisCO (e.g., Form II
  RuBisCO from bacteria, directed evolution) for crop improvement.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{23}
\tightlist
\item
  Shade-adapted plants have higher LHCII content and lower PSII/PSI
  ratios than sun plants. Evaluate the molecular mechanisms of this
  acclimation: how does excess excitation pressure in low light signal
  LHCII assembly vs LHCII disassembly in high light? What role does STN7
  kinase (LHCII phosphorylation) play in state transitions?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{24}
\tightlist
\item
  Oxygenic photosynthesis evolved about 2.7 billion years ago
  and fundamentally transformed Earth's atmosphere. Evaluate the
  geochemical evidence (banded iron formations, the Great Oxidation
  Event) for the timing of oxygenic photosynthesis. What was the
  ecological impact on anaerobic life, and how did some lineages evolve
  oxygen tolerance?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{25}
\tightlist
\item
  Synthetic biology has produced a ``photosynthetic organism'' where an
  entire C\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{4}}{4} photosynthetic apparatus is introduced into a C\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{3}}{3} plant (C\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{4}}{4}
  rice project). Evaluate what genetic modifications are required, which
  modifications have been achieved, and what the bottlenecks are for
  realising this in a crop plant.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{26}
\tightlist
\item
  Photoinhibition occurs when PSII is irreversibly damaged by excess
  light. The D1 protein of PSII is a site of photodamage and must be
  replaced every about 30 minutes under high light. Evaluate
  the molecular mechanism of D1 turnover (degradation by FtsH protease,
  ribosomal de novo synthesis, PSII reassembly in thylakoid membrane)
  and explain why this turnover rate limits maximal photosynthetic
  productivity.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{27}
\tightlist
\item
  Horizontal gene transfer of photosynthesis genes between cyanobacteria
  and early eukaryotes (primary endosymbiosis) versus between
  non-photosynthetic organisms and photosynthetic ones (secondary
  endosymbiosis) produced the diverse eukaryotic algal groups. Evaluate
  the complexity of gene transfer that was required to set up a
  functional chloroplast, focusing on the challenge of targeting
  nuclear-encoded proteins to the chloroplast (TIC/TOC translocon
  import).
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{28}
\tightlist
\item
  Phytoplankton (mainly diatoms, dinoflagellates, cyanobacteria) account
  for about 50\% of global CO\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{2}}{2} fixation despite having about
  1\% of terrestrial plant biomass. Evaluate what properties of aquatic
  photosynthesis explain this high per-mass productivity, and assess the
  feasibility of enhancing ocean photosynthesis (e.g., iron
  fertilisation) as a climate change mitigation strategy.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{29}
\tightlist
\item
  Critically assess whether an organism could be engineered to
  simultaneously perform photosynthesis AND oxidative phosphorylation in
  the same compartment. What major thermodynamic and biochemical
  obstacles would need to be overcome? (Consider: O\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{2}}{2} produced by
  photosynthesis would support oxidative phosphorylation, but the
  competing demands for NAD(P)H, the different evolutionary origins of
  the two systems, and the compartmentation challenges in a single
  organelle context.)
\end{enumerate}

\newpage

\section*{Questions --- Ch 11: Metabolic Integration and
Regulation}\label{questions-ch-11-metabolic-integration-and-regulation}
\addcontentsline{toc}{section}{Questions --- Ch 11: Metabolic
Integration and Regulation}

\label{sec:q_unit_III_metabolic_integration}

\subsection*{Instructor Use and Coverage
Notes}\label{instructor-use-and-coverage-notes-13}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Instructor Use and Coverage Notes}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{Coverage target:} Predict how a change in substrate, hormone,
  or enzyme activity redirects flux.
\item
  \textbf{Model/data emphasis:} Energy charge, control points, and
  pathway-flux comparisons.
\item
  \textbf{Assessment alignment:} Representing and Describing Data,
  Statistical Tests and Data Analysis.
\item
  \textbf{Misconception probe:} A pathway is not a one-way assembly
  line; reversibility and regulation define the real route.
\item
  \textbf{Transfer product:} Apply metabolic network reasoning to
  diabetes, fasting, exercise, or cancer metabolism.
\item
  \textbf{Grading focus:} award full credit for mechanism, evidence,
  boundary conditions, and units when a calculation is required.
\item
  \textbf{Suggested use:} draw one recall item, one application item,
  and one synthesis item when building a short quiz from this bank.

\subsection*{Questions 1--10: Recall and
Comprehension}\label{questions-110-recall-and-comprehension-10}

\emph{This activity accompanies
\cref{sec:unit_III_metabolic_integration} of the textbook --- review
that chapter before attempting the exercises below.}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  What does ``metabolic integration'' mean? Give one example of how
  carbohydrate and lipid metabolism are connected.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{1}
\tightlist

  Define anabolism and catabolism. Give one example of each.

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{2}
\tightlist
\item
  What is the role of AMP:ATP ratio as a metabolic signal? Which enzyme
  is the key AMP sensor?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{3}
\tightlist

  What is AMPK? Describe two metabolic processes it activates and two it

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{4}
\tightlist

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}

  Name the organs that play a primary role in glucose homeostasis after

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}

  Define the Cori cycle. Which two organs are involved, and which

\begin{enumerate}

\subsection*{Questions 11--20: Application and
Analysis}\label{questions-1120-application-and-analysis-10}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Questions 11--20: Application and
Analysis}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{10}
\tightlist
\item
  After a high-carbohydrate meal, blood glucose rises. Trace the
  hormonal and metabolic responses in: (a) the pancreas; (b) the liver;
  (c) skeletal muscle; (d) adipose tissue --- over the 2 hours
  post-meal.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{11}
\tightlist
\item
  During prolonged fasting (48 hours), the body must maintain blood
  glucose for the brain. List in order the fuels used: (a) which depot
  is depleted first; (b) when and where does gluconeogenesis begin; (c)
  when do ketone bodies become the primary brain fuel?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{12}
\tightlist
\item
  Insulin stimulates GLUT4 translocation to the plasma membrane of
  muscle and adipose cells via PI3K-Akt-AS160 pathway. Explain the
  molecular cascade from insulin receptor activation to GLUT4 vesicle
  exocytosis. What happens to GLUT4 when insulin is removed?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{13}
\tightlist
\item
  PFK-1 (phosphofructokinase-1) is a key regulatory enzyme of
  glycolysis. It is activated by AMP, ADP, and fructose-2,6-bisphosphate
  (F-2,6-BP) and inhibited by ATP, citrate, and H\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{+}}{+}. Explain how each
  regulator makes physiological sense in terms of energy status
  signalling.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{14}
\tightlist
\item
  A patient with Type 2 Diabetes has high fasting blood glucose and high
  insulin (insulin resistance). Explain: (a) why cells are resistant to
  insulin; (b) why the liver continues gluconeogenesis despite high
  insulin; (c) what happens to HbA1c in chronic hyperglycaemia; (d) why
  metformin (activates AMPK) is effective.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{15}
\tightlist
\item
  The malate-aspartate shuttle moves NADH equivalents from the cytoplasm
  to the mitochondrial matrix. Explain: (a) why direct NADH cannot cross
  the inner mitochondrial membrane; (b) the carrier proteins involved;
  (c) why cardiac muscle prefers this shuttle over the
  glycerol-3-phosphate shuttle.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{16}
\tightlist
\item
  Brown adipose tissue (BAT) thermogenesis is mediated by UCP1. Explain
  the adrenergic activation cascade: cold \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} sympathetic nervous system \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
  \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\beta}}{beta}\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{3}}{3}-adrenergic receptor \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} cAMP \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} PKA \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} hormone-sensitive lipase \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} free
  fatty acid (FFA) release \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} FFA activate/open UCP1 \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} H\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{+}}{+} leak \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} heat. At
  which step is UCP1 expression also increased transcriptionally?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{17}
\tightlist
\item
  Glucagon activates gluconeogenesis in liver cells. Trace from glucagon
  binding \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} Gs \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} cAMP \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} PKA \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} phosphorylation of CREB \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} activation of
  PEPCK and G6Pase gene transcription. How does insulin oppose this
  pathway via Akt (inactivating FOXO1 transcription factor)?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{18}
\tightlist
\item
  The hypothalamus integrates hunger and satiety signals from peripheral
  hormones (leptin, ghrelin, PYY, insulin). Explain: (a) which neurons
  (NPY/AgRP vs POMC/CART) are activated by fasting vs feeding; (b) how
  melanocortin-4 receptor (MC4R) controls food intake; (c) why leptin
  resistance in obesity prevents normalisation of energy balance.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{19}
\tightlist
\item
  Fatty acid synthesis and \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\beta}}{beta}-oxidation cannot occur simultaneously ---
  they would create a futile cycle. Explain how the cell prevents this:
  (a) what molecule inhibits carnitine palmitoyltransferase I (CPTI)
  during fatty acid synthesis; (b) in which compartment is malonyl-CoA
  produced; (c) why this system specifically blocks mitochondrial FA
  import while allowing FA synthesis in the cytoplasm.
\end{enumerate}

\subsection*{Questions 21--30: Synthesis and
Evaluation}\label{questions-2130-synthesis-and-evaluation-10}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Questions 21--30: Synthesis and
Evaluation}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{20}
\tightlist
\item
  Evaluate the ``fuel partitioning'' hypothesis in obesity: does obesity
  arise primarily from excess carbohydrate or excess fat intake, and
  does macronutrient composition matter for energy balance beyond
  caloric excess? Cite the results of isocaloric controlled diet trials.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{21}
\tightlist
\item
  Evaluate the ketogenic diet as a treatment for drug-resistant
  epilepsy. Propose at least three molecular mechanisms by which
  elevated ketone bodies (\texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\beta}}{beta}-hydroxybutyrate primarily as an HDAC
  inhibitor, adenosine release, or KATP channel opening) could reduce
  neuronal excitability.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{22}
\tightlist
\item
  Design an experiment to determine whether AMPK activation in liver
  cells reduces hepatic glucose output primarily by: (a) decreasing
  gluconeogenesis gene expression; (b) acutely phosphorylating and
  inactivating TORC2 (CREB co-activator); (c) decreasing hepatic ATP to
  slow enzymatic gluconeogenesis. Distinguish these mechanisms using
  selective inhibitors and reporter assays.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{23}
\tightlist
\item
  Evaluate the evidence for ``metabolic flexibility'' --- the ability of
  healthy cells to switch between glucose and fat oxidation based on
  substrate availability. How does this differ in Type 2 Diabetes,
  insulin resistance, and cancer cells? What biochemical assay (Seahorse
  XF analyser) measures metabolic flexibility?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{24}
\tightlist
\item
  The metabolic role of the gut microbiome is increasingly recognised:
  SCFAs (acetate, propionate, butyrate) produced by bacterial
  fermentation of dietary fibre signal to host cells. Evaluate how
  propionate signals to the liver (inhibiting gluconeogenesis) and
  butyrate signals to colonocytes (primary fuel) and immune cells (HDAC
  inhibition, regulatory T cell induction).
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{25}
\tightlist
\item
  Evaluate the metabolic rationale for intermittent fasting (IF)
  regimens (16:8 time-restricted eating, 5:2 alternate-day fasting).
  Identify three metabolic benefits of IF beyond simple caloric
  restriction, and propose the molecular mechanisms driving each
  benefit.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{26}
\tightlist
\item
  Cancer cells depend on glutamine (not glucose) for anaplerosis ---
  replenishing TCA cycle intermediates for biosynthesis. Evaluate: (a)
  which TCA intermediate is most depleted in rapidly proliferating
  cells; (b) how glutamine enters the TCA cycle (via glutaminase \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
  glutamate \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\alpha}}{alpha}-ketoglutarate); (c) why targeting glutamine metabolism
  (CB-839, a glutaminase inhibitor) might be selectively toxic to cancer
  cells.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{27}
\tightlist
\item
  Evaluate the concept of ``metaflammation'' --- the chronic low-grade
  inflammation seen in obesity. Propose a mechanistic link from
  adipocyte lipid overload \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} ER stress \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} NF-\texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\kappa}}{kappa}B activation \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
  pro-inflammatory cytokine (TNF-\texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\alpha}}{alpha}, IL-6) secretion \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} insulin resistance
  in muscle and liver. At which step would you intervene
  pharmacologically?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{28}
\tightlist
\item
  NAFLD (non-alcoholic fatty liver disease) progresses from steatosis \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
  NASH (steatohepatitis) \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} cirrhosis. Evaluate the ``two-hit
  hypothesis'': what is the first hit (lipid accumulation), what is the
  second hit (oxidative stress, inflammatory cytokines from adipose
  tissue or gut microbiome), and why targeting a single hit is
  insufficient for treatment?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{29}
\tightlist
\item
  Critically evaluate the use of GLP-1 receptor agonists (semaglutide,
  tirzepatide) for obesity treatment. What are the distinct mechanisms
  by which GLP-1 agonists reduce appetite (hypothalamic signalling),
  slow gastric emptying, and promote pancreatic \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\beta}}{beta}-cell survival? What
  are the metabolic consequences of rapid weight loss induced by these
  drugs (muscle loss, bone density) and how should therapy be managed?
\end{enumerate}

\section*{Questions --- Ch 12: DNA Replication and the Cell
Cycle}\label{questions-ch-12-dna-replication-and-the-cell-cycle}

the Cell Cycle}
