\subsection*{Instructor Use and Coverage
Notes}\label{instructor-use-and-coverage-notes-14}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Instructor Use and Coverage Notes}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{Coverage target:} Calculate replication timing or error burden
  and infer checkpoint consequences.
\item
  \textbf{Model/data emphasis:} Replication-fork speed, error-rate, and
  cell-cycle timing calculations.
\item
  \textbf{Assessment alignment:} Concept Explanation, Questions and
  Methods, Argumentation.
\item
  \textbf{Misconception probe:} High fidelity is not automatic; it is
  built from multiple partially redundant safeguards.
\item
  \textbf{Transfer product:} Transfer replication logic to cancer,
  aging, viral replication, or antibiotic targets.
\item
  \textbf{Grading focus:} award full credit for mechanism, evidence,
  boundary conditions, and units when a calculation is required.
\item
  \textbf{Suggested use:} draw one recall item, one application item,
  and one synthesis item when building a short quiz from this bank.
\end{itemize}

\subsection*{Questions 1--10: Recall and
Comprehension}\label{questions-110-recall-and-comprehension-11}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Questions 1--10: Recall and
Comprehension}

\emph{This activity accompanies
\cref{sec:unit_IV_dna_replication_and_cell_cycle} of the textbook ---
review that chapter before attempting the exercises below.}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  Describe the semiconservative model of DNA replication. What
  experiment confirmed it (Meselson-Stahl, 1958)?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{1}
\tightlist
\item
  List the enzymes required for DNA replication and state one function
  of each.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{2}
\tightlist
\item
  Why does DNA polymerase require a primer? Who synthesises the primer?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{3}
\tightlist
\item
  Distinguish the leading strand from the lagging strand during
  replication. Why does the lagging strand form Okazaki fragments?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{4}
\tightlist
\item
  What is the replication fork? Name the enzyme that separates the
  double helix at the fork.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{5}
\tightlist
\item
  Name the four phases of the eukaryotic cell cycle. What occurs in
  each?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{6}
\tightlist
\item
  What are cyclins and cyclin-dependent kinases (CDKs)? Give one example
  of a cyclin-CDK pair and its function.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{7}
\tightlist
\item
  What is a checkpoint? Name three checkpoints in the cell cycle and
  their functions.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{8}
\tightlist
\item
  What does the tumour suppressor protein p53 do when DNA damage is
  detected?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{9}
\tightlist
\item
  What is telomerase? Why do most somatic cells lack telomerase
  activity?
\end{enumerate}

\subsection*{Questions 11--20: Application and
Analysis}\label{questions-1120-application-and-analysis-11}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Questions 11--20: Application and
Analysis}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{10}
\tightlist
\item
  Using the Meselson-Stahl data: if \texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{1}}{1}\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{5}}{5}N/\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{1}}{1}\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{5}}{5}N-labelled DNA is allowed to
  replicate for two rounds in \texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{1}}{1}\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{4}}{4}N medium, what densities of DNA are
  expected and in what proportions? Show your reasoning with a diagram.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{11}
\tightlist
\item
  DNA polymerase III (prokaryotic) and DNA polymerase \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\delta}}{delta}/\texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\varepsilon}}{epsilon} (eukaryotic)
  require a processivity clamp (\texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\beta}}{beta}-clamp in prokaryotes; PCNA in
  eukaryotes). Explain how the sliding clamp increases processivity, and
  why this matters for replication speed of the 3 \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\times}}{x} 10\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{9}}{9} bp human genome.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{12}
\tightlist
\item
  Okazaki fragments in eukaryotes are about 200 nucleotides
  (roughly one nucleosome length). After primase removes the primer, DNA
  pol \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\delta}}{delta} fills the gap using the downstream Okazaki fragment as a flap.
  Explain the role of FEN1 (flap endonuclease) and DNA ligase in
  completing lagging strand synthesis.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{13}
\tightlist
\item
  The G\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{1}}{1}/S checkpoint (restriction point) ensures cells don't enter S
  phase with insufficient resources or DNA damage. Explain the molecular
  mechanism: how does mitogen (growth factor) signalling lead to Rb
  phosphorylation \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} release of E2F transcription factor \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} S-phase gene
  expression? At what step does p16 (CDKN2A tumour suppressor) block
  this pathway?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{14}
\tightlist
\item
  Aphidicolin blocks DNA polymerase \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\alpha}}{alpha} and \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\delta}}{delta}, arresting cells at the G\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{1}}{1}/S
  boundary. Hydroxyurea (HU) depletes dNTP pools. Compare the effects of
  each drug on: (a) replication fork speed; (b) fork stalling vs
  collapse; (c) activation of ATR checkpoint kinase; (d) cell cycle
  arrest phase.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{15}
\tightlist
\item
  Telomere shortening occurs at a rate of about 100 bp per cell
  division in most somatic cells. Calculate how many divisions a cell
  with initial telomere length of 15 kb could undergo before reaching
  the critical length of 6 kb. What happens to cells that continue
  dividing past this limit (crisis)?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{16}
\tightlist
\item
  The spindle assembly checkpoint (SAC) detects kinetochores not under
  tension (unattached to spindle microtubules). Explain the molecular
  mechanism: how does an unattached kinetochore produce the wait
  anaphase signal (MCC complex), how does this inhibit APC/C
  (anaphase-promoting complex), and what happens to separase and cohesin
  when SAC is satisfied?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{17}
\tightlist
\item
  CDK1-Cyclin B drives entry into mitosis. CDK1-Cyclin B phosphorylates
  nuclear lamins (dissolving the nuclear envelope), activates condensin
  (chromosome condensation), and activates APC/C (through intermediate
  steps). Explain why Cyclin B must be abruptly degraded at the
  metaphase-anaphase transition.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{18}
\tightlist
\item
  Oncogenes often bypass cell cycle checkpoints. Compare how Ras
  (constitutively active mutant) vs Myc (overexpressed) each drive cell
  cycle progression: through which cyclin-CDK pair(s) do they act, and
  why do cells with oncogenic mutations often also need to lose p53 or
  Rb to become fully cancerous?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{19}
\tightlist
\item
  Yeast two-hybrid screens identified that geminin (overexpressed in
  many cancers) inhibits Cdt1, preventing re-licensing of origins of
  replication. Explain: (a) what origin licensing means; (b) why
  re-replication would be catastrophic; (c) how overexpression of
  geminin PREVENTS re-replication by preventing MCM loading even after S
  phase begins.
\end{enumerate}

\subsection*{Questions 21--30: Synthesis and
Evaluation}\label{questions-2130-synthesis-and-evaluation-11}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Questions 21--30: Synthesis and
Evaluation}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{20}
\tightlist
\item
  Evaluate the precision of the S-phase checkpoint: ATR kinase is
  activated by RPA-coated single-stranded DNA (from stalled forks). How
  does this trigger CHK1 activation \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} Cdc25A phosphorylation \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
  degradation \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} CDK2 inactivation \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} fork stabilisation? What happens if
  ATR is constitutively inactive (as in a mutation)?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{21}
\tightlist
\item
  Design an experiment to test whether telomerase reactivation in a
  telomere-shortened cancer cell line would allow unlimited
  proliferation or would require additional changes. Include: how you
  would deliver hTERT (the catalytic subunit), how you would measure
  telomere length over generations, and what growth advantage you would
  expect and under what assay conditions.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{22}
\tightlist
\item
  DNA replication is not 100\% accurate --- polymerase error rate is
  about 1 in 10\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{7}}{7}. After mismatch repair (MMR), the rate drops
  to about 1 in 10\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{9}}{9}. Evaluate: (a) the molecular mechanism of
  MMR (MutS, MutL, excision, resynthesis); (b) why MMR deficiency causes
  microsatellite instability (MSI); (c) why MSI cancers respond better
  to immune checkpoint inhibitors (PD-1 blockade).
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{23}
\tightlist
\item
  Evaluate origin-of-replication usage in cancer: cancer cells often
  show replication stress (RFS --- replication fork stalling) due to
  premature S-phase entry driven by oncogenes. Propose how elevated RFS
  leads to: (a) DSB (double-strand break) formation at stalled forks;
  (b) inappropriate NHEJ repair causing chromosomal translocations; (c)
  selection pressure for p53 loss (cells that could normally
  checkpoint-arrest now instead die, so p53 loss allows survival).
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{24}
\tightlist
\item
  The pre-replication complex (pre-RC) assembly (ORC \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} Cdc6 \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} Cdt1 \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
  MCM2-7) licenses origins from late mitosis to G\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{1}}{1}. Evaluate two
  licensing control systems: (a) Cdt1 degradation (Cullin4-Cdt2 E3
  ligase triggered by PCNA on DNA); (b) Geminin inhibition of Cdt1.
  Propose why two redundant mechanisms are needed, and what would happen
  if both were inactivated simultaneously.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{25}
\tightlist
\item
  Replication stress is thought to be the earliest event in
  pre-cancerous lesions (before DNA mutation). Evaluate the evidence
  from oncogene-induced senescence (OIS): how does RAS\^{}V12
  overexpression initially stall replication forks and activate the DNA
  damage response (p53-p21 axis, producing cellular senescence) before
  genomic instability occurs?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{26}
\tightlist
\item
  Centromere identity in eukaryotes is determined not by DNA sequence
  but by the presence of CENP-A (a histone H3 variant). Evaluate the
  epigenetic model of centromere inheritance: how is CENP-A loaded (by
  HJURP chaperone) at each S phase, and how can a ``centromere'' be
  moved to a new chromosomal location (neocentromere formation)?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{27}
\tightlist
\item
  Multi-fork replication in prokaryotes: \emph{E. coli} can initiate
  replication at the same origin before the previous round is complete
  (multi-fork replication), allowing doubling times faster than the
  S-phase duration. Evaluate whether eukaryotes could employ multi-fork
  replication and what structural constraints (nuclear envelope,
  nucleosomes, cohesin) would prevent this.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{28}
\tightlist
\item
  Evaluate the hypothesis that cancer is fundamentally a disease of the
  cell cycle: most hallmarks of cancer (unlimited proliferation, evasion
  of apoptosis, invasion) result from failure of cell cycle checkpoints
  rather than from any particular oncogenic mutation. Construct the best
  argument for and against this view using specific molecular examples.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{29}
\tightlist
\item
  Critically evaluate the kinetics of DNA repair: NHEJ (non-homologous
  end joining, fast, about 30 min) and HR (homologous
  recombination, slow, requires sister chromatid, restricted to S/G2).
  Predict the consequences for genomic integrity if NHEJ were the
  primary repair pathway available in a cell. Why is NHEJ
  ``error-prone'' at the molecular level, and what types of mutations
  does it introduce?
\end{enumerate}

the textbook --- review that chapter before attempting the exercises
below.}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  Define gene expression. What are the two major steps?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{1}
\tightlist
\item
  Describe the structure of a eukaryotic mRNA from 5' to 3', including
  most regulatory elements.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{2}
\tightlist
\item
  What is the role of RNA polymerase II in transcription? Where does it
  bind?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{3}
\tightlist
\item
  Define a transcription factor. Distinguish general vs specific
  transcription factors.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{4}
\tightlist
\item
  What is RNA splicing? What molecular machinery performs it?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{5}
\tightlist
\item
  Define the genetic code. What is a codon? How many codons encode amino
  acids?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{6}
\tightlist
\item
  What is the ribosome composed of? Name the three ribosomal sites (A,
  P, E sites).
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{7}
\tightlist
\item
  Describe initiation, elongation, and termination of translation in
  eukaryotes.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{8}
\tightlist
\item
  What is tRNA? What is the anticodon, and what is aminoacyl-tRNA
  synthetase?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{9}
\tightlist
\item
  What is the wobble hypothesis? Which position of the codon allows
  degeneracy?
\end{enumerate}

\subsection*{Questions 11--20: Application and
Analysis}\label{questions-1120-application-and-analysis-12}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Questions 11--20: Application and
Analysis}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{10}
\tightlist
\item
  Pre-mRNA splicing must be precise to within one nucleotide. Explain
  the two-step transesterification mechanism of splicing and the role of
  branch point A, 5' splice site, and 3' splice site in spliceosome
  assembly.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{11}
\tightlist
\item
  Alternative splicing generates multiple protein isoforms from one
  gene. \emph{Drosophila Dscam} gene can produce \textgreater38,000
  isoforms through mutually exclusive exon splicing. Explain: (a) the
  general mechanism of alternative splicing; (b) why \emph{Dscam}
  diversity is important for axon guidance in neural wiring; (c) one
  human disease caused by aberrant alternative splicing.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{12}
\tightlist
\item
  The 5' cap (m\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{7}}{7}G) and poly-A tail of eukaryotic mRNA serve similar
  functions --- protecting mRNA from exonuclease attack and promoting
  translation initiation. Explain: (a) how the 5' cap is added; (b) how
  eIF4E binding to the cap recruits the 43S pre-initiation complex; (c)
  why some viruses (e.g., poliovirus) cleave eIF4G to direct ribosomes
  to IRES sequences instead.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{13}
\tightlist
\item
  The ribosome proof-reads aminoacyl-tRNA selection at the A site.
  Explain: (a) initial selection based on codon-anticodon base pairing
  (induced fit); (b) proofreading step (kinetokinetics --- GTPase
  activation primarily if correct aa-tRNA is bound); (c) why errors
  occur at about 1 in 10,000 vs DNA polymerase errors of 1 in
  10\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{9}}{9} (why is translation less accurate?).
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{14}
\tightlist
\item
  Cycloheximide blocks the elongation step of eukaryotic translation
  (not prokaryotic), because it specifically inhibits the 60S subunit
  translocation step. Explain: (a) what translocation means
  mechanistically; (b) why prokaryotic ribosomes (70S) are not blocked;
  (c) how this selectivity is exploited in laboratory cell biology
  experiments.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{15}
\tightlist
\item
  Nonsense-mediated mRNA decay (NMD) degrades mRNAs with premature stop
  codons. Explain: (a) how the cell recognises a premature vs normal
  stop codon (role of exon-junction complexes); (b) the UPF1/SMG
  cascade; (c) why NMD is a quality control mechanism that also
  regulates normal gene expression for about 10\% of genes.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{16}
\tightlist
\item
  Polyribosomes (polysomes) consist of multiple ribosomes simultaneously
  translating the same mRNA. If a 1,500-nt coding sequence is occupied
  by ribosomes spaced on average every 80 nt, how many ribosomes are
  simultaneously translating this mRNA? Calculate the rate of protein
  synthesis per mRNA if each ribosome adds 2 amino acids/sec.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{17}
\tightlist
\item
  Internal ribosome entry sites (IRES) allow cap-independent translation
  initiation, used by viruses (Hepatitis C, poliovirus) and in cellular
  stress responses, when eIF4E activity is reduced. Compare
  IRES-mediated vs cap-dependent initiation: which cellular proteins are
  replaced by viral ITAF proteins, and under what stress conditions does
  cellular IRES-mediated translation occur?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{18}
\tightlist
\item
  The signal recognition particle (SRP) recognises hydrophobic signal
  peptides emerging from ribosomes translating secretory proteins.
  Explain: (a) how SRP stalls translation while targeting the ribosome
  to the rough ER; (b) how signal peptidase cleaves the signal peptide
  in the ER lumen; (c) what happens to cytosolic misfolded proteins
  lacking a signal peptide vs ER-targeted ones.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{19}
\tightlist
\item
  Transcription factors bind specific DNA sequences (motifs). A
  transcriptional activator contains a DNA-binding domain (DBD) and an
  activation domain (AD). Explain: (a) what structural motifs are common
  in DBDs (zinc finger, helix-turn-helix, leucine zipper); (b) how the
  activation domain recruits the Mediator complex; (c) how enhancers
  (located kb away from promoters) loop to contact the preinitiation
  complex through cohesin-mediated chromosome looping.
\end{enumerate}

\subsection*{Questions 21--30: Synthesis and
Evaluation}\label{questions-2130-synthesis-and-evaluation-12}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Questions 21--30: Synthesis and
Evaluation}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{20}
\tightlist
\item
  Evaluate the dual role of SR proteins (serine-arginine-rich splicing
  factors) in both constitutive and alternative splicing and mRNA
  export. What does the dual role of SR proteins reveal about the
  evolutionary coupling between nuclear RNA processing and cytoplasmic
  translation?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{21}
\tightlist
\item
  Design a comprehensive experiment to map most enhancers controlling a
  specific gene in a given cell type using: (a) H3K27ac ChIP-seq (active
  enhancer mark); (b) ATAC-seq (open chromatin); (c) HiC chromatin
  conformation capture; (d) CRISPR deletion of candidate enhancers and
  transcriptional output measurement. How would you prioritise which
  enhancers are most important?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{22}
\tightlist
\item
  The ``RNA world'' hypothesis proposes that early life was based on RNA
  molecules that could both carry genetic information and catalyse
  reactions. Evaluate: (a) the evidence supporting RNA world (ribozymes,
  ribosome as a ribozyme, universality of the genetic code); (b) the
  transition from RNA world to the DNA-protein world; (c) what modern
  ribozymes tell us about the chemistry of early catalysis.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{23}
\tightlist
\item
  Transcription and translation are physically coupled in prokaryotes
  (translation begins before transcription is complete). Evaluate the
  consequences of this coupling: how does it allow attenuation
  (regulation of transcription termination by ribosome speed), and why
  would coupling like this have evolved in prokaryotes but not
  eukaryotes (where transcription and translation are spatially
  separated)?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{24}
\tightlist
\item
  Ribosome biogenesis occurs in the nucleolus and is rate-limiting for
  cell growth. Evaluate the regulatory relationship between mTORC1, Pol
  I transcription of rDNA, and ribosome biogenesis. Why does mTOR
  inhibition suppress cell growth even in cells with unlimited amino
  acid supply?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{25}
\tightlist
\item
  Evaluate the molecular mechanism of translation by the ribosome in the
  context of the ``peptidyl transferase'' ribosome activity:
  specifically, is the catalysis chemical (RNA catalysis) or entropic
  (positioning effect)? Cite the key experiment (Nobel Prize 2009) that
  settled this debate.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{26}
\tightlist
\item
  Single-molecule translation experiments using fluorescently labelled
  ribosomes and mRNAs have revealed ``pausing'' during elongation
  opposite rare codons, and ``synchronised'' waves of ribosome density
  on mRNA. Evaluate what these observations reveal about codon usage
  optimisation and how synonymous mutations (same amino acid, different
  codon) can dramatically affect protein folding by altering translation
  speed.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{27}
\tightlist
\item
  Design a gene therapy strategy for a patient with haemophilia A
  (lacking factor VIII). Compare: mRNA therapy (synthetic mRNA with
  pseudo-uridine modification for stability); AAV vector gene therapy
  (liver-tropism, long-term expression); and base editing (correct the
  point mutation in situ). Evaluate the trade-offs in immunogenicity,
  duration of effect, and delivery efficiency.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{28}
\tightlist
\item
  RNA interference (RNAi) was discovered when dsRNA triggered gene
  silencing in \emph{C. elegans} (Fire and Mello, 1998). Evaluate the
  mechanism (Dicer, RISC, Ago2-mediated cleavage), the evolutionary
  origin of RNAi (antiviral defence), and the clinical development of
  siRNA therapeutics (inclisiran for PCSK9 silencing). What advantages
  does siRNA have over antisense oligonucleotides (ASOs) for gene
  silencing?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{29}
\tightlist
\item
  Critically evaluate the concept of the ``central dogma'' (DNA \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} RNA \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
  protein). Identify three biological exceptions that violate a strict
  reading of the central dogma (reverse transcription, RNA editing,
  prion replication), explain their mechanisms, and assess whether these
  exceptions require a fundamental revision of the central dogma or
  merely represent elaborations within the same framework.
\end{enumerate}

\subsection*{Questions 1--10: Recall and
Comprehension}\label{questions-110-recall-and-comprehension-13}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Questions 1--10: Recall and
Comprehension}

\emph{This activity accompanies
\cref{sec:unit_IV_mutations_and_genomics} of the textbook --- review
that chapter before attempting the exercises below.}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  Define a mutation. Classify mutations by: (a) type of base change; (b)
  effect on the protein.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{1}
\tightlist
\item
  What is a frameshift mutation? How does an insertion vs deletion cause
  this?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{2}
\tightlist
\item
  What are transposons? Distinguish replicative (copy-and-paste) from
  non-replicative (cut-and-paste) transposons.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{3}
\tightlist
\item
  What is the Ames test? What does a positive result indicate?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{4}
\tightlist
\item
  Describe the three types of DNA damage repair: (a) nucleotide excision
  repair (NER); (b) base excision repair (BER); (c) mismatch repair
  (MMR).
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{5}
\tightlist
\item
  What is CRISPR-Cas9? Where does CRISPR originate in bacteria?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{6}
\tightlist

  What is gRNA (guide RNA) and what does it do in the Cas9 complex?

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{7}
\tightlist
\item
  Define the PAM sequence. Why is it required for CRISPR cutting?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{8}
\tightlist
\item
  What is whole-genome sequencing (WGS)? What sequencing technology is
  most commonly used?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{9}
\tightlist
\item
  What is a single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP)? How many SNPs does the
  average human genome contain?
\end{enumerate}

\subsection*{Questions 11--20: Application and
Analysis}\label{questions-1120-application-and-analysis-13}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Questions 11--20: Application and
Analysis}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{10}
\tightlist
\item
  A chemotherapy drug causes G:C \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} A:T transitions. What type of DNA
  damage mechanism does this suggest (alkylation, intercalation,
  cross-linking, or depurination)? What repair pathway would normally
  correct this damage?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{11}
\tightlist
\item
  Xeroderma pigmentosum (XP) patients have mutations in NER pathway
  genes (XPA-XPG). Explain: (a) what lesion NER repairs (CPDs from
  UV-B); (b) why XP patients have dramatically increased skin cancer
  risk; (c) why the nervous system is also affected in some XP subtypes.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{12}
\tightlist
\item
  A researcher designs a CRISPR experiment to correct a point mutation
  (G\texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}A) in the \emph{HBB} gene causing sickle-cell disease. List: (a)
  the guide RNA design rules; (b) the delivery method for cells (RNP
  electroporation vs viral vector); (c) why homology-directed repair
  (HDR, requiring a donor template) is needed rather than NHEJ; (d) how
  to increase HDR efficiency.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{13}
\tightlist
\item
  A patient's tumour has microsatellite instability (MSI-high) due to
  MMR deficiency. Explain: (a) what kinds of mutations accumulate in
  MSI-high tumours; (b) why MSI tumours produce many neoantigens; (c)
  why pembrolizumab (anti-PD-1) is effective in MSI-high tumours
  regardless of cancer type (tissue-agnostic treatment).
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{14}
\tightlist
\item
  Transposaon Alu (SINE family) comprise about 11\% of the
  human genome. Explain: (a) how Alu elements replicate via RNA
  intermediates (SINE retrotransposition); (b) how an Alu insertion in
  exon 16 of BRCA2 could cause breast cancer; (c) how the host genome
  suppresses transposon activity in the germline (piRNA pathway).
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{15}
\tightlist
\item
  GWAS (genome-wide association studies) have identified thousands of
  SNPs associated with disease risk, but most are in non-coding regions.
  Explain: (a) why non-coding SNPs are biologically meaningful (enhancer
  activity, splicing regulation); (b) how eQTL analysis links SNPs to
  gene expression levels; (c) why a SNP with odds ratio 1.2 for Type 2
  Diabetes is clinically uninformative for individual risk prediction.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{16}
\tightlist
\item
  The P53 gene is mutated in \textgreater50\% of all human cancers.
  Explain: (a) the ``gain-of-function'' mutations in TP53 (R248W, R175H)
  that not only eliminate tumour suppression but actively promote
  invasion; (b) how wild-type p53 regulates CDK inhibitor p21 and
  pro-apoptotic PUMA; (c) what therapeutic strategy (restoring wild-type
  TP53 conformation using small molecules --- APR-246) is being tested.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{17}
\tightlist
\item
  Gene therapy for Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD, caused by large
  deletions in \emph{Dystrophin}) uses exon skipping with antisense
  oligonucleotides (AONs). Explain: (a) why some deletions cause severe
  DMD while frameshifted deletions are less severe (in-frame vs
  out-of-frame); (b) how AON targeting exon 51 restores the reading
  frame; (c) why this produces ``Becker-like'' dystrophin rather than
  fully corrected dystrophin.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{18}
\tightlist
\item
  Epigenome-wide association studies (EWAS) examine DNA methylation
  differences between cases and controls. Explain: (a) why methylation
  differences (epimutations) are harder to interpret than genetic
  mutations; (b) why cell-type composition confounds EWAS analysis; (c)
  how MR (Mendelian randomisation) can be used to determine whether
  methylation changes are causal or merely correlative with disease.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{19}
\tightlist
\item
  Oxford Nanopore sequencing reads individual DNA/RNA molecules by
  measuring ionic current changes as they pass through a protein pore.
  Compare this technology to Illumina short-read sequencing: advantages
  (read length, direct RNA, base modifications, real-time),
  disadvantages (raw error rate about 5\% vs \textless0.1\%),
  and the application where each is most suitable.
\end{enumerate}

\subsection*{Questions 21--30: Synthesis and
Evaluation}\label{questions-2130-synthesis-and-evaluation-13}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Questions 21--30: Synthesis and
Evaluation}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{20}
\tightlist
\item
  Evaluate the safety of germline CRISPR editing (modifying embryo DNA,
  producing heritable changes) as attempted by He Jiankui in 2018.
  Identify three specific scientific risks (off-target edits, mosaicism,
  unintended immune consequences) and three ethical concerns (informed
  consent, enhancement vs therapy, equity of access). What international
  governance frameworks should govern germline editing?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{21}
\tightlist
\item
  A patient carries a disease-associated haplotype in which short reads
  map poorly because a 3-kb insertion and nearby promoter variant are
  absent from the linear reference. Design a graph-aware interpretation
  workflow: compare a single-reference call, a pangenome graph path, and
  long-read validation; then explain when base editing, prime editing,
  or Casgevy-style enhancer disruption would be the most defensible
  therapeutic logic.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{22}
\tightlist
\item
  Evaluate the ``cancer genome atlas'' concept: sequencing thousands of
  tumour genomes has generated a mutation landscape for most cancer
  types, identifying ``drivers'' vs ``passengers.'' What statistical
  criteria distinguish drivers from passengers, and why have most cancer
  driver mutations proven difficult to target therapeutically?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{23}
\tightlist
\item
  Synthetic chromosomes have been designed and built in yeast (Sc2.0,
  synthetic chromosome project). Evaluate the design principles (removal
  of transposons, recombination tags added, inducible evolution mode via
  SCRaMbLE), and discuss whether a fully synthetic human chromosome
  could be built and what it would require.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{24}
\tightlist
\item
  Transposons in the germline are silenced by piRNAs (PIWI-interacting
  RNAs). The piRNA pathway (PIWI proteins, ping-pong amplification)
  produces a feed-forward silencing loop. Evaluate: (a) how piRNAs
  recognise transposons without classical Watson-Crick base pairing; (b)
  why depletion of PIWI proteins causes germline transposon mobilisation
  and infertility in mice; (c) whether piRNAs can also target
  non-transposon mRNAs.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{25}
\tightlist
\item
  Precision oncology based on tumour sequencing identifies actionable
  mutations. However, intratumoral heterogeneity (ITH) means that some
  cells within the tumour may lack the targeted mutation. Evaluate: (a)
  how clonal vs subclonal mutations are distinguished by variant allele
  frequency; (b) why targeting a clonal mutation (present in most cells)
  is more likely to be effective; (c) how liquid biopsy (circulating
  tumour DNA, ctDNA) can detect resistance mechanisms before clinical
  progression.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{26}
\tightlist
\item
  Evaluate whether ``de-extinction'' (reviving extinct species via
  CRISPR genome editing of a close relative) is scientifically feasible
  for: (a) the woolly mammoth (editing \emph{Loxodonta africana} genome
  about 50 key cold-adaptation genes); (b) the passenger pigeon
  (\emph{Ectopistes migratorius}, using band-tailed pigeon as template).
  What are the ecological risks of reintroducing de-extinct animals?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{27}
\tightlist
\item
  Retroviral integration (HIV integrates into host genome) is both a
  challenge for cure research and a tool for gene therapy vectors.
  Evaluate the ``semi-random'' integration pattern of HIV (preference
  for active transcription units) and how this differs from AAV
  (predominantly episomal in non-dividing cells, rare integration at
  AAVS1 safe harbour). Why does insertional mutagenesis risk differ
  between retroviral and AAV gene therapies?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{28}
\tightlist
\item
  tRNA suppressors can read through stop codons, restoring protein
  production from genes with premature stop mutations. Evaluate the
  therapeutic use of aminoglycoside antibiotics (gentamicin) as
  readthrough agents for nonsense mutations (e.g., in \emph{Dystrophin})
  --- what are the molecular mechanisms, the challenges of specificity
  (also read through normal stop codons), and the clinical results to
  date?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{29}
\tightlist
\item
  Critically evaluate the technical and ethical implications of building
  a ``minimal synthetic cell'' with a fully defined genome (as in the
  Venter Institute's JCVI-syn3.0, about 473 genes). What does
  the set of essential genes reveal about the minimal requirements for
  cellular life? If this minimal genome could be commercially
  manufactured and sold, what biosafety and biosecurity regulations
  should apply?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}

\item
  Define epigenetics. Give two examples of epigenetic modifications.

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}

\tightlist

  What is DNA methylation? Which nucleotide is typically methylated in
  mammals, and what effect does methylation at gene promoters generally
  have on transcription?

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{2}

\item
  What is a histone? Name four types of histone modification and one

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}

\tightlist

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}

\item

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}

\begin{enumerate}

\subsection*{Questions 11--20: Application and
Analysis}\label{questions-1120-application-and-analysis-14}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Questions 11--20: Application and
Analysis}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{10}
\tightlist
\item
  A CpG island in the CDKN2A (p16) promoter is hypermethylated in a lung
  cancer cell. Trace the molecular consequences: (a) which protein is
  silenced; (b) what happens to CDK4/6 activity; (c) what happens to
  cell cycle progression; (d) why this is an alternative mechanism to
  p16 deletion for bypassing the G\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{1}}{1} checkpoint.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{11}
\tightlist
\item
  Polycomb repressive complex 2 (PRC2) trimethylates H3K27 and is
  overexpressed in many cancers. Explain: (a) the molecular mechanism of
  H3K27me3-mediated gene silencing; (b) how PRC2 spreads repression
  across large chromosomal domains; (c) why EZH2 (the catalytic subunit
  of PRC2) is a therapeutic target (tazemetostat).
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{12}
\tightlist
\item
  In the lac operon, explain the logic of dual control by the lac
  repressor AND catabolite activator protein (CAP). Under which
  combination of conditions is the operon most highly transcribed? Under
  which is it completely silent?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{13}
\tightlist
\item
  RNA interference (RNAi) via siRNA silences gene expression
  post-transcriptionally. Compare siRNA (perfectly complementary \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} mRNA
  cleavage by Ago2) vs miRNA (partially complementary \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} translational
  repression and mRNA destabilisation). How does each affect the
  steady-state abundance of target mRNA?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{14}
\tightlist
\item
  Enhancers can activate promoters over distances of \textgreater1 Mb in
  the genome by chromatin looping mediated by cohesin and CTCF. Explain:
  (a) the role of CTCF as a chromatin barrier/insulator; (b) how loss of
  a CTCF binding site at the IGF2/H19 imprinting control region (ICR)
  causes Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome; (c) how 4C and HiC experiments
  confirm enhancer-promoter looping.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{15}
\tightlist
\item
  The X-inactivation centre (Xic) on the inactive X chromosome produces
  Xist lncRNA, which coats the inactive X in cis. Explain: (a) how Xist
  RNA spreads along the chromosome; (b) how it recruits PRC2 (H3K27me3)
  and PRC1 (H2AK119ub1) to compact the Xi; (c) why a small region
  (pseudo-autosomal region, PAR) escapes X-inactivation.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{16}
\tightlist
\item
  A researcher uses Cas9 fused to a DNMT3A (DNA methyltransferase)
  domain (dCas9-DNMT3A) to specifically methylate a target promoter.
  Predict: (a) the epigenetic effect at the target gene; (b) whether the
  silencing will be maintained through DNA replication (yes, DNMT1
  maintenance methyltransferase copies the pattern); (c) how you would
  verify that methylation, not dCas9 binding alone, is responsible for
  silencing.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{17}
\tightlist
\item
  Transgenerational epigenetic inheritance refers to the transmission of
  epigenetic marks across generations without DNA sequence change. The
  agouti mouse model showed that maternal methyl-donor diet changes
  offspring coat colour and obesity risk via CpG methylation of the Avy
  allele. What does this imply about the erasure of epigenetic marks
  between generations (which normally occurs in primordial germ cells)?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{18}
\tightlist
\item
  Long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) number \textgreater100,000 in the human
  transcriptome but most have unknown functions. Evaluate the challenges
  of studying lncRNA function: (a) conservation is low across species
  (cannot use model organisms easily); (b) knockdown may affect the
  genomic region itself (enhancer function of the locus); (c) lncRNAs
  have complex secondary structure but no ORFs. Propose a systematic
  approach to determine function.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{19}
\tightlist
\item
  Chromatin accessibility (measured by ATAC-seq) is strongly correlated
  with gene expression. Explain: (a) how nucleosome positioning
  regulates transcription factor accessibility; (b) the role of pioneer
  transcription factors (e.g., FOXA1) in opening closed chromatin; (c)
  how ATAC-seq works mechanistically (Tn5 transposase cuts accessible
  DNA and adds sequencing adapters).
\end{enumerate}

\subsection*{Questions 21--30: Synthesis and
Evaluation}\label{questions-2130-synthesis-and-evaluation-14}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Questions 21--30: Synthesis and
Evaluation}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{20}
\tightlist
\item
  Evaluate the claim that cancer is largely an epigenetic disease. Cite
  evidence from: (a) global hypomethylation and CpG island
  hypermethylation in cancer; (b) frequent mutations in chromatin
  remodelling enzymes (ARID1A, SMARCA4, KMT2D) in cancer; (c) the
  success of HDAC inhibitors and DNMT inhibitors clinically. Under what
  conditions are purely epigenetic therapies (without targeted mutation
  correction) appropriate?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{21}
\tightlist
\item
  Design a pharmaceutical strategy to reactivate a silenced tumour
  suppressor gene in a cancer with promoter hypermethylation. Compare
  DNMT inhibitors (5-azacitidine, broad demethylation), targeted
  dCas9-TET1 (site-specific demethylation), and HDAC inhibitors. What
  are the risks of broad epigenome reprogramming vs targeted approaches?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{22}
\tightlist
\item
  Super-enhancers are clusters of enhancers (about 25--50 kb)
  bound by an unusually high density of transcription factors (BRD4,
  Mediator), associated with strong transcription of oncogenes (MYC,
  BCL2) in cancer. Evaluate the evidence for super-enhancer addiction in
  cancer cells, and explain why BET bromodomain inhibitors (JQ1)
  preferentially disengage from super-enhancers over typical enhancers.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{23}
\tightlist
\item
  Evaluate the concept of ``epigenetic clock'' (Horvath clock):
  methylation of specific CpG sites in blood DNA correlates with
  biological age more accurately than chronological age. What do
  deviations from the epigenetic clock predict? Can lifestyle
  interventions (caloric restriction, exercise) reduce epigenetic age,
  and what experimental evidence supports this?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{24}
\tightlist
\item
  3D chromatin organisation (TADs --- topologically associating domains)
  is largely maintained by CTCF and cohesin. Evaluate what would happen
  to gene regulation if cohesin loading were abolished globally: (a)
  which enhancer-promoter pairs would become aberrantly activated; (b)
  what new gene expression states would emerge; (c) is this consistent
  with the observation that cohesin mutations cause Cornelia de Lange
  syndrome?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{25}
\tightlist
\item
  CRISPR interference (CRISPRi) uses dCas9-KRAB (a transcriptional
  repressor) to silences target genes without cutting DNA. Compare
  CRISPRi with ASO (antisense oligonucleotide) knockdown at the mRNA
  level and classical promoter deletion by CRISPR. What are the
  therapeutic advantages of CRISPRi (temporal control, reversibility, no
  off-target DSBs)?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{26}
\tightlist
\item
  Maternal nutrition during peri-conception affects offspring health
  across the life course (Barker/DOHaD hypothesis). Using three specific
  nutrients (folate, methionine, choline) and their roles in one-carbon
  metabolism \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} SAM production \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} methyltransferase substrate supply,
  evaluate the molecular mechanism by which poor maternal nutrition
  could cause persistent epigenetic changes in offspring that increase
  adult diabetes or cardiovascular disease risk.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{27}
\tightlist
\item
  Evaluate the concept of ``bivalent chromatin domains'' in embryonic
  stem cells: developmental gene promoters carry both active (H3K4me3)
  and repressive (H3K27me3) marks simultaneously, maintaining them in a
  ``poised'' state. How does this enable rapid differentiation in either
  direction, and what happens to bivalent domains as cells commit to a
  specific lineage?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{28}
\tightlist
\item
  Fragile X syndrome is caused by CGG repeat expansion (\textgreater200
  repeats) in the \emph{FMR1} gene's 5' UTR, leading to hypermethylation
  and gene silencing. Evaluate the molecular relationship between repeat
  expansion and hypermethylation: which comes first, what protein
  (MBNL1/DNMT3A) reads the repeat expansion, and why does the
  ``premutation'' (55--200 repeats) have a partially different phenotype
  (FXTAS) compared to full mutation?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{29}
\tightlist
\item
  Critically evaluate the potential of epigenetic editing as a permanent
  therapeutic intervention. Specifically: if dCas9-DNMT3A is used to
  methylate and silence an oncogene, will the silencing persist through
  cell division (via DNMT1 maintenance methylation), and what are the
  risks of epigenetic drift or passenger methylation at off-target
  sites? Propose experimental criteria to determine whether a
  therapeutic epigenetic edit is ``safe and durable.''
\end{enumerate}

\subsection*{Questions 11--20: Application and
Analysis}\label{questions-1120-application-and-analysis-15}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Questions 11--20: Application and
Analysis}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{10}
\tightlist
\item
  A black cat (BB) is crossed with a white cat (bb). What is the F\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{1}}{1}
  phenotype? What is the F\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{2}}{2} ratio if F\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{1}}{1} cats are interbred? If black is
  incompletely dominant, what is the F\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{1}}{1} phenotype?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{11}
\tightlist
\item
  A chi-square analysis of 580 pea seeds (450 round:130 wrinkled) gives
  \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\chi}}{chi}\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{2}}{2} = 2.6 (critical value 3.84, p = 0.05). Should the null hypothesis
  of 3:1 ratio be rejected? What does this conclusion mean biologically?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{12}
\tightlist
\item
  Two true-breeding strains of wheat produce red and white kernels. The
  cross produces medium-red F\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{1}}{1}, and F\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{2}}{2} shows a continuous range of
  colours with frequencies approximately 1:4:6:4:1. This is consistent
  with two genes each contributing an additive unit of colour. What mode
  of inheritance does this illustrate?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{13}
\tightlist
\item
  A woman is phenotypically normal but her father had phenylketonuria
  (PKU, autosomal recessive). What is the probability that she is a
  carrier? If she marries a known carrier, what is the probability their
  first child will have PKU?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{14}
\tightlist
\item
  In coat colour genetics of Labrador retrievers: B is dominant for
  black pigment; b is recessive (brown/chocolate). E is dominant for
  coat expression; ee gives yellow regardless of B/b. Set up the
  dihybrid cross BbEe \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\times}}{x} BbEe and calculate the expected ratio of
  black:chocolate:yellow.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{15}
\tightlist
\item
  ABO blood type shows codominance (A and B antigens) and simple
  recessive (O, no antigen). A man of unknown blood type has a type O
  child with a type A woman (confirmed genotype IA\^{}i). What is the
  man's blood type? What are most possible blood types of this union's
  children?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{16}
\tightlist
\item
  Maternal effect genes in \emph{Drosophila} (e.g., \emph{bicoid})
  determine the embryo's polarity based on the maternal genotype, not
  the embryo's genotype. Explain how this violates the simple Mendelian
  expectation that offspring phenotype reflects offspring genotype. What
  does this tell us about developmental genetics?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{17}
\tightlist
\item
  Haemophilia A is X-linked recessive. A carrier woman (X\^{}H X\^{}h)
  has children with a normal man (X\^{}H Y). What are the expected
  phenotype ratios for daughters? For sons? What is the probability that
  the first four children include at least two affected sons (use
  binomial distribution)?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{18}
\tightlist
\item
  Set up and interpret the F\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{2}}{2} results of a dihybrid cross (AaBb \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\times}}{x} AaBb)
  if the two genes show complementary epistasis (A-B- = one phenotype;
  A-bb, aaB-, aabb = albino). What is the expected ratio? What does this
  imply about the biochemical pathway?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{19}
\tightlist
\item
  Three pea plants of unknown genotype most produce round seeds. Two
  plants crossed to a wrinkled plant (rr) produce: plant A = most round;
  plant B = 50\% round:50\% wrinkled; plant C = 75\% round:25\%
  wrinkled. Determine the genotype of each plant and explain the
  crosses.
\end{enumerate}

\subsection*{Questions 21--30: Synthesis and
Evaluation}\label{questions-2130-synthesis-and-evaluation-15}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Questions 21--30: Synthesis and
Evaluation}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{20}
\tightlist
\item
  Evaluate the concept of ``genetic heterogeneity'': the same phenotype
  (e.g., congenital deafness) can result from mutations in any of
  \textgreater100 different genes, each segregating in different
  families. How does genetic heterogeneity complicate: (a) pedigree
  analysis; (b) population frequency estimates; (c) the development of a
  comprehensive gene therapy?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{21}
\tightlist
\item
  Design a genetic screen in \emph{C. elegans} to identify most genes
  involved in a specific pathway (e.g., vulva development). Describe the
  EMS (ethyl methanesulfonate) mutagenesis strategy, the phenotypic
  screen, and how you would determine whether two mutations affect the
  same gene (complementation test) or the same pathway (epistasis test).
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{22}
\tightlist
\item
  Quantitative traits (height, intelligence, blood pressure) are
  determined by many genes plus environment. Evaluate the methodology of
  heritability estimation from twin studies: what does h\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{2}}{2} = 0.8 actually
  mean, and why does high heritability NOT mean that environmental
  interventions are ineffective? Use PKU as a concrete counter-example.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{23}
\tightlist
\item
  Evaluate Mendel's choice of pea traits: most seven traits happened to
  be either not linked or on different chromosomes. If two of Mendel's
  traits had been tightly linked (say, flower colour and pod colour on
  the same chromosome), how would the F\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{2}}{2} data have deviated from the
  9:3:3:1 ratio, and would Mendel still have discovered independent
  assortment?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{24}
\tightlist
\item
  Inbreeding increases homozygosity and can reveal recessive deleterious
  alleles. Calculate the inbreeding coefficient (F) for offspring of a
  first-cousin mating, and predict the increase in: (a) homozygosity for
  a rare allele (q = 0.01); (b) probability of autosomal recessive
  disease compared to random mating. Why do many societies have legal or
  cultural prohibitions against close-relative marriages?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{25}
\tightlist
\item
  Anticipation (increasing severity across generations) occurs in
  trinucleotide repeat disorders (Huntington's disease, myotonic
  dystrophy). Explain the molecular mechanism by which repeats expand
  between generations (slippage during DNA replication) and why larger
  repeats cause earlier onset and greater severity. Why is repeat
  expansion more common through the paternal germline in HD but the
  maternal germline in DM1?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{26}
\tightlist
\item
  Evaluate the concept of ``genomic imprinting conflict'' (kinship
  theory): paternally imprinted genes (expressed primarily from paternal
  allele) are generally growth-promoting (\emph{IGF2}), while maternally
  imprinted genes (expressed primarily from maternal allele) are
  generally growth-restraining (\emph{H19}). Evaluate the evolutionary
  logic that predicts this based on parent-offspring conflict theory.
  What happens when this balance is disrupted (Silver-Russell syndrome
  vs Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome)?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{27}
\tightlist
\item
  Multifactorial diseases (Type 1 Diabetes, schizophrenia) have both
  genetic and environmental contributions. Evaluate the strengths and
  limitations of GWAS and polygenic risk scores: (a) minimum detectable
  effect size at genome-wide significance (p \textless{} 5\texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\times}}{x}10\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{-}}{-}\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{8}}{8}); (b)
  the ``missing heritability'' problem; (c) why PRS transferability
  across ancestries is a scientific and equity concern; (d) what consent
  and privacy information belongs in a clinical PRS report.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{28}
\tightlist
\item
  Phenocopies are environmentally caused conditions that resemble
  genetic conditions. Thalidomide-induced limb malformations in
  1950s--60s phenocopied the autosomal recessive condition phocomelia.
  Evaluate: (a) how phenocopies complicate pedigree analysis; (b) how
  you would distinguish a phenocopy from a genetic condition in a
  clinical or research context; (c) the ethical implications of
  confusing genetic and environmental causation for public health
  policy.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{29}
\tightlist
\item
  Critically evaluate Mendel's pea experiments, considering: (a) sample
  sizes (he used thousands of plants, giving high statistical power);
  (b) evidence that Mendel may have ``improved'' his data (Weldon's 1902
  re-analysis and Ronald Fisher's 1936 statistical critique suggesting
  perfect ratios are too good to be true); (c) whether Mendel's results
  are reproducible, and what this debate reveals about the role of
  confirmation bias in science.
\end{enumerate}

\subsection*{Questions 1--10: Recall and
Comprehension}\label{questions-110-recall-and-comprehension-16}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Questions 1--10: Recall and
Comprehension}

\emph{This activity accompanies
\cref{sec:unit_V_chromosomal_inheritance} of the textbook --- review
that chapter before attempting the exercises below.}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  What is a chromosome? How many chromosomes does a normal human somatic
  cell contain?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{1}
\tightlist
\item
  Define linkage. Why do linked genes violate Mendel's law of
  independent assortment?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{2}
\tightlist
\item
  What is a centimorgan (cM)? What recombination frequency corresponds
  to 1 cM?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{3}
\tightlist
\item
  Describe the process of crossing over. At what stage of meiosis does
  it occur?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{4}
\tightlist
\item
  What is a genetic map? How is it constructed from recombination
  frequency data?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{5}
\tightlist
\item
  What is X-linked inheritance? Give two examples of X-linked recessive
  disorders.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{6}
\tightlist
\item
  Define nondisjunction. What aneuploid conditions result from
  nondisjunction at meiosis I vs meiosis II?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{7}
\tightlist
\item
  What is trisomy 21? What maternal-age-related risk factor is
  associated with it?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{8}
\tightlist
\item
  What is a chromosomal translocation? How does the Philadelphia
  chromosome arise?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{9}
\tightlist
\item
  What is a karyotype? How is one prepared?
\end{enumerate}

\subsection*{Questions 11--20: Application and
Analysis}\label{questions-1120-application-and-analysis-16}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Questions 11--20: Application and
Analysis}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{10}
\tightlist
\item
  Three linked genes A, B, C have pairwise recombination frequencies:
  A--B = 12\%, B--C = 7\%, A--C = 19\%. Does map distance A--C equal
  A--B + B--C? If not, why, and what genetic phenomenon accounts for the
  discrepancy?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{11}
\tightlist
\item
  Morgan's experiments showed that white eye and miniature wing in
  \emph{Drosophila} are X-linked and linked to each other (recombination
  frequency about 36\%). Explain how these results violate both
  Mendel's laws simultaneously, and how recombination still produces
  some parental and recombinant gamete classes.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{12}
\tightlist
\item
  A man with colour blindness (X-linked recessive) who has normal vision
  has a sister who is a confirmed carrier. What is the probability that
  his daughter will: (a) be a carrier; (b) be colour blind; (c) have
  normal vision? What is the probability any son of his will be colour
  blind?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{13}
\tightlist
\item
  Barr bodies (condensed inactive X chromosomes) are present in cells
  with \textgreater1 X chromosome: 1 Barr body per n+1 X chromosomes.
  How many Barr bodies would be present in cells from: (a) 46,XX female;
  (b) 47,XXX female (triple X); (c) 47,XXY male (Klinefelter); (d) 45,X
  female (Turner)?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{14}
\tightlist
\item
  Down syndrome (trisomy 21) risk rises with maternal age. Propose a
  mechanistic explanation: which proteins hold meiosis I arrested in the
  human oocyte, how does cohesin decline with age, and how does
  premature chromatid separation \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} nondisjunction \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} trisomy? Name the
  specific cohesin subunit implicated.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{15}
\tightlist
\item
  Robertsonian translocation Down syndrome: a chromosome 21 fuses to
  chromosome 14. A carrier parent (45 chromosomes, with 14;21
  translocation) produces offspring via meiosis. Using a diagram, show
  the three viable gamete types and predict the proportion of offspring
  who have translocation Down syndrome, normal karyotype, and carrier
  status.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{16}
\tightlist
\item
  The Fst (fixation index) of a particular autosomal gene between two
  human populations is 0.08. Interpret this value: how much of total
  human genetic variation lies between populations vs within
  populations? Compare this to the claim that ``race explains most human
  genetic variation.''
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{17}
\tightlist
\item
  Huntington's disease is autosomal dominant. The causative allele (HTT
  with \textgreater36 CAG repeats) shows near-100\% penetrance. If an
  affected parent (heterozygous, Hh) has five children, what fraction
  are expected to be affected? Why does penetrance differ from simple
  Mendelian dominant inheritance in this context?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{18}
\tightlist
\item
  Genomic imprinting: if the paternal allele of IGF2 is expressed and
  the maternal allele is silenced, predict the phenotype of: (a) a child
  who inherits a deletion on the paternal chromosome 11
  (Beckwith-Wiedemann: overgrowth); (b) a child inheriting a deletion on
  the maternal chromosome 11 (Silver-Russell: growth restriction). Use
  the concept of parent-of-origin-specific expression to explain both.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{19}
\tightlist
\item
  Inversion heterozygosity in \emph{Drosophila} suppresses recombination
  in the inverted region because crossing over within an inversion
  produces unbalanced chromosomes (duplications and deletions), which
  are lethal. Explain the mechanism and why evolution often preserves
  inversions if they capture coadapted gene complexes.
\end{enumerate}

\subsection*{Questions 21--30: Synthesis and
Evaluation}\label{questions-2130-synthesis-and-evaluation-16}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Questions 21--30: Synthesis and
Evaluation}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{20}
\tightlist
\item
  Evaluate the role of the synaptonemal complex (SC) in meiotic
  recombination: how does the SC align homologous chromosomes, what
  components does it consist of, and how does SC disassembly correlate
  with chiasma formation? What happens when SC formation fails?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{21}
\tightlist
\item
  Comparative genomic hybridisation (CGH) and SNP arrays detect copy
  number variation (CNVs) across the genome. Evaluate the clinical
  utility of chromosomal microarray (CMA) analysis in: (a) prenatal
  diagnosis (replacing karyotyping?); (b) diagnosing children with
  unexplained intellectual disability; (c) identifying germline vs
  somatic CNVs in cancer. What is the main limitation of CMA vs
  long-read sequencing for CNV detection?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{22}
\tightlist
\item
  Design an experiment to map the XIC (X-inactivation centre) on the
  human X chromosome using: (a) X-autosome translocation cell lines; (b)
  CRISPR deletion of candidate regions; (c) Xist RNA FISH in human iPSC
  differentiation. What molecular result would confirm the XIC has been
  correctly identified?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{23}
\tightlist
\item
  Evaluate the genomic consequences of chromosomal rearrangements that
  bring proto-oncogenes near active enhancers (``enhancer hijacking'').
  Give two specific examples (BCL2 and IGH in follicular lymphoma; MYC
  and IGH in Burkitt lymphoma) and explain why the same translocation in
  different individuals produces the same cancer phenotype.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{24}
\tightlist
\item
  The genetic and epigenetic mechanisms of centromere identity are
  distinct from those of euchromatin. Evaluate: (a) why centromeres
  require CENP-A (not canonical H3) for proper kinetochore assembly; (b)
  why centromere sequences are highly repetitive (\texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\alpha}}{alpha}-satellite) despite
  being functionally defined by CENP-A deposition; (c) what would happen
  to chromosome segregation if CENP-A deposition were globally
  abolished.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{25}
\tightlist
\item
  Position effects in Drosophila (position effect variegation, PEV)
  occur when a gene is relocated near heterochromatin via chromosomal
  inversion, causing mosaic silencing. Evaluate the molecular basis of
  heterochromatic silencing spreading (HP1-H3K9me3 loop), what
  suppresses PEV (loss of heterochromatin factors), and how this relates
  to genes at the chromosome 16p11.2 deletion locus in autism.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{26}
\tightlist
\item
  Evaluate the selective sweep as an evolutionary force producing
  chromosomal linkage disequilibrium (LD). When a beneficial mutation
  sweeps to fixation, flanking variants are dragged along (``genetic
  hitchhiking''), producing extended LD. How is extended LD detected
  (iHS statistic), and what gene regions in the human genome show
  evidence of recent selective sweeps?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{27}
\tightlist
\item
  Chromosome conformation capture (3C/4C/HiC) reveals that chromosomes
  occupy specific territories in the nucleus and that A (active) and B
  (inactive) compartments are spatially separated. Evaluate how
  compartment identity is maintained through cell division (given that
  nuclear organisation must be re-established after mitosis), and what
  proteins mark the A vs B compartment boundaries.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{28}
\tightlist
\item
  Meiotic drive (non-Mendelian segregation) is a selfish genetic element
  that biases its own transmission into gametes at \textgreater50\%
  frequency. Evaluate the molecular mechanisms of drive (t-allele in
  mice, SD system in \emph{Drosophila}) and the population genetic
  consequences: under what conditions does a driving allele reach
  fixation vs form a stable polymorphism? What restricts drive from
  eliminating the drive-suppressor population?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{29}
\tightlist
\item
  Critically evaluate the concept of ``chromosomal instability'' (CIN)
  in cancer, where cells gain and lose whole chromosomes or large
  chromosome arms with each division. Is CIN a cause or consequence of
  cancer? Evaluate the evidence that CIN generates the aneuploidy needed
  for tumour evolution vs the evidence that CIN is incompatible with
  cell viability and is therefore tolerated primarily within a narrow
  window of ``just right'' instability.
\end{enumerate}
