\subsection*{Questions 11--20: Application and
Analysis}\label{questions-1120-application-and-analysis-17}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Questions 11--20: Application and
Analysis}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{10}
\tightlist
\item
  A population has 500 individuals: 200 AA, 240 Aa, 60 aa. Calculate
  allele frequencies p and q. Calculate expected HWE genotype
  frequencies. Use chi-square to test if the population is in HWE.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{11}
\tightlist
\item
  After a natural disaster reduces a population from 10,000 to 100
  individuals, what are the genetic consequences? Calculate how much
  genetic variation is expected to be lost (as measured by
  heterozygosity) in one generation: H\_t = H\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{0}}{0}(1 \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{-}}{-} 1/(2N\_e)).
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{12}
\tightlist
\item
  In a population of N\_e = 50 individuals, an allele at frequency q =
  0.2 is selectively neutral. Calculate the probability it is lost by
  drift in the first generation (approximate using 1 \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{-}}{-} q = 0.8). Over
  many generations, what is the probability it eventually reaches
  fixation (= q\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{0}}{0})?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{13}
\tightlist
\item
  Selection against a recessive allele (s = 1, lethal; aa dies before
  reproduction): starting from q\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{0}}{0} = 0.5, calculate the allele frequency
  after 1, 5, and 10 generations using q\_t = q\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{0}}{0}/(1 + t\texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\cdot}}{.}s\texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\cdot}}{.}q\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{0}}{0}). How many
  generations to reduce q from 0.5 to 0.01?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{14}
\tightlist
\item
  Cystic fibrosis has a frequency of 1/2,500 in European populations.
  Calculate: (a) q (frequency of CF allele); (b) the carrier frequency
  (2pq); (c) what Hardy-Weinberg assumption must hold for this
  calculation to be valid; (d) why the CF allele is maintained at
  relatively high frequency (propose two hypotheses).
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{15}
\tightlist
\item
  Fst between two populations is 0.15 for an autosomal locus. Interpret
  this: what fraction of total variation is between vs within
  populations? Calculate the estimated gene flow (Nm) using the
  approximation Fst \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\approx}}{~} 1/(1 + 4Nm).
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{16}
\tightlist
\item
  A bottleneck reduces a population to 10 individuals for one
  generation, then expands. If initial heterozygosity was 0.6, calculate
  expected heterozygosity after the bottleneck (H = H\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{0}}{0}(1 \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{-}}{-}
  1/(2N\_bottleneck))). After 10 generations of recovery with large N,
  how does heterozygosity change?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{17}
\tightlist
\item
  The neutral theory predicts that the rate of neutral molecular
  evolution equals the mutation rate (\texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\mu}}{mu}), independent of population
  size. Explain the logic: if advantageous mutations are rare and
  deleterious mutations are removed by selection, then substitutions in
  the fossil record should primarily reflect neutral changes. What types
  of sequences evolve fastest (synonymous sites) and slowest (amino
  acid-changing in essential proteins)?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{18}
\tightlist
\item
  Balancing selection maintains two or more alleles at a locus above
  neutral expectations. Name three types of balancing selection and one
  example of each: (a) heterozygote advantage; (b) frequency-dependent
  selection; (c) fluctuating selection (spatially or temporally
  varying). Which type is operative at MHC loci?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{19}
\tightlist
\item
  Sexual selection is a form of natural selection acting on mating
  success rather than survival. Distinguish intrasexual selection
  (competition between same-sex individuals) from intersexual selection
  (mate choice). Give one example of each in animals. How might sexual
  selection drive the rapid evolution of secondary sexual
  characteristics even if they reduce survival (Zahavian handicap
  model)?
\end{enumerate}

\subsection*{Questions 21--30: Synthesis and
Evaluation}\label{questions-2130-synthesis-and-evaluation-17}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Questions 21--30: Synthesis and
Evaluation}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{20}
\tightlist
\item
  Evaluate the molecular clock hypothesis: if the neutral substitution
  rate equals \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\mu}}{mu} (the mutation rate), then the number of differences
  between sequences accumulates linearly with time. What calibrates the
  molecular clock (fossil dates), how has the clock been used to date
  the human-chimpanzee split, and what are the sources of rate variation
  (generation time, effective population size, repair efficiency) that
  make the clock ``sloppy''?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{21}
\tightlist
\item
  The 1000 Genomes Project revealed that most human genetic variants are
  rare (minor allele frequency \textless{} 1\%). Evaluate what the site
  frequency spectrum (SFS) of human variants tells us about recent
  population expansion (bottleneck \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} colonisation of new territories \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
  rapid expansion), and how deviations from neutral SFS predictions
  (Tajima's D) detect selection.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{22}
\tightlist
\item
  Evaluate the evidence that human populations show significantly
  different allele frequencies at loci controlling pigmentation (MC1R,
  SLC24A5, HERC2/OCA2) and that these differences reflect recent local
  adaptation (UV radiation, vitamin D synthesis) rather than random
  drift. What evolutionary mechanism drove rapid adaptation at these
  loci in the past 10,000--20,000 years?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{23}
\tightlist
\item
  Design an analysis to identify signatures of selection in a
  genome-wide SNP dataset from 1,000 individuals in two populations.
  Describe the following statistical tests you would use: Fst outlier
  analysis, XP-EHH (cross-population extended haplotype homozygosity),
  and Tajima's D, stating what each detects. What results would indicate
  recent selective sweeps, and how would you validate a candidate gene
  using functional data?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{24}
\tightlist
\item
  Evaluate ``negative frequency-dependent selection'' at the ABO blood
  group locus. Propose why O (producing no antigen) remains at
  \textgreater60\% frequency in many human populations despite the
  disadvantage of lacking most antigens (O individuals cannot receive A,
  B, or AB blood). What pathogens preferentially target specific blood
  group antigens, and how does this drive balancing selection?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{25}
\tightlist
\item
  Effective population size (N\_e) in humans is estimated at
  about 10,000--20,000 (from genetic diversity), far smaller
  than the current census population (about 8 billion).
  Evaluate three reasons why N\_e \textless\textless{} N\_c: (a) highly
  unequal reproductive success; (b) past bottlenecks; (c) sex ratio
  inequality. How does a small historical N\_e affect our genome (e.g.,
  low heterozygosity, linkage disequilibrium)?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{26}
\tightlist
\item
  Genetic load is the reduction in population fitness due to deleterious
  alleles. Evaluate the ``mutation load paradox'' in humans: each human
  carries about 70--100 de novo mutations per generation, yet
  the population continues to grow. How is deleterious load purged by
  selection (purifying selection), and what analytical framework
  (fitness decline per mutation, calculated from GWAS) resolves the
  paradox?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{27}
\tightlist
\item
  Evaluate the role of sexual reproduction vs asexual reproduction in
  maintaining genetic variation under selection. The Red Queen
  hypothesis proposes that sexual reproduction is advantageous because
  it generates novel combinations to keep pace with rapidly evolving
  parasites. Evaluate: (a) the ecological evidence (host-parasite
  coevolution in snails, \emph{Potamopyrgus antipodarum}); (b) the
  genetic evidence (rate of Muller's ratchet in asexual vs sexual
  populations); (c) the cost of sex (only about 50\% of offspring bear
  offspring themselves).
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{28}
\tightlist
\item
  Population stratification in GWAS occurs when ancestry-related allele
  frequency differences confound disease-association signals. Evaluate
  how principal component analysis (PCA) corrects for stratification in
  GWAS, why failing to correct can generate spurious associations, and
  why the same caution applies to forensic or outbreak
  population-inference claims.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{29}
\tightlist
\item
  Critically evaluate the ``mutation-selection-drift'' balance framework
  as a complete explanation for the maintenance of genetic variation in
  natural populations. Where does this framework work well (e.g., for
  clearly deleterious alleles), and where does it break down (complex
  traits with many loci of small effect, phenotypic plasticity,
  developmental canalization, environmental gene \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\times}}{x} environment
  interactions)? Propose how the modern extended synthesis incorporates
  concepts beyond classical population genetics.
\end{enumerate}

\section*{Questions --- Ch 19: Evolution --- Theory, Natural Selection,
and
Adaptation}\label{questions-ch-19-evolution-theory-natural-selection-and-adaptation}

Theory, Natural Selection, and Adaptation}

\label{sec:q_unit_VI_evolution_and_selection}

\subsection*{Instructor Use and Coverage
Notes}\label{instructor-use-and-coverage-notes-21}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Instructor Use and Coverage Notes}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{Coverage target:} Estimate selection strength from data and
  explain why the result is context dependent.
\item
  \textbf{Model/data emphasis:} Selection coefficient and
  allele-frequency trajectory calculations.
\item
  \textbf{Assessment alignment:} Visual Representations, Statistical
  Tests and Data Analysis, Argumentation.
\item
  \textbf{Misconception probe:} Evolution is not goal-directed progress;
  it is local change in populations under constraints.
\item
  \textbf{Transfer product:} Transfer selection reasoning to
  antibiotics, pesticide resistance, cancer, or climate adaptation.
\item
  \textbf{Grading focus:} award full credit for mechanism, evidence,
  boundary conditions, and units when a calculation is required.
\item
  \textbf{Suggested use:} draw one recall item, one application item,
  and one synthesis item when building a short quiz from this bank.

\subsection*{Questions 1--10: Recall and
Comprehension}\label{questions-110-recall-and-comprehension-18}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Questions 1--10: Recall and
Comprehension}

\emph{This activity accompanies
\cref{sec:unit_VI_evolution_and_selection} of the textbook --- review
that chapter before attempting the exercises below.}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  State Darwin's mechanism of natural selection in four steps.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{1}
\tightlist
\item
  What is fitness in evolutionary biology? Does it relate to physical
  strength?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{2}
\tightlist
\item
  Define adaptation. Give one structural, one physiological, and one
  behavioural example.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{3}
\tightlist
\item
  What is directional selection? What is stabilising selection? Give one
  example of each.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{4}
\tightlist
\item
  What is the difference between microevolution and macroevolution?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{5}
\tightlist
\item
  Name four lines of evidence for evolution by natural selection.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{6}
\tightlist
\item
  What is the fossil record? What is a transitional fossil? Give one
  example.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{7}
\tightlist
\item
  What is homology? Distinguish structural homology from molecular
  homology.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{8}
\tightlist
\item
  What are vestigial structures? Give two examples in humans.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{9}
\tightlist
\item
  What is convergent evolution? Give one example.
\end{enumerate}

\subsection*{Questions 11--20: Application and
Analysis}\label{questions-1120-application-and-analysis-18}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Questions 11--20: Application and
Analysis}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{10}
\tightlist
\item
  Rock pocket mice in New Mexico exist on both dark lava and light soil
  habitats. Mice with dark coats survive better on lava; light mice
  survive better on soil. Explain: (a) the type of selection
  (disruptive); (b) the molecular basis of dark coat colour (MC1R
  mutations); (c) what the independent evolution of dark coats in
  different geographic populations tells us about convergent evolution.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{11}
\tightlist
\item
  The industrial melanism of the peppered moth (\emph{Biston betularia})
  is a textbook example of directional selection. Calculate: if initial
  light morph frequency = 0.99 and dark morph = 0.01, and selection
  coefficient against light morph = 0.33 (on industrial trees), after 50
  years (50 generations), predict the approximate frequency of the dark
  morph using the directional selection equation.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{12}
\tightlist
\item
  Sexual selection can drive traits to fixation even when they reduce
  survival (peacock tail). Use the Zahavian handicap principle to
  explain: (a) why primarily males with good ``condition'' can afford to
  develop large ornaments; (b) how female preference for ornaments
  evolves (Fisherian runaway vs good genes models); (c) evidence
  distinguishing the two models.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{13}
\tightlist
\item
  Kin selection allows altruistic behaviour to evolve when altruism
  benefits genetic relatives. Apply Hamilton's rule: altruism evolves
  when rb \textgreater{} c (r = relatedness, b = benefit, c = cost). A
  worker honey bee (r = 0.75 to sisters) helps raise 10 sisters (b = 10)
  at the cost of 0 own offspring (due to sterility). Is altruism
  favoured? What would rB need to be to just exceed c = 3.0?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{14}
\tightlist
\item
  Selection on quantitative traits can be modelled by the breeder's
  equation: R = h\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{2}}{2}S (R = response to selection, h\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{2}}{2} = heritability, S =
  selection differential). If height heritability is 0.80 and we select
  parents who are 5 cm taller than the population mean, predict R. How
  many generations of selection would be needed to shift mean height by
  10 cm?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{15}
\tightlist
\item
  Gould and Lewontin's ``spandrel'' argument suggests that not most
  traits are adaptations --- some are architectural by-products of other
  adaptations (spandrels in the context of evolutionary biology). Give
  two specific biological examples of putative spandrels and evaluate
  the methodological criteria needed to distinguish a spandrel from an
  adaptation.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{16}
\tightlist
\item
  Antibiotic resistance evolution offers real-time evidence of natural
  selection. Describe the Lenski long-term evolution experiment with
  \emph{E. coli} (\textgreater75,000 generations). What phenotypic
  innovations have evolved, and how does the experiment distinguish
  ``chance'' events from adaptive improvement?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{17}
\tightlist
\item
  Coevolution occurs when two species reciprocally affect each other's
  evolution. Describe the Red Queen model of host-parasite coevolution:
  (a) why does the host need to evolve continuously; (b) what does the
  snail (\emph{Potamopyrgus antipodarum}) -- trematode parasite system
  teach us; (c) what arms race dynamics emerge between plant alkaloids
  and insect detoxification enzymes?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{18}
\tightlist
\item
  Punctuated equilibrium (Gould and Eldredge, 1972) argues that most
  evolutionary change is concentrated in rapid bursts associated with
  speciation, not in gradual anagenesis. Evaluate the fossil evidence
  for and against punctuated equilibrium using the Cerion land snail
  data from the Bahamas and the evolution of horse lineages.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{19}
\tightlist
\item
  Biogeography provides evidence for evolution: organisms on islands
  often resemble those on the nearest mainland but have evolved unique
  adaptations. Apply the concept of adaptive radiation to Hawaiian
  honeycreepers (about 50 species from one ancestral finch-like
  coloniser): which resources were exploited by different lineages, and
  what ecological opportunity allowed such rapid diversification?
\end{enumerate}

\subsection*{Questions 21--30: Synthesis and
Evaluation}\label{questions-2130-synthesis-and-evaluation-18}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Questions 21--30: Synthesis and
Evaluation}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{20}
\tightlist
\item
  Evaluate the extended evolutionary synthesis (EES) relative to the
  modern synthesis. Which additional mechanisms does EES incorporate
  (developmental plasticity, epigenetic inheritance, niche construction,
  evolvability)? Choose one mechanism and evaluate the evidence that it
  plays a role comparable in importance to natural selection in at least
  one biological system.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{21}
\tightlist
\item
  Design an experiment to test the ``good genes'' hypothesis for female
  preference in peacocks (\emph{Pavo cristatus}). Describe: the relevant
  measurements (eyespot count, parasite load, extra-pair offspring
  survival), statistical analyses needed, and a falsification criterion.
  What result would confirm vs reject the hypothesis?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{22}
\tightlist
\item
  Evaluate the evolutionary arms race between cuckoos and their hosts
  (\emph{Cuculus canorus} vs reed warblers). Describe: (a) forgery (egg
  mimicry); (b) host counter-adaptations (pattern recognition, egg
  ejection); (c) what would have to happen for the host to ``win'' and
  cuckoos to go extinct. What does the coevolutionary balance tell us
  about the role of Red Queen dynamics in parasite-host coevolution?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{23}
\tightlist
\item
  Molecular convergence (independent evolution of the same molecular
  change in different lineages) provides the strongest evidence for
  adaptation at the sequence level. Evaluate three examples: (a) same
  amino acid substitution in haemoglobin for high-altitude adaptation in
  birds; (b) convergent microbial drug resistance mutations; (c)
  convergent VLDLR mutations for flight in birds. What does molecular
  convergence tell us about the size of genotypic variation space
  accessible by natural selection?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{24}
\tightlist
\item
  The ``fitness landscape'' model represents most possible genotypes as
  a surface where height corresponds to fitness. Evaluate the
  limitations of this model for understanding: (a) epistasis
  (non-additive interactions between loci); (b) adaptive valleys (can
  evolution cross fitness valleys?); (c) frequency-dependent fitness
  (landscape changes with allele frequency). Propose an alternative
  model that addresses these limitations.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{25}
\tightlist
\item
  Group selection (selection acting on groups rather than individuals)
  was largely dismissed after Williams (1966), but has been revived as
  multilevel selection (MLS) theory. Evaluate: (a) the conditions under
  which group selection overrides individual selection; (b) the evidence
  from slime mould (\emph{Dictyostelium}) cooperation; (c) whether human
  cooperation can be explained by MLS or requires cultural group
  selection.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{26}
\tightlist
\item
  Evaluate the claim that evolutionary theory is a scientific fact while
  specific evolutionary narratives (the origin of feathers, the
  evolution of eukaryotes) are provisional hypotheses. What does
  ``theory'' mean in science compared to colloquial usage? How does the
  misunderstanding of ``theory'' fuel creationist objections, and what
  is the appropriate scientific response?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{27}
\tightlist
\item
  Evolvability --- the capacity to evolve --- may itself be a product of
  natural selection. Evaluate: (a) the evidence that the modular
  architecture of proteins (protein domains) evolved to enhance
  evolvability; (b) whether mutation rate itself can be subject to
  natural selection; (c) the concept of robustness (canalization) and
  its relationship to evolvability.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{28}
\tightlist
\item
  The ``major evolutionary transitions'' (Szathmáry and Maynard Smith,
  1995) describe eight key events in the history of life (e.g., origin
  of the eukaryotic cell, origin of multicellularity). Evaluate what
  distinguishes each transition from ordinary speciation, and propose
  what the next major evolutionary transition might be (e.g., a digital
  information-based evolving system?).
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{29}
\tightlist
\item
  Critically evaluate whether evolutionary theory can be directly
  applied to artificial systems (machine learning algorithms, memes,
  cultural evolution). What structural features must any system have to
  undergo Darwinian evolution (heritable variation, differential
  reproduction, competition)? Does cultural evolution satisfy these
  criteria, and how does it differ from biological evolution in terms of
  inheritance mechanisms and selection units?
\end{enumerate}

\subsection*{Questions 1--10: Recall and
Comprehension}\label{questions-110-recall-and-comprehension-19}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Questions 1--10: Recall and
Comprehension}

\emph{This activity accompanies
\cref{sec:unit_VI_genetic_drift_and_speciation} of the textbook ---
review that chapter before attempting the exercises below.}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  Define genetic drift. How does it differ from natural selection?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{1}
\tightlist
\item
  What is the founder effect? What is the bottleneck effect? How do they
  differ?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{2}
\tightlist
\item
  Define gene flow. What effect does gene flow have on genetic
  differentiation between populations?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{3}
\tightlist
\item
  Define biological species concept (BSC). What is a reproductive
  isolation barrier?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{4}
\tightlist
\item
  Distinguish pre-zygotic from post-zygotic reproductive isolation
  barriers. Give two examples of each.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{5}
\tightlist
\item
  What is allopatric speciation? What is sympatric speciation? Give one
  natural example of each.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{6}
\tightlist
\item
  What is parapatric speciation? Give one example from plant
  populations.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{7}
\tightlist
\item
  Define peripatric speciation. How does it relate to the founder
  effect?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{8}
\tightlist
\item
  Define Fst (fixation index). What does Fst = 0 mean? What does Fst = 1
  mean?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{9}
\tightlist
\item
  What is adaptive radiation? Give one famous example.
\end{enumerate}

\subsection*{Questions 11--20: Application and
Analysis}\label{questions-1120-application-and-analysis-19}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Questions 11--20: Application and
Analysis}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{10}
\tightlist
\item
  A population of 1,000 individuals is reduced to 5 for three
  generations, then recovers to 1,000. Calculate the harmonic mean of
  the effective population size over the three-generation bottleneck,
  and use H\_t = H\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{0}}{0}(1 \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{-}}{-} 1/(2N\_e))\^{}t to estimate the heterozygosity
  remaining after recovery.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{11}
\tightlist
\item
  The Amish population (descended from 200 founders in the 1700s) has a
  1,000-fold higher frequency of Ellis-van Creveld syndrome (short-limb
  dwarfism) than the general population. Explain: (a) which mechanism is
  responsible; (b) whether natural selection for or against the
  condition is required to explain its frequency; (c) what this implies
  for genetic counselling in this community.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{12}
\tightlist
\item
  Two sister populations of fish separated 10,000 years ago are now
  parapatrically distributed along a river system. They differ in colour
  pattern and mating call. When brought together in the lab, they
  hybridise successfully but hybrids show reduced fertility. Classify:
  (a) what type of speciation occurred; (b) what type of reproductive
  isolation is demonstrated; (c) whether they are currently separate
  species under the BSC.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{13}
\tightlist
\item
  Calculate the estimated gene flow (Nm = number of migrants per
  generation) between two populations with Fst = 0.08, using Fst \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\approx}}{~} 1/(1
  + 4Nm). Is this a high or low level of gene flow? What migration rate
  (Nm \textgreater{} 1) is needed to prevent significant divergence?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{14}
\tightlist
\item
  In cichlid fish adaptive radiation in Lake Victoria, \textgreater{}
  500 species evolved in \textless{} 15,000 years --- an extremely rapid
  speciation event. Propose: (a) what ecological opportunity promoted
  rapid radiation; (b) what role mate choice based on colour pattern
  played in sympatric speciation; (c) how light transmission in
  different lake depths may have driven divergence.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{15}
\tightlist
\item
  Ring species provide a spatial illustration of the speciation
  continuum. The Larus gull chain circles the Arctic: populations A
  interbreed with B, B with C, C with D, D with E, but A and E do not
  interbreed. Explain: (a) why A and E are or are not separate species
  under BSC; (b) what this shows about speciation as a gradual,
  continuous process; (c) how climate change and habitat connectivity
  changes could affect this ring.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{16}
\tightlist
\item
  Hybridisation between species can produce evolutionary novelty.
  Allopolyploidy (hybrid + chromosome doubling) has produced many crop
  species: bread wheat (AABBDD, from three diploid ancestors). Explain:
  (a) how polyploidy immediately produces reproductive isolation from
  both ancestors; (b) why polyploid plants are often phenotypically
  superior (hybrid vigour/heterosis); (c) what the estimated
  contribution of allopolyploidy to flowering plant diversity is.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{17}
\tightlist
\item
  ``Magic traits'' are traits that simultaneously cause both ecological
  divergence (adaptation to different niches) and assortative mating
  (non-random mating based on the same trait). Give one example of a
  magic trait and explain why this simplifies the theory of sympatric
  speciation.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{18}
\tightlist
\item
  The biological species concept has been criticised as inapplicable to:
  (a) asexual organisms; (b) freely hybridising plant species. Evaluate
  two alternative species concepts (phylogenetic species concept,
  ecological species concept) and explain which is most useful for
  biodiversity conservation.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{19}
\tightlist
\item
  Hybrid zones are regions where two distinct populations interbreed.
  Using the tension zone model: (a) explain why a hybrid zone maintains
  a stable width; (b) what happens to hybrid fitness at the centre of
  the zone; (c) how hybrid zone data can estimate the selection against
  hybrids and the rate of gene flow.
\end{enumerate}

\subsection*{Questions 21--30: Synthesis and
Evaluation}\label{questions-2130-synthesis-and-evaluation-19}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Questions 21--30: Synthesis and
Evaluation}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{20}
\tightlist
\item
  Evaluate the evidence that speciation can occur without geographic
  separation (sympatric speciation) using the apple maggot fly
  (\emph{Rhagoletis pomonella}) host-race formation as a case study.
  What conditions (assortative mating by habitat, additive gene effects,
  limited gene flow) are required, and what genetic evidence suggests
  incipient sympatric speciation is occurring?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{21}
\tightlist
\item
  Design a population genomics study to determine whether two
  morphologically distinct bird populations on isolated islands should
  be classified as separate species. Describe: the genomic data you
  would collect (RAD-seq or whole-genome resequencing), the analyses you
  would perform (Fst, phylogeny, ABBA-BABA test for gene flow), and the
  threshold values you would use to make the classification decision.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{22}
\tightlist
\item
  Evaluate the ``glacial refugia'' hypothesis for European biodiversity:
  during Pleistocene glaciations, populations were isolated in southern
  refugia (Iberia, Italy, Balkans), underwent allopatric evolution, then
  expanded northward after glaciers retreated. What phylogeographic data
  would test this hypothesis, and what consequences does secondary
  contact of previously isolated populations have for hybrid zone
  formation?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{23}
\tightlist
\item
  Gene drive technology (e.g., CRISPR-based homing drives) can spread a
  gene (e.g., infertility) through a wild population at rates faster
  than Mendelian inheritance. Evaluate the ecological risks of releasing
  a gene drive into a wild mosquito population to suppress malaria
  transmission: (a) off-target spread to non-target species; (b)
  irreversibility; (c) international governance challenges (the drive
  does not respect national borders).
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{24}
\tightlist
\item
  Inbreeding depression (reduced fitness in highly homozygous
  individuals) limits the viability of small, isolated populations.
  Evaluate: (a) the mechanisms of inbreeding depression (overdominance
  vs partial dominance of deleterious recessives); (b) the threshold
  F\_cr (critical inbreeding coefficient) below which genetic rescue is
  needed; (c) policy implications for reintroduction of individuals from
  genetically distinct populations.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{25}
\tightlist
\item
  The concept of ``reproductive character displacement'' predicts that
  the signal used for mate recognition must diverge faster between
  sympatric sister species than between allopatric ones, to prevent
  costly hybridisation. Evaluate the evidence for reproductive character
  displacement in: (a) \emph{Ficedula} flycatchers in Scandinavia; (b)
  cricket frog calling frequencies; (c) \emph{Phlox drummondii} flower
  colour contrast.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{26}
\tightlist
\item
  Evaluate the genomics of speciation: ``genomic islands of divergence''
  are regions of elevated Fst interspersed with regions of low Fst in
  partially reproductively isolated populations. Interpret these
  patterns: do islands represent targets of selection, or artefacts of
  reduced recombination around centromeres? What sequencing/analysis
  strategy would distinguish selective sweeps from reduced recombination
  as drivers of Fst peaks?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{27}
\tightlist
\item
  Evaluate the concept of the ``speciation continuum'': from partially
  isolated populations (e.g., Fst = 0.1) through incipient species
  (partial reproductive isolation, fertile hybrids) to full species
  (complete reproductive isolation). At what point on this continuum
  should conservation efforts classify distinct evolutionary significant
  units (ESUs) for legal protection?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{28}
\tightlist
\item
  Mass extinction events (e.g., end-Cretaceous, 66 Mya) dramatically
  restructured biodiversity. Evaluate: (a) what evolutionary patterns
  characterise the burst of diversification after mass extinction
  (adaptive radiation); (b) whether the sixth mass extinction (current
  human-driven biodiversity crisis) is comparable in rate to previous
  ones; (c) whether survivors of previous extinctions provide models for
  predicting which present-day species will persist.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{29}
\tightlist
\item
  Critically evaluate the ``two-speed genome'' concept in fungi
  (\emph{Zymoseptoria tritici}, wheat pathogen): the genome is divided
  into ``core'' (gene-rich, slowly evolving) and ``accessory''
  (transposon-rich, rapidly evolving) chromosomes. How does this
  architecture accelerate host-pathogen coevolution, and how might it
  apply to our understanding of evolutionary rate variation in other
  organisms, including humans (conserved regions vs rapidly evolving
  regions)?
\end{enumerate}

\section*{Questions --- Ch 21: Phylogenetics and the Tree of
Life}\label{questions-ch-21-phylogenetics-and-the-tree-of-life}
\addcontentsline{toc}{section}{Questions --- Ch 21: Phylogenetics and
the Tree of Life}

\label{sec:q_unit_VI_phylogenetics}

\subsection*{Instructor Use and Coverage
Notes}\label{instructor-use-and-coverage-notes-23}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Instructor Use and Coverage Notes}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{Coverage target:} Use a tree to infer shared ancestry,
  character transitions, or divergence time.
\item
  \textbf{Model/data emphasis:} Tree-distance, parsimony, and
  molecular-clock calculations.
\item
  \textbf{Assessment alignment:} Visual Representations, Statistical
  Tests and Data Analysis, Argumentation.
\item
  \textbf{Misconception probe:} Living species are cousins, not
  ancestors of one another.
\item
  \textbf{Transfer product:} Transfer tree thinking to pathogens,
  conservation units, gene families, and development.
\item
  \textbf{Grading focus:} award full credit for mechanism, evidence,
  boundary conditions, and units when a calculation is required.
\item
  \textbf{Suggested use:} draw one recall item, one application item,
  and one synthesis item when building a short quiz from this bank.
\end{itemize}

\subsection*{Questions 1--10: Recall and
Comprehension}\label{questions-110-recall-and-comprehension-20}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Questions 1--10: Recall and
Comprehension}

\emph{This activity accompanies \cref{sec:unit_VI_phylogenetics} of the
textbook --- review that chapter before attempting the exercises below.}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  What is a phylogenetic tree? What does each node, branch, and tip
  represent?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{1}
\tightlist
\item
  What is a clade (monophyletic group)? Distinguish monophyletic,
  paraphyletic, and polyphyletic groups.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{2}
\tightlist
\item
  Define synapomorphy. How does it differ from a plesiomorphy?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{3}
\tightlist
\item
  What is parsimony in phylogenetics? What does the most parsimonious
  tree minimise?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{4}
\tightlist
\item
  What is a molecular phylogeny? What type of data is used to construct
  one?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{5}
\tightlist
\item
  What is a bootstrap value? What does a bootstrap of 90\% indicate?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{6}
\tightlist
\item
  What is an outgroup? How is it used to root a phylogenetic tree?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{7}
\tightlist
\item
  What is horizontal gene transfer (HGT)? In which domains of life is it
  most common?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{8}
\tightlist
\item
  Define convergent evolution. How can it mislead phylogenetic analysis?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{9}
\tightlist
\item
  What are molecular clocks? How are they calibrated?
\end{enumerate}

\subsection*{Questions 11--20: Application and
Analysis}\label{questions-1120-application-and-analysis-20}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Questions 11--20: Application and
Analysis}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{10}
\tightlist
\item
  Given the character matrix below (1=present, 0=absent): determine the
  synapomorphies that define the clade (birds + crocodiles) relative to
  lizards and snakes, using the parsimony principle.
\end{enumerate}

{\def\LTcaptype{none} % do not increment counter
\begin{longtable}[]{@{}lllll@{}}
\toprule\noalign{}
Taxon & Archosaur skull & Feathers & 4-chambered heart & Endothermy \\
\midrule\noalign{}
\endhead
\bottomrule\noalign{}
\endlastfoot
Lizard & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\
Crocodile & 1 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\
Bird & 1 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\
\end{longtable}
}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{11}
\tightlist
\item
  Two competing phylogenies are proposed for the Paleocene mammals: (A)
  requires 12 evolutionary changes; (B) requires 15 changes. By
  parsimony, which tree is preferred? Explain what assumption is made
  when choosing the more parsimonious tree.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{12}
\tightlist
\item
  Dolphins and ichthyosaurs (extinct reptiles) both have streamlined
  bodies and fin-like forelimbs. Explain: (a) why a morphological
  phylogeny based solely on body shape would incorrectly group them; (b)
  what more reliable character would avoid this error; (c) what type of
  evolution produced the similarity.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{13}
\tightlist
\item
  A molecular phylogeny based on 16S rRNA sequences places Archaea as a
  sister clade to Eukaryotes, while Bacteria branch more basely. Explain
  what this means for the ``three-domain of life'' vs ``two-domain of
  life'' (Eocyte hypothesis) debate.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{14}
\tightlist
\item
  The molecular clock for mitochondrial cytochrome b sequences in
  mammals ticks at about 2\% divergence per million years
  (Mya). Two sister species differ by 8\% in their cytochrome b
  sequences. Estimate when they diverged, and list two sources of
  uncertainty in this estimate.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{15}
\tightlist
\item
  ABBA-BABA (D-statistics) tests detect gene flow between populations.
  If D is significantly positive, what does it imply about the
  relationships between the four taxa (P1, P2, P3, and outgroup)? How
  did this test reveal Neanderthal--modern human gene flow?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{16}
\tightlist
\item
  Biogeographic analysis shows that the freshwater fish genus
  \emph{Nannoperca} is distributed across southwestern Australia
  (isolated from other parts by arid zones). How would you distinguish
  between: (a) vicariance (ancient populations separated by geological
  changes); (b) long-distance dispersal (a single colonisation event
  across an unsuitable barrier)?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{17}
\tightlist
\item
  Maximum likelihood (ML) phylogenetics uses an explicit model of
  sequence evolution (e.g., GTR+\texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\Gamma}}{Gamma}) to evaluate the likelihood of
  observing the data given a tree. Why is ML generally preferred over
  parsimony for molecular data, especially for distantly related taxa?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{18}
\tightlist
\item
  Gene trees vs species trees: individual gene trees can differ from the
  species tree due to incomplete lineage sorting (ILS) or horizontal
  gene transfer. What is ILS, and why is it more likely for genes with
  short internodal branches (rapid speciation)?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{19}
\tightlist
\item
  The ``long branch attraction'' (LBA) artefact occurs when rapidly
  evolving lineages with many changes falsely cluster together in
  parsimony or distance analysis. Explain the mechanism of LBA and
  propose two strategies to avoid it (taxon sampling, model-based
  methods).
\end{enumerate}

\subsection*{Questions 21--30: Synthesis and
Evaluation}\label{questions-2130-synthesis-and-evaluation-20}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Questions 21--30: Synthesis and
Evaluation}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{20}
\tightlist
\item
  Evaluate the evidence that Archaean clade Asgard is the closest
  prokaryotic relative of eukaryotes. What specific eukaryotic features
  (endomembrane, cytoskeleton homologues, ubiquitin) were identified in
  their genomes? What does this suggest about the origin of eukaryotic
  complexity?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{21}
\tightlist
\item
  Design a phylogenomic study (using hundreds of genes rather than one
  marker) to resolve a ``soft polytomy'' (unresolved node) in the avian
  tree of life. Describe: coalescent methods (ASTRAL) vs concatenation
  (ML on combined alignment), what sources of conflict between gene
  trees need to be accounted for, and how you would determine whether
  the polytomy reflects rapid radiation rather than incomplete data.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{22}
\tightlist
\item
  The ribosomal RNA (rRNA) phylogeny (Woese, 1977) unified most life
  into three domains. Evaluate why rRNA was chosen as a comprehensive
  phylogenetic marker: (a) ubiquitous, almost universally homologous;
  (b) highly conserved but containing variable regions; (c) unlikely to
  undergo HGT. Are there limitations to rRNA as a ``true'' species tree
  marker?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{23}
\tightlist
\item
  Bayesian phylogenetics (MrBayes, BEAST) uses prior probabilities and
  MCMC sampling to estimate the posterior distribution of trees. Compare
  Bayesian vs maximum likelihood approaches: (a) what is the difference
  in interpretation of the ``support'' values (posterior probabilities
  vs bootstrap); (b) when does Bayesian inference provide overconfident
  node support; (c) how is divergence time estimation performed in
  BEAST?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{24}
\tightlist
\item
  Ancient DNA (aDNA) sequencing has transformed our understanding of
  human history by adding extinct hominin and historical populations to
  phylogenies. Evaluate the technical challenges of aDNA analysis: (a)
  DNA degradation (short fragments, C\texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}U deamination); (b) contamination
  from environmental microbes and modern human DNA; (c) how mapDamage
  software and UDG treatment are used to address these.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{25}
\tightlist
\item
  Evaluate the ``bush of life'' metaphor vs the traditional ``tree of
  life'' for describing microbial evolution. How prevalent is HGT among
  bacteria and archaea (what fraction of the typical prokaryote genome
  has been acquired by HGT), and at what level (genus, family, phylum)
  does HGT obscure true vertical inheritance?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{26}
\tightlist
\item
  TransposableElements have been used as phylogenetic markers
  (SINEs/LINEs as synapomorphies): a SINE insertion shared by multiple
  taxa must have occurred once in a common ancestor. Evaluate the
  advantages of transposon-based markers over sequence-based
  phylogenetics: (a) irreversibility of insertion; (b) independence of
  molecular evolution model assumptions; (c) limitations (element
  excision, parallel insertions in hotspot regions).
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{27}
\tightlist
\item
  The ``total evidence dating'' approach (tip calibration) uses
  morphological characters from fossils as direct terminal taxa (not
  just calibration points) in Bayesian time-tree analysis. Evaluate the
  advantages of total evidence dating over node calibration, and
  describe what happens to morphological branch length estimates when
  the model of trait evolution (e.g., Mk model) is misspecified.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{28}
\tightlist
\item
  Horizontal gene transfer in cancer (somatic HGT from tumour
  microenvironment bacteria into human cells) has been reported but
  remains controversial. Evaluate the evidence: (a) what sequencing
  artefacts can mimic bacterial HGT; (b) what controls are needed to
  rule out contamination; (c) if real, what functional consequences
  might cancer-incorporated bacterial genes have?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{29}
\tightlist
\item
  Critically assess whether a ``tree of life'' can be reconstructed from
  extant biodiversity alone, without fossil calibration. What
  information is intrinsically lost when primarily the tips (extant
  species) and not the internal nodes (extinct ancestors) are known? Use
  the concept of incomplete ancestry and the ``big-bang'' topology
  problem of rapid early diversification as a specific example.
\end{enumerate}

\newpage

\section*{Questions --- Ch 22: Bacteria, Archaea, and
Viruses}\label{questions-ch-22-bacteria-archaea-and-viruses}
\addcontentsline{toc}{section}{Questions --- Ch 22: Bacteria, Archaea,
and Viruses}

\label{sec:q_unit_VII_bacteria_archaea_viruses}

\subsection*{Instructor Use and Coverage
Notes}\label{instructor-use-and-coverage-notes-24}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Instructor Use and Coverage Notes}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{Coverage target:} Classify a microbe or virus from evidence
  and predict a likely vulnerability.
\item
  \textbf{Model/data emphasis:} Growth-rate, genome-size, and dilution
  calculations.
\item
  \textbf{Assessment alignment:} Questions and Methods, Representing and
  Describing Data, Argumentation.
\item
  \textbf{Misconception probe:} Viruses are not simply tiny bacteria;
  they use fundamentally different replication logic.
\item
  \textbf{Transfer product:} Apply microbial diversity reasoning to
  antibiotics, biotechnology, ecology, and outbreaks.
\item
  \textbf{Grading focus:} award full credit for mechanism, evidence,
  boundary conditions, and units when a calculation is required.
\item
  \textbf{Suggested use:} draw one recall item, one application item,
  and one synthesis item when building a short quiz from this bank.
\end{itemize}

\subsection*{Questions 1--10: Recall and
Comprehension}\label{questions-110-recall-and-comprehension-21}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Questions 1--10: Recall and
Comprehension}

\emph{This activity accompanies
\cref{sec:unit_VII_bacteria_archaea_viruses} of the textbook --- review
that chapter before attempting the exercises below.}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  List three differences between bacteria and archaea in cell wall
  chemistry and membrane lipids.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{1}
\tightlist
\item
  What is the Gram stain? What does Gram-positive vs Gram-negative
  indicate about cell wall structure?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{2}
\tightlist
\item
  Describe the replication cycle of a bacteriophage. Distinguish lytic
  from lysogenic cycles.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{3}
\tightlist
\item
  What is a prophage? What signal triggers induction of the lytic cycle
  from lysogeny?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{4}
\tightlist
\item
  Name three types of bacterial reproduction. Which is the fastest?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{5}
\tightlist
\item
  What is binary fission? How does the doubling time relate to bacterial
  growth rate?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{6}
\tightlist
\item
  Describe the structure of a typical bacterium: nucleoid, ribosomes,
  pili, flagella, capsule.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{7}
\tightlist
\item
  What is conjugation? What is an F plasmid?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{8}
\tightlist
\item
  Distinguish DNA viruses from RNA viruses. Give one example of each.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{9}
\tightlist

  What is a retrovirus? Describe its replication cycle.
\end{enumerate}

\subsection*{Questions 11--20: Application and
Analysis}\label{questions-1120-application-and-analysis-21}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Questions 11--20: Application and
Analysis}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{10}
\tightlist
\item
  A bacterial culture starts with 100 cells and has a doubling time of
  20 minutes. Calculate: (a) the number of cells after 2 hours; (b) the
  approximate mass of bacteria (assuming 10\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{-}}{-}\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{1}}{1}\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{5}}{5} g/cell) after 24 hours.
  Why does exponential growth not continue indefinitely?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{11}
\tightlist
\item
  Design a serial dilution experiment to count colonies from a bacterial
  sample expected to have about 10\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{6}}{6} CFU/mL. Which dilutions
  would give countable plates (30--300 colonies)? Calculate CFU/mL from
  a plate showing 175 colonies at 10\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{-}}{-}\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{5}}{5} dilution.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{12}
\tightlist
\item
  Compare the lytic and lysogenic cycles: what are the advantages of
  each for the phage? Under what environmental/physiological conditions
  does the lambda phage switch from lysogeny to the lytic cycle? (Name
  the specific protease.)
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{13}
\tightlist
\item
  MRSA (methicillin-resistant \emph{Staphylococcus aureus}) carries
  \emph{mecA} or \emph{mecC}, encoding a modified penicillin-binding
  protein (PBP2a/PBP2c) with low affinity for most traditional \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\beta}}{beta}-lactam
  antibiotics. Explain: (a) how \emph{mec} genes are acquired by
  horizontal gene transfer on SCC\emph{mec} elements; (b) why many
  \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\beta}}{beta}-lactams fail but anti-MRSA cephalosporins can be exceptions in
  susceptible isolates; (c) what alternative antibiotics are used and
  how their mechanisms bypass PBP2a.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{14}
\tightlist
\item
  Archaea are found in extreme environments (hyperthermophiles,
  halophiles, methanogens). Explain how: (a) archaeal lipid membranes
  (isoprene ether-linked, rather than ester-linked) withstand high
  temperatures; (b) halophilic archaea stabilise proteins at high salt
  by having an excess of surface-facing acidic residues; (c)
  methanogenic archaea use H\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{2}}{2} and CO\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{2}}{2} as energy sources via a unique
  archaeal pathway.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{15}
\tightlist
\item
  The CRISPR-Cas system in bacteria provides adaptive immunity against
  phage. Explain: (a) spacer acquisition from phage DNA; (b)
  crRNA-guided Cas9 surveillance; (c) cleavage of matching invader DNA;
  (d) why the phage can evolve to escape CRISPR immunity (PAM sequence
  mutation). How did bacterial CRISPR inspire the molecular biology
  tool?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{16}
\tightlist
\item
  Viral tropism (which cells a virus can infect) depends on
  receptor-ligand binding. HIV infects cells expressing both CD4 and
  CCR5/CXCR4 (co-receptors). Individuals homozygous for a 32-bp deletion
  in \emph{CCR5} (\texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\Delta}}{Delta}32 allele) are largely resistant to HIV infection.
  Explain why this is and why CCR5 antagonists (maraviroc) alone do not
  fully cure HIV.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{17}
\tightlist
\item
  Prions are misfolded proteins (PrP\^{}Sc) that convert normally folded
  proteins (PrP\^{}C) to the pathogenic conformation. Explain: (a) why
  prion diseases (CJD, BSE) are transmissible without nucleic acid; (b)
  the proposed templating mechanism; (c) why prions are nearly extremely
  difficult to decontaminate by standard autoclaving.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{18}
\tightlist
\item
  Bacteriophage therapy (phage therapy) is being reconsidered as an
  alternative to antibiotics for drug-resistant infections. Compare
  phage therapy vs antibiotics: (a) host range (broad-spectrum
  antibiotics vs phage-host specificity); (b) resistance evolution rate;
  (c) phage ability to co-evolve with bacterial host. Give one clinical
  case report of successful phage therapy.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{19}
\tightlist
\item
  SARS-CoV-2 is a +ssRNA coronavirus. Explain: (a) how it uses its spike
  protein to bind ACE2 and enter cells; (b) why mRNA vaccines encoding
  spike protein induce protective immunity; (c) why variants (Omicron)
  with many spike mutations can partially evade vaccine-induced
  antibodies.
\end{enumerate}

\subsection*{Questions 21--30: Synthesis and
Evaluation}\label{questions-2130-synthesis-and-evaluation-21}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Questions 21--30: Synthesis and
Evaluation}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{20}
\tightlist
\item
  Evaluate the hypotheses for the origin of viruses: (a) regression
  hypothesis (viruses are degenerate cells); (b) escape hypothesis
  (mobile genetic elements that gained capsids); (c) primordial virion
  hypothesis (viruses predate cells). Which hypothesis is most
  consistent with current phylogenomic data (nucleocytoplasmic large DNA
  viruses and their relatives)?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{21}
\tightlist
\item
  Design a strategy to engineer a phage to specifically kill a
  Gram-negative ESKAPE pathogen (\emph{Klebsiella pneumoniae}) that is
  resistant to multiple first-line antibiotics and has few standard
  options. Describe: (a) the host-range engineering approach (tail fibre
  protein swapping); (b) the anti-biofilm component you would add; (c)
  the regulatory and safety evidence required before use in humans.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{22}
\tightlist
\item
  Quorum sensing in \emph{Pseudomonas aeruginosa} controls virulence
  gene expression via N-acyl-homoserine lactone (AHL) signalling (las
  and rhl systems). Evaluate: (a) how quorum sensing allows coordinated
  virulence (biofilm formation, exotoxin production) primarily at high
  cell density; (b) why quorum sensing inhibitors (QSIs) are attractive
  anti-virulence targets (less resistance selection pressure); (c) why
  QSI clinical development has stalled.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{23}
\tightlist
\item
  Evaluate the evolutionary biology of rapid viral evolution (HIV,
  influenza). HIV's high mutation rate (error-prone RT,
  about 3\texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\times}}{x}10\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{-}}{-}\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{5}}{5}/base/replication) generates enormous diversity.
  How does this diversity allow immune escape and drug resistance?
  Evaluate why combination antiretroviral therapy (ART) --- targeting
  multiple steps simultaneously --- dramatically suppresses resistance
  evolution and how ``cure'' strategies (shock and kill) aim to
  eliminate latent reservoirs.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{24}
\tightlist
\item
  Giant viruses (Mimivirus, Pandoravirus) have genomes \textgreater1 Mb
  --- larger than some bacteria --- and contain genes for
  translation-related functions unprecedented in viruses. Evaluate
  whether giant viruses blur the boundary between viruses and cells, and
  whether they support the regression hypothesis for viral origin.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{25}
\tightlist
\item
  Horizontal gene transfer (HGT) in bacteria can be transduction,
  transformation, or conjugation. Use a One Health AMR map to compare
  how an ESBL or carbapenemase gene could move among hospital patients,
  wastewater, livestock, soil microbes, and wildlife. Which transfer
  mechanism is most plausible in each setting, and what surveillance
  evidence would distinguish clonal spread from mobile-element spread?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{26}
\tightlist
\item
  The microbiome of the human gut contains \textgreater1,000 bacterial
  species that collectively perform essential metabolic functions (SCFA
  production, vitamin synthesis, immune training). Evaluate whether the
  gut microbiome should be considered an ``accessory genome'' of the
  human host, and what criteria would need to be met for this ``extended
  genome'' concept to be scientifically defensible.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{27}
\tightlist
\item
  Bacteriophage encode auxiliary metabolic genes (AMGs) --- metabolic
  genes that boost host metabolism during infection (e.g., phage-encoded
  photosynthesis genes in cyanophages). Evaluate the role of phage AMGs
  in global carbon and nitrogen cycling, and propose how phage-encoded
  metabolic capacity shapes marine primary productivity.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{28}
\tightlist
\item
  The virome --- the complete collection of viruses in an ecosystem ---
  is far larger than the known virome catalogued to date. Evaluate
  metagenomics approaches (shotgun metagenomics, viromics with CRISPR
  spacer-based enrichment) for discovering novel viruses, and assess
  what fraction of global viral diversity may remain undiscovered.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{29}
\tightlist
\item
  Critically evaluate the claim that viruses are ``the dark matter of
  the biosphere'' --- underappreciated forces shaping ecosystems, gene
  flows, and evolution. What evidence from marine phage ecology, the
  pan-genome of bacteria, and viral integration into eukaryotic genomes
  supports this claim? How does the expanding virology of the
  2010s--2020s change our understanding of life's diversity?
\end{enumerate}

\section*{Questions --- Ch 23: Microbial Ecology and the

  and interaction-network reasoning.

  \textbf{Misconception probe:} A microbiome is not automatically
  beneficial; context determines the effect.

  \textbf{Transfer product:} Transfer microbial ecology to soils,
  oceans, digestion, disease, and climate feedbacks.
\item
  \textbf{Grading focus:} award full credit for mechanism, evidence,
  boundary conditions, and units when a calculation is required.
\item
  \textbf{Suggested use:} draw one recall item, one application item,
  and one synthesis item when building a short quiz from this bank.
\end{itemize}

\subsection*{Questions 1--10: Recall and
Comprehension}\label{questions-110-recall-and-comprehension-22}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Questions 1--10: Recall and
Comprehension}

\emph{This activity accompanies \cref{sec:unit_VII_microbial_ecology} of
the textbook --- review that chapter before attempting the exercises
below.}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist

  Define the microbiome. What is the difference between microbiome and
  microbiota?

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}

\tightlist

  What is 16S rRNA sequencing? Why is the 16S gene used to classify
  bacteria?

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}

  Define the Shannon diversity index. What does a high value indicate?

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{3}
\tightlist
\item
  What are the four major phyla of the human gut microbiome?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{4}
\tightlist
\item
  What is a biofilm? Name two biological advantages biofilm growth

\begin{enumerate}

  Define mutualism, commensalism, and parasitism. Give one example of

\begin{enumerate}

  What is the rhizosphere? Name one bacterium that benefits plant growth

\begin{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}

\subsection*{Questions 11--20: Application and
Analysis}\label{questions-1120-application-and-analysis-22}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Questions 11--20: Application and
Analysis}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{10}
\tightlist
\item
  Fecal microbiome transplant (FMT) resolves recurrent
  \emph{Clostridioides difficile} infection in about 90\% of
  cases. Explain: (a) why antibiotic use predisposes patients to C.
  diff; (b) how FMT restores colonisation resistance; (c) why FMT is
  less likely to be effective in IBD (Crohn's, ulcerative colitis)?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{11}
\tightlist
\item
  A researcher performs 16S metagenomics on soil samples from fertile
  farmland, degraded land, and old-growth forest. Predict: which
  environment would show highest Shannon diversity; whether any taxa
  would serve as indicators of soil health; and what functional genes
  you would look for in shotgun metagenomics data.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{12}
\tightlist
\item
  The ``hygiene hypothesis'' (now refined as the ``old friends''
  hypothesis) proposes that reduced microbial exposure in early life
  increases allergic and autoimmune disease risk. Evaluate the evidence:
  (a) epidemiological (higher allergy rates in developed countries); (b)
  experimental (germ-free mice have hyperactive immune systems); (c)
  specific microbial species (Lactobacillus, Faecalibacterium
  prausnitzii) that prevent allergy.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{13}
\tightlist
\item
  Nitrogen cycle: N-fixing bacteria (\emph{Rhizobium} in legume nodules)
  convert N\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{2}}{2} \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} NH\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{3}}{3}. Nitrifying bacteria convert NH\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{3}}{3} \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} NO\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{2}}{2}\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{-}}{-} \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} NO\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{3}}{3}\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{-}}{-}.
  Denitrifying bacteria convert NO\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{3}}{3}\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{-}}{-} \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} N\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{2}}{2}. Trace a nitrogen atom from
  atmospheric N\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{2}}{2} through these steps into a plant protein, and then back
  to N\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{2}}{2} in soil. Why is this cycle vulnerable to disruption by synthetic
  fertilisers?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{14}
\tightlist
\item
  Marine microbial ecology: \emph{Prochlorococcus} is the most abundant
  photosynthetic organism on Earth (about 10\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{2}}{2}\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{7}}{7} cells). Explain:
  (a) its adaptations for low-nutrient, high-light (and low-light) ocean
  zones; (b) how phage predation of Prochlorococcus releases dissolved
  organic carbon (DOC) fuelling heterotrophic bacteria; (c) what would
  happen to ocean productivity if Prochlorococcus were eliminated.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{15}
\tightlist
\item
  The human oral microbiome (about 700 species) produces dental
  caries via \emph{Streptococcus mutans} acidifying enamel via lactic
  acid fermentation. Explain: (a) how sucrose is a uniquely cariogenic
  sugar (forms glucan adhesion matrix via glucosyltransferase); (b) what
  pH triggers enamel demineralisation (\textless5.5); (c) how fluoride
  in drinking water chemically protects enamel.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{16}
\tightlist
\item
  Quorum sensing coordinates population-level behaviour in bacteria
  (biofilm formation, bioluminescence, sporulation). Explain in
  \emph{Vibrio harveyi}: (a) how two quorum sensing circuits (LuxN and
  LuxPQ) integrate autoinducer signals at different cell densities; (b)
  why \emph{Vibrio fischeri} in the squid light organ shows
  population-density-dependent luminescence; (c) how quorum quenching
  enzymes (AHL lactonase) disrupt this signalling.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{17}
\tightlist
\item
  Antibiotic resistance spreads horizontally via mobile genetic elements
  (plasmids, integrons, transposons). Trace how resistance to
  trimethoprim and ampicillin on a co-integrated resistance plasmid
  would affect \emph{E. coli} evolution in a hospital drain environment:
  (a) does selection for one resistance indirectly maintain the other?
  (b) how does this create a co-selection problem when antibiotics are
  used?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{18}
\tightlist
\item
  Extremophile archaea in deep-sea hydrothermal vents oxidise H\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{2}}{2}S as
  electron donor, fixing CO\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{2}}{2} via the reverse TCA cycle (without
  photosynthesis). Compare this chemolithoautotrophic primary production
  to photosynthesis: (a) what is the electron donor; (b) what energy
  source; (c) how much biomass is produced per unit energy; (d) why this
  is important for understanding the origin of life.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{19}
\tightlist
\item
  Meta-analysis of 10 gut microbiome studies in Type 2 Diabetes (T2D)
  patients vs healthy controls identified depletion of \emph{Akkermansia
  muciniphila} and \emph{Faecalibacterium prausnitzii} in T2D. Design a
  causal inference test: (a) what correlation measure would you use; (b)
  what germ-free mouse experiment would establish causality; (c) what
  confounders (diet, medication) need controlling?
\end{enumerate}

\subsection*{Questions 21--30: Synthesis and
Evaluation}\label{questions-2130-synthesis-and-evaluation-22}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Questions 21--30: Synthesis and
Evaluation}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{20}
\tightlist
\item
  Evaluate the ``microbiome-brain axis'' (gut-brain axis): propose the
  mechanistic routes (vagus nerve, SCFAs, immune mediators, enteric
  serotonin) by which gut microbial composition can influence mood and
  cognition. What evidence from: (a) germ-free mice (increased anxiety,
  HPA axis changes); (b) faecal transfer from depressed patients to
  rats; (c) probiotic clinical trials in humans --- supports a causal
  role?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{21}
\tightlist
\item
  Design a metagenomics study to characterise the resistome (complete
  antibiotic resistance gene complement) of wastewater treatment plant
  effluent. Describe: (a) DNA extraction strategy; (b) how you would
  annotate resistance genes; (c) how you would determine whether
  identified genes are in pathogens vs harmless commensals; (d) how you
  would track the resistome over a full seasonal cycle.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{22}
\tightlist
\item
  Evaluate the concept of the ``core microbiome'' --- a set of microbial
  taxa present in most healthy individuals of a species. What criteria
  would define a ``core'' species, how would you distinguish core from
  accessory microbiome species, and why the concept is complicated by
  inter-individual variation (about 20\% of gut species may be
  ``comprehensive core'').
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{23}
\tightlist
\item
  Microbial succession in natural environments follows predictable
  patterns (e.g., pioneer \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} climax community in forest soils;
  successional microbiome during decomposition of whale falls). Evaluate
  the mechanisms (facilitation, inhibition, tolerance) controlling
  succession, and propose an experiment to test whether succession is
  driven by deterministic (niche-based) or stochastic processes.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{24}
\tightlist
\item
  Evaluate the concept of ``ecosystem services'' provided by soil
  microbiomes: nitrogen cycling, carbon sequestration, plant pathogen
  suppression. How does intensive agriculture (tillage, pesticide,
  monoculture) reduce soil microbial diversity and function? Propose a
  restorative soil management strategy that would re-establish lost
  ecosystem services.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{25}
\tightlist
\item
  The human virome includes about 6 \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\times}}{x} 10\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{1}}{1}\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{2}}{2} phage particles,
  largely matching the bacteriome. Evaluate: (a) how the virome
  influences bacteriome composition (phage predation driving community
  dynamics); (b) the evidence that an abnormal virome (e.g., expanded
  Caudovirales in Crohn's disease) can drive inflammation independently
  of the bacteriome; (c) whether the virome should be considered in the
  design of microbiome therapeutics.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{26}
\tightlist
\item
  Syntrophic communities (where no single organism can grow on a
  substrate alone --- requires metabolic cross-feeding with a partner)
  are central to anaerobic digestion of organic matter. Using the
  sulfate-reducing and methanogenic guild competition as an example,
  evaluate how thermodynamic constraints (Gibbs energy for each
  reaction) determine community composition, and why hydrogen partial
  pressure is the key variable.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{27}
\tightlist
\item
  Evaluate the potential of engineered synthetic microbial consortia for
  biotechnology (e.g., consortium for complete cellulose-to-ethanol
  conversion, or coordinated tumour-targeting drug delivery). What
  design principles govern consortium stability, and how can synthetic
  quorum sensing circuits be used to coordinate the activities of
  different strains?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{28}
\tightlist
\item
  The ocean microbiome is structured by ``niche partitioning'' on
  individual dissolved organic carbon (DOC) molecules: the ``competitive
  exclusion/keystone species'' model predicts that competitive exclusion
  dominates in low-diversity environments, while microbes coexist in
  complex high-DOC environments by partitioning onto different
  compounds. Evaluate how ``genome streamlining'' (loss of non-essential
  genes) in marine bacteria (e.g., SAR11) reflects adaptation to this
  competitive, nutrient-limited environment.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{29}
\tightlist
\item
  Critically evaluate the therapeutic potential of ``designer
  probiotics'' --- genetically engineered bacteria with specific
  metabolic or signalling functions. Using the example of a genetically
  engineered \emph{E. coli} Nissle expressing a GLP-1 precursor for
  treating obesity (clinical trial, 2025), evaluate: the safety concerns
  (containment of GMO bacteria, gene transfer to resident microbiome),
  the evidence of efficacy, and the regulatory framework needed.
\end{enumerate}
