\subsection*{Questions 11--20: Application and
Analysis}\label{questions-1120-application-and-analysis-23}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Questions 11--20: Application and
Analysis}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{10}
\tightlist
\item
  SARS-CoV-2 infected about 700 million people globally.
  Estimate the herd immunity threshold (H = 1 \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{-}}{-} 1/R\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{0}}{0}) if R\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{0}}{0} for the
  original strain was 2.5. For the Omicron variant (R\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{0}}{0} \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\approx}}{~} 10),
  recalculate the herd immunity threshold and explain the implications
  for vaccination coverage needed.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{11}
\tightlist
\item
  The inflammasome (NLRP3) is activated by uric acid crystals (gout),
  cholesterol crystals (atherosclerosis), and pathogens. Explain: (a)
  how NLRP3 assembles and activates caspase-1; (b) how caspase-1 cleaves
  pro-IL-1\texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\beta}}{beta} and pro-IL-18; (c) why NLRP3 inhibitors (MCC950) are under
  development for inflammatory diseases.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{12}
\tightlist
\item
  Influenza can shift from H1N1 to H3N2 by antigenic shift (segment
  reassortment) or antigenic drift (point mutations in haemagglutinin).
  Explain: (a) why antigenic drift requires annual vaccine
  reformulation; (b) why antigenic shift can cause pandemics; (c) what
  ``original antigenic sin'' means for immune memory.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{13}
\tightlist
\item
  The complement system (C1-C9) is a cascade of proteolytic activation
  that opsonises pathogens and lyses bacteria directly (MAC --- membrane
  attack complex). Describe the three complement activation pathways
  (classical, lectin, alternative), naming the central converging point
  (C3 convertase), and explain how bacteria evade complement (factor H
  mimicry, capsule).
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{14}
\tightlist
\item
  Natural killer (NK) cells kill virus-infected cells that downregulate
  MHC class I (a strategy used by many viruses to evade CTLs). Explain
  the ``missing self'' hypothesis: how do inhibitory KIR receptors
  normally inhibit NK killing, and how does MHC class I downregulation
  remove inhibition and trigger NK-mediated lysis?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{15}
\tightlist
\item
  mRNA vaccines (Pfizer-BioNTech, Moderna) for SARS-CoV-2 required
  solving two key problems: (a) mRNA instability in vivo (solution:
  pseudouridine substitution reduces TLR7/8 sensing and increases
  stability); (b) delivery to antigen-presenting cells in lymph nodes
  (solution: LNP --- lipid nanoparticle encapsulation). Trace the
  cascade from IM injection \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} LNP uptake by dendritic cells \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} spike
  protein expression \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} naive B and T cell activation \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} class switch
  recombination \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} IgG antibody production.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{16}
\tightlist
\item
  Regulatory T cells (Tregs, FOXP3\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{+}}{+}) suppress immune responses and
  prevent autoimmunity. Explain: (a) how Tregs develop (thymic selection
  vs peripheral induction); (b) their mechanisms of suppression (IL-10,
  TGF-\texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\beta}}{beta}, CTLA-4-mediated antigen-presenting cell suppression); (c) why
  depleting Tregs in cancer (anti-CTLA-4, ipilimumab) can restore
  anti-tumour immunity at the cost of autoimmunity.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{17}
\tightlist
\item
  Malaria (\emph{Plasmodium falciparum}) has complex immune evasion
  through antigenic variation of PfEMP1 (erythrocyte membrane protein 1)
  encoded by about 60 \emph{var} genes, a single active at a
  time. Explain: (a) why the immune system struggles to clear malaria;
  (b) how epigenetic switching between var genes works; (c) what
  approach (conserved antigen targets) vaccine developers use to
  circumvent this evasion.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{18}
\tightlist
\item
  Calculate basic epidemiological parameters: if an influenza outbreak
  shows 15 secondary cases per 10 infected individuals over a mean
  infectious period of 3 days (generation time 3 days), estimate R\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{0}}{0} and
  the doubling time of the epidemic. What control measure would need to
  be implemented to bring R to \textless{} 1?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{19}
\tightlist
\item
  Intestinal IgA is produced in the lamina propria by plasma cells and
  specifically transported into the gut lumen (via polymeric
  immunoglobulin receptor, pIgR). Explain: (a) how secretory IgA (sIgA)
  differs from serum IgA structurally; (b) the role of the secretory
  component; (c) how sIgA provides ``immune exclusion'' of pathogens
  without triggering inflammation.
\end{enumerate}

\subsection*{Questions 21--30: Synthesis and
Evaluation}\label{questions-2130-synthesis-and-evaluation-23}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Questions 21--30: Synthesis and
Evaluation}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{20}
\tightlist
\item
  Evaluate the ``inverted-U'' relationship between immune activation and
  pathogen clearance, using sepsis as a model: (a) why severe sepsis
  kills by cytokine storm (uncontrolled innate immune activation) rather
  than the pathogen itself; (b) the failure of anti-TNF-\texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\alpha}}{alpha} therapy in
  sepsis trials despite success in rheumatoid arthritis; (c) how the
  ``immunological hysteresis'' concept explains why the same cytokine
  blockade is beneficial in autoimmunity but harmful in sepsis.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{21}
\tightlist
\item
  Build a paper-based infectious-disease decision matrix for three
  current interventions: (a) BPaL/BPaLM-style most-oral treatment for
  rifampicin-resistant tuberculosis; (b) twice-yearly lenacapavir PrEP
  for people with substantial HIV exposure risk; (c) indoor spatial
  emanators added to insecticide-treated nets for malaria control. For
  each, state the biological target, the surveillance or eligibility
  evidence required, one equity constraint, and one reason the
  intervention should not be treated as a standalone solution.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{22}
\tightlist
\item
  Evaluate the evidence for ``trained innate immunity'': after exposure
  to \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\beta}}{beta}-glucan (from \emph{Candida}) or BCG vaccination, innate immune
  cells (macrophages, NK cells) show epigenetically reprogrammed,
  enhanced responses 3--6 months later. What epigenetic changes (H3K4me1
  at enhancers, mTOR-dependent metabolic rewiring) mediate this
  ``immunological memory'' in non-adaptive immune cells, and what are
  the implications for innate immune-based vaccines (BCG against
  COVID-19)?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{23}
\tightlist
\item
  Autoimmune diseases arise when self-tolerance breaks down. Evaluate
  three mechanisms of self-tolerance failure in Type 1 Diabetes (T1D):
  (a) central tolerance failure (inadequate thymic deletion of
  autoreactive T cells directed at insulin); (b) peripheral tolerance
  failure (Treg dysfunction); (c) molecular mimicry (GAD65-Coxsackie B
  virus homology). What evidence supports each mechanism in human T1D?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{24}
\tightlist
\item
  During COVID-19 pandemic, several SARS-CoV-2 variants of concern
  (Alpha, Delta, Omicron) arose sequentially. Evaluate the evolutionary
  pressures (immune evasion vs transmissibility) that drove variant
  emergence, and why Omicron showed more ACE2-binding mutations
  (increased transmissibility) but more spike mutations outside the RBD
  (immune evasion from vaccine-induced antibodies).
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{25}
\tightlist
\item
  Evaluate checkpoint immunotherapy for cancer: PD-1/PD-L1 blockade,
  CTLA-4 blockade, LAG-3 blockade. For what biomarker(s) (TMB, PD-L1
  expression, MSI-H) are these drugs most effective, and why do about
  20--30\% of eligible cancer patients benefit? Propose a combination
  therapy strategy to increase response rates while managing autoimmune
  toxicity (immune-related adverse events, irAEs).
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{26}
\tightlist
\item
  Evaluate the concept of the ``immunological homunculus'' --- that the
  normal immune system retains low-frequency self-reactive clones that
  perform surveillance and immunoregulation (not only pathology).
  Critically assess the evidence that low-affinity self-reactive T and B
  cells are essential for shaping the immune repertoire, and what
  happens when these regulatory self-reactive cells are eliminated by
  lymphodepletion.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{27}
\tightlist
\item
  The ``two-signal model'' of T cell activation requires: (1) TCR
  engagement with MHC-peptide and (2) a co-stimulatory signal (CD28-B7).
  Without signal 2, T cells become anergic (unresponsive). Evaluate how
  tumours exploit this model to suppress anti-tumour T cells by: (a)
  expressing PD-L1 (sending an anergy-inducing signal); (b) lacking
  co-stimulatory molecules; (c) expressing IDO (depleting tryptophan
  needed for T cell activation). How does CAR-T cell therapy bypass this
  requirement for co-stimulation?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{28}
\tightlist
\item
  Evaluate the emerging field of ``onco-immunology'' --- the mechanisms
  by which tumours edit the immune landscape (immunoediting: elimination
  \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} equilibrium \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} escape). Give specific molecular examples of immune
  editing at each phase, and assess whether the immune equilibrium phase
  can be maintained indefinitely in any cancer type, or whether escape
  is inevitable.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{29}
\tightlist
\item
  Critically evaluate the public health ethics of mandatory vaccination
  programmes. Using the framework of herd immunity thresholds,
  individual liberty, social contract theory, and harm principle (Mill),
  construct a utilitarian argument for and a libertarian argument
  against mandatory vaccination. What vaccination coverage is minimally
  required for herd immunity against measles (R\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{0}}{0} \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\approx}}{~} 18), and how do
  vaccine hesitancy and anti-vaccine movements affect public health?
\end{enumerate}

\subsection*{Questions 1--10: Recall and
Comprehension}\label{questions-110-recall-and-comprehension-24}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Questions 1--10: Recall and
Comprehension}

\emph{This activity accompanies
\cref{sec:unit_VIII_plant_structure_and_water} of the textbook ---
review that chapter before attempting the exercises below.}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  Name the three major tissue systems in plants. Give one cell type
  belonging to each.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{1}
\tightlist
\item

\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{2}
\tightlist
\item
  Define xylem and phloem. Which transports water and which transports
  sugars?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{3}
\tightlist
\item
  What are tracheids and vessel elements? How do they differ
  structurally?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{4}
\tightlist
\item
  Define water potential (\texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\Psi}}{Psi}). Write the equation \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\Psi}}{Psi} = \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\Psi}}{Psi}\_s + \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\Psi}}{Psi}\_p.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{5}
\tightlist
\item
  What is the Casparian strip? In which cell layer is it found and what

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{6}
\tightlist

  Define transpiration. What drives transpiration in leaves?

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{7}
\tightlist
\item
  What are stomata? What cells regulate their opening and closing?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{8}
\tightlist
\item
  What is root pressure? Under what conditions does it occur?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{9}
\tightlist
\item
  Describe the pressure-flow (Münch) hypothesis for phloem transport.
\end{enumerate}

\subsection*{Questions 11--20: Application and
Analysis}\label{questions-1120-application-and-analysis-24}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Questions 11--20: Application and
Analysis}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{10}
\tightlist
\item
  A plant cell has \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\Psi}}{Psi}\_s = \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{-}}{-}0.9 MPa and \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\Psi}}{Psi}\_p = +0.4 MPa. Calculate its \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\Psi}}{Psi}.
  If placed in a solution with \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\Psi}}{Psi} = \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{-}}{-}0.3 MPa, will water enter or leave
  the cell? What will change as the cell reaches equilibrium?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{11}
\tightlist
\item
  The cohesion-tension theory explains xylem water transport. Explain
  each component: (a) cohesion (H-bonds between water molecules); (b)
  adhesion (attraction to xylem walls); (c) tension (negative pressure
  from leaf transpiration). How does this mechanism pull water to 100 m
  in tall trees?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{12}
\tightlist
\item
  A researcher applies ABA (abscisic acid) to stomatal guard cells.
  Predict: (a) what happens to K\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{+}}{+} channels (efflux activated); (b) what
  happens to guard cell turgor; (c) what happens to stomatal aperture;
  (d) how CO\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{2}}{2} supply to mesophyll cells changes.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{13}
\tightlist
\item
  Compare apoplastic vs symplastic water transport from root epidermis
  to the xylem. What role does the Casparian strip play in forcing water
  through the symplastic pathway? Why is this gatekeeping important for
  ion selection?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{14}
\tightlist
\item
  Phloem loading concentrates sucrose in sieve tubes at the source.
  Explain: (a) the apoplastic loading pathway (H\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{+}}{+}-sucrose
  co-transporter); (b) how increased solute concentration in sieve tubes
  lowers \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\Psi}}{Psi}\_s; (c) how water follows by osmosis, generating turgor
  pressure that drives bulk flow toward the sink.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{15}
\tightlist
\item
  Cavitation (air bubble formation) in xylem vessels can block water
  transport. Explain: (a) how tension increases cavitation risk during
  drought; (b) how pit membranes between vessel elements limit
  cavitation spread; (c) how some trees (ring-porous oaks) repair
  cavitated vessels at night via root pressure.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{16}
\tightlist
\item
  A potometer measures transpiration rate by tracking water uptake. If a
  leafy shoot uptakes 4.5 mL/h at 25°C and 2.0 mL/h at 15°C, calculate:
  (a) the Q\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{1}}{1}\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{0}}{0} for transpiration; (b) what factor associated with
  temperature change drives this difference; (c) why humidity must also
  be controlled.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{17}
\tightlist
\item
  Mycorrhizal fungi dramatically increase root surface area and provide
  phosphorus to plants in exchange for photosynthetic carbon. Compare
  arbuscular mycorrhizae (AM, intracellular fungal hyphae) vs
  ectomycorrhizal (ECM, extracellular mantle). Estimate the increase in
  effective root absorptive area (10\texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\times}}{x} to 1,000\texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\times}}{x}) and explain why nearly
  90\% of plant species have mycorrhizal associations.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{18}
\tightlist
\item
  Halophytes (salt-tolerant plants) grow in saline soils (\texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\Psi}}{Psi}\_s
  \textless{} \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{-}}{-}1.0 MPa). Explain three strategies: (a) accumulation of
  compatible solutes (proline) to lower \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\Psi}}{Psi}\_s; (b) ion
  compartmentalisation into vacuoles (NHX1 Na\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{+}}{+}/H\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{+}}{+} antiporter); (c) salt
  secretion via specialised salt glands.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{19}
\tightlist
\item
  A plant anatomist sections a dicot stem and a monocot stem. List four
  differences in vascular bundle arrangement, cambium presence,
  cortex/pith proportions, and secondary growth capability.
\end{enumerate}

\subsection*{Questions 21--30: Synthesis and
Evaluation}\label{questions-2130-synthesis-and-evaluation-24}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Questions 21--30: Synthesis and
Evaluation}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{20}
\tightlist
\item
  Evaluate the limits of the cohesion-tension theory: the maximum
  theoretical xylem tension is approximately \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{-}}{-}20 MPa, but measured
  tensions rarely exceed \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{-}}{-}3 MPa. Does this discrepancy refute the
  theory? Discuss the ``vulnerability curve'' (loss of hydraulic
  conductivity vs tension) and how different species show different
  cavitation thresholds. What evolutionary strategies balance xylem
  safety vs efficiency?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{21}
\tightlist
\item
  Design an experiment to measure the hydraulic conductivity of a stem
  segment. Describe the apparatus (pressure head, flow rate
  measurement), the calculation (K\_h = flow rate \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\times}}{x} segment length /
  pressure difference), and how you would normalise for sapwood area.
  What would you expect for a conifer (tracheids primarily) vs a
  diffuse-porous angiosperm (vessel elements)?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{22}
\tightlist
\item
  Evaluate the evidence that aquaporins regulate short-term water
  transport in roots. How does the abundance and phosphorylation state
  of root aquaporins (PIP1, PIP2 subfamilies) change in response to: (a)
  drought; (b) flooding; (c) diurnal light cycles? What does this imply
  about the relative importance of the apoplastic vs symplastic pathway
  under different environmental conditions?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{23}
\tightlist
\item
  Propose a bioengineering strategy to improve drought tolerance in crop
  plants by manipulating water transport. Compare three approaches: (a)
  engineering deeper root systems (overexpressing DRO1); (b) increasing
  xylem vessel diameter for greater hydraulic conductivity; (c)
  constitutively closing stomata (overexpressing OST1 kinase). For each,
  evaluate the trade-off between water conservation and carbon
  assimilation. Which strategy is most promising for wheat in arid
  environments?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{24}
\tightlist
\item
  Phloem transport speed is about 1 m/h. Calculate: if a tree
  is 30 m tall and assimilate loading occurs in the canopy, how long
  does it take for sucrose to reach root tips? Compare this to xylem
  transport speed (about 10--40 m/h). What limits phloem
  transport speed (viscosity of concentrated sucrose solution, sieve
  plate resistance)?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{25}
\tightlist
\item
  Evaluate the evolutionary transition from tracheids (present in most
  vascular plants) to vessel elements (present in angiosperms and some
  gymnosperms). What anatomical changes (perforation plates, wider
  diameter) conferred increased hydraulic efficiency, and what
  trade-offs (increased vulnerability to cavitation) accompanied this
  transition? How does this relate to the ecological dominance of
  angiosperms?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{26}
\tightlist
\item
  The pressure-flow model (Münch) for phloem transport makes predictions
  about: (a) turgor in source vs sink phloem; (b) the osmotic potential
  gradient between source and sink; (c) the effect of girdling (removing
  phloem) on sugar accumulation above the girdle. Evaluate each
  prediction using experimental evidence, and assess the main criticism
  of the model (can passive flow alone explain transport over
  \textgreater50 m?).
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{27}
\tightlist
\item
  Evaluate the role of plasmodesmata in cell-to-cell communication in
  plants. How do plasmodesmata allow selective symplastic transport
  (size exclusion limit about 1 kDa), what signals move through
  them (transcription factors like KNOTTED1, siRNAs), and how do viruses
  exploit plasmodesmata for cell-to-cell spread (movement proteins)?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{28}
\tightlist
\item
  Climate change increases atmospheric CO\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{2}}{2} and temperature, both of
  which affect transpiration, stomatal conductance, and water-use
  efficiency. Evaluate the predicted effects on forest water balance:
  (a) increased CO\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{2}}{2} \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} partial stomatal closure \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} reduced transpiration \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
  increased runoff; (b) increased temperature \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} increased VPD \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
  increased transpiration \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} drought stress. Which effect dominates in
  tropical forests vs boreal forests?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{29}
\tightlist
\item
  Critically evaluate whether the ``hydraulic architecture'' of a tree
  (the specific pattern of vessel diameters, vessel density, and branch
  tapering from base to tip) is optimised by natural selection for
  efficient water delivery. Apply Murray's law (branching geometry) and
  the ``safety vs efficiency'' trade-off framework. What does damage
  from extreme drought events reveal about the limits of optimisation?
\end{enumerate}

\section*{Questions --- Ch 26: Plant Reproduction and

and Development}

\subsection*{Questions 1--10: Recall and
Comprehension}\label{questions-110-recall-and-comprehension-25}

below.}

\begin{enumerate}

  Describe the alternation of generations in plant life cycles. What is

\subsection*{Questions 11--20: Application and
Analysis}\label{questions-1120-application-and-analysis-25}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Questions 11--20: Application and
Analysis}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{10}
\tightlist
\item
  Double fertilisation: one sperm fuses with the egg (2n zygote),
  another fuses with the central cell (3n endosperm). Explain the
  evolutionary advantage of triploid endosperm vs a haploid nutritive
  tissue. Why is endosperm essential for seed development in cereals?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{11}
\tightlist
\item
  SI (self-incompatibility) mechanisms prevent self-pollination. In
  gametophytic SI (e.g., \emph{Nicotiana}), pollen S-RNases degrade RNA
  in incompatible (self) pollen tubes. Explain: (a) the molecular logic
  --- why would a plant destroy its own pollen; (b) the advantage for
  genetic diversity; (c) how SI is overcome in commercial apple orchards
  (polliniser trees).
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{12}
\tightlist
\item
  Seed dormancy allows seeds to delay germination until conditions are
  favourable. Explain: (a) the role of ABA (prevents germination) vs
  gibberellin (promotes germination); (b) why stratification (cold
  treatment) breaks dormancy in temperate-region seeds; (c) the
  ecological advantage of dormancy for fire-adapted species
  (heat-triggered germination).
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{13}
\tightlist
\item
  Fruit types: distinguish fleshy fruits (berry, drupe, pome) from dry
  fruits (achene, capsule, legume). For each type, name an example
  species and explain how the fruit structure promotes seed dispersal
  (animal, wind, water, or ballistic).
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{14}
\tightlist
\item
  Arabidopsis ABCE model of floral organ identity: A genes \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} sepals; A+B
  \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} petals; B+C \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} stamens; C \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} carpels; E is required in most whorls.
  Predict the floral phenotype when: (a) the B gene is knocked out; (b)
  the A gene is knocked out; (c) both A and C are knocked out. What
  would each mutant flower look like?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{15}
\tightlist
\item
  Pollen tube navigation: pollen tubes grow through the style following
  chemical gradients (e.g., LURE peptides from the synergid cells
  flanking the egg cell). Explain: (a) how Ca\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{2}}{2}\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{+}}{+} oscillations drive
  directional tip growth; (b) the role of the filiform apparatus in
  synergid cells; (c) what happens if a pollen tube arrives at an
  already-fertilised ovule (polytubey block).
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{16}
\tightlist
\item
  Apomixis (asexual seed production without fertilisation) occurs
  naturally in some grasses and dandelions. Explain: (a) the mechanism
  (unreduced embryo sac, parthenogenesis); (b) why agriculture would
  benefit from engineered apomixis in hybrid crops (fixing heterosis
  permanently); (c) the rice synthetic-apomixis approach using MiMe plus
  a parthenogenesis trigger; (d) what field-translation risks remain.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{17}
\tightlist
\item
  Compare seed dispersal strategies: epizoochory (burs attaching to
  animal fur), endozoochory (fleshy fruits eaten by birds), anemochory
  (wind, e.g., dandelion pappus), hydrochory (water, coconut). For each,
  predict which seed/fruit trait is maximised (adhesion strength,
  palatability, surface area, buoyancy).
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{18}
\tightlist
\item
  The transition from vegetative to reproductive growth (floral
  transition) is controlled by the florigen protein FT (FLOWERING LOCUS
  T) produced in leaves and transported via phloem to the shoot apical
  meristem. Explain: (a) how photoperiod (sensed by CONSTANS protein in
  leaves) triggers FT expression; (b) how FT interacts with FD
  transcription factor at the meristem to activate floral identity genes
  (AP1); (c) why vernalisation (prolonged cold) is required for winter
  annuals.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{19}
\tightlist
\item
  Embryogenesis in plants establishes the apical-basal axis (shoot-root)
  and radial axis (epidermis-vascular tissue-ground tissue). Using
  Arabidopsis as a model, describe: (a) the role of the asymmetric first
  division; (b) the signalling between the suspensor and the embryo
  proper; (c) the auxin gradient that specifies the root pole
  (PIN-mediated polar transport).
\end{enumerate}

\subsection*{Questions 21--30: Synthesis and
Evaluation}\label{questions-2130-synthesis-and-evaluation-25}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Questions 21--30: Synthesis and
Evaluation}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{20}
\tightlist
\item
  Coevolution between flowering plants and their pollinators has shaped
  morphological diversity. Evaluate the evidence for pollination
  syndromes (e.g., red tubular flowers \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} hummingbird; white fragrant
  nocturnal \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} moth; UV-patterned \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} bee). Are syndromes perfect
  predictors? What does the ``most effective pollinator'' principle say
  about syndrome fidelity vs pollinator generalisation?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{21}
\tightlist
\item
  Design a breeding programme to introduce self-incompatibility from a
  wild relative into a self-compatible crop species (e.g., tomato).
  Describe the genetic crosses required, how you would screen for SI
  expression, and the trade-off between enforced outcrossing (greater
  heterosis) and practical challenges (pollinator dependence).
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{22}
\tightlist
\item
  Evaluate the hypothesis that the origin of the flower was a single
  evolutionary event (monophyletic origin of angiosperms). Cite evidence
  from: (a) molecular phylogenies (most angiosperms share a common
  ancestor); (b) fossil data (earliest undisputed flower fossils
  about 132 Mya); (c) the ``evo-devo'' evidence that the
  MADS-box gene family was duplicated and diversified at the base of
  angiosperms. What is ``Darwin's abominable mystery''?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{23}
\tightlist
\item
  Parthenocarpy (seedless fruit production) can be induced by GA\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{3}}{3}
  application (seedless grapes) or by gene engineering (auxin- or
  GA-overproduction in ovary). Evaluate: (a) why seedless fruits are
  commercially valuable; (b) what transcriptional changes GA\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{3}}{3} induces in
  the ovary wall (cell expansion genes); (c) whether GM parthenocarpy
  would require approval as a GMO in the EU.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{24}
\tightlist
\item
  Evaluate the evolutionary transition from water-dependent reproduction
  (bryophytes --- motile sperm requiring a water film) to
  water-independent reproduction (angiosperms --- pollen grain, pollen
  tube, sealed ovule). What were the key innovations at each transition
  (vascular plants \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} seeds \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} flowers \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} enclosed ovules), and how did
  each innovation expand environmental range?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{25}
\tightlist
\item
  The seed coat (testa) provides physical and chemical protection
  against pathogens, UV, and desiccation. Evaluate the molecular basis
  of seed coat impermeability (suberin and lignin deposits) and how seed
  coat-imposed dormancy is released by scarification (physical damage)
  or microbial degradation. What trade-off exists between strong
  dormancy (survival) and rapid germination (competitive advantage)?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{26}
\tightlist
\item
  Epigenetic regulation of seed development: the MEDEA/FIE Polycomb
  complex prevents autonomous endosperm development before
  fertilisation. After fertilisation, paternal genome expression
  overcomes MEDEA repression (genomic imprinting). Evaluate: (a) why the
  paternal genome specifically is needed to initiate endosperm; (b) the
  parent-of-origin conflict hypothesis (Haig theory) applied to seed
  provisioning; (c) what happens in interploidy crosses (2x \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\times}}{x} 4x) where
  parental dosage is disrupted.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{27}
\tightlist
\item
  Evaluate the potential of synthetic seeds (somatic embryos
  encapsulated in alginate beads) for clonal propagation of elite crop
  genotypes. What are the technical challenges (desiccation tolerance of
  somatic embryos, germination rate, production at scale), and how do
  synthetic seeds compare to traditional seed in terms of cost, genetic
  uniformity, and epigenetic stability?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{28}
\tightlist
\item
  Climate change alters flowering phenology (timing of first bloom).
  Evaluate: (a) how warming temperatures can alter vernalisation,
  florigen release, and pollen fertility; (b) what happens when plant
  flowering phenology shifts but pollinator phenology does not; (c) what
  field evidence would distinguish pollen heat failure from
  plant-pollinator phenological mismatch.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{29}
\tightlist
\item
  Critically evaluate CRISPR-based gene drives in wild plant
  populations: if a drive were engineered to spread herbicide resistance
  from a crop to its wild relatives, evaluate the ecological risks
  (invasive hybrid vigour, competitive dominance), the containment
  strategies (temporal/spatial/genetic containment), and the regulatory
  framework needed. Is there ever a scenario where a gene drive in
  plants would be ethically justified?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}

\tightlist

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{4}
\tightlist
\item
  Name four plant hormones other than auxin and state one major function
  of each.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{5}
\tightlist
\item
  What is ethylene? What role does it play in fruit ripening?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{6}
\tightlist
\item
  What is the phytochrome system? Distinguish Pr and Pfr forms.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{7}
\tightlist
\item
  What are plant defence responses to herbivory? Name two chemical
  defences.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{8}
\tightlist
\item
  Define thigmotropism. Give one example.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{9}
\tightlist
\item
  What is vernalisation? Which gene (FLC) is epigenetically silenced by
  prolonged cold?
\end{enumerate}

\subsection*{Questions 11--20: Application and
Analysis}\label{questions-1120-application-and-analysis-26}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Questions 11--20: Application and
Analysis}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{10}
\tightlist
\item
  The Cholodny-Went model explains phototropism: auxin redistributes
  laterally to the shaded side, causing differential elongation.
  Describe the evidence: (a) agar block experiments; (b) PIN3 auxin
  efflux carrier redistribution; (c) auxin-responsive reporter
  (DR5::GFP). What alternative explanations (differential auxin
  sensitivity, flavonoid phototropins) have been proposed?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{11}
\tightlist
\item
  Gibberellins promote stem elongation by degrading DELLA growth
  repressors. Explain: (a) the molecular pathway (GA \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} GID1 receptor \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
  DELLA ubiquitination \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} proteasome degradation); (b) how dwarf mutants
  (GA-deficient or DELLA gain-of-function) fail to elongate; (c) why the
  Green Revolution wheat varieties (Rht-B1b, Rht-D1b) carry
  semi-dominant DELLA mutations that reduce height and lodging.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{12}
\tightlist
\item
  Ethylene triggers the triple response in dark-grown seedlings
  (shortened stem, thickened stem, horizontal growth). Design an
  experiment using: (a) the ethylene biosynthesis inhibitor AVG; (b) the
  ethylene-insensitive mutant \emph{ein2}; (c) an ethylene-overproducing
  mutant (\emph{eto1}) to confirm that each component of the triple
  response is ethylene-dependent.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{13}
\tightlist
\item
  Jasmonic acid (JA) mediates herbivore-induced defences. When a
  caterpillar chews a leaf, systemin (a peptide signal) activates JA
  biosynthesis, which induces protease inhibitors in distant unwounded
  leaves. Trace the entire signalling cascade: wounding \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} systemin
  release \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} systemin receptor \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} JA biosynthesis (from linolenic acid in
  chloroplast) \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} COI1-JAZ interaction \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} MYC2 transcription factor
  activation \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} PI gene expression.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{14}
\tightlist
\item
  Phytochrome interconversion: Pr (absorbs red 660 nm, inactive) \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\rightleftharpoons}}{<=>} Pfr
  (absorbs far-red 730 nm, active). In a long-day plant, flowering is
  promoted by long photoperiods (short nights). Explain: (a) how the
  phytochrome system measures night length (Pfr \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} Pr reversion rate in
  the dark); (b) how a brief red flash in the middle of a long night
  promotes flowering; (c) how a subsequent far-red flash reverses this.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{15}
\tightlist
\item
  Abscisic acid (ABA) promotes stomatal closure under drought stress.
  Explain the guard cell signalling cascade: ABA \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} RCAR/PYL receptor \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
  PP2C inactivation \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} SnRK2 activation \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} SLAC1 anion channel opening \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
  Cl\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{-}}{-} and malate\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{2}}{2}\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{-}}{-} efflux \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} K\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{+}}{+} efflux \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} turgor loss \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} stomata close.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{16}
\tightlist
\item
  Auxin dose-response curves differ between stems and roots: stems show
  maximum elongation at about 10\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{-}}{-}\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{5}}{5} M auxin, while roots show
  maximum elongation at about 10\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{-}}{-}\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{1}}{1}\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{0}}{0} M auxin and are inhibited
  at concentrations that stimulate stems. Explain: (a) how this
  difference underlies gravitropism (auxin accumulates on the lower
  side, inhibiting root elongation while stimulating shoot elongation);
  (b) why 2,4-D (a synthetic auxin) is an effective herbicide for
  broadleaf plants.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{17}
\tightlist
\item
  Plants produce volatile organic compounds (VOCs) in response to
  herbivory that attract predators of the herbivore (``crying for
  help''). The lima bean-spider mite-predatory mite tritrophic system is
  a classic example. Explain: (a) which VOCs (terpenoids, green leaf
  volatiles) are emitted; (b) how neighbouring undamaged plants
  ``eavesdrop'' via VOC-induced defensive gene expression; (c) whether
  this constitutes plant communication or merely an information-rich
  cue.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{18}
\tightlist
\item
  Circadian clock in plants: the core oscillator (CCA1/LHY \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} TOC1 \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
  CCA1/LHY feedback loop) regulates about 30\% of plant gene
  expression. Explain: (a) how the clock anticipates dawn (pre-dawn
  expression of photosynthesis genes); (b) how jet-lag experiments
  (sudden photoperiod shift) reveal resynchronisation kinetics; (c) why
  clock mutants (TOC1-ox) have reduced fitness under natural light-dark
  cycles.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{19}
\tightlist
\item
  SAR (systemic acquired resistance) provides long-lasting,
  broad-spectrum pathogen protection. Following a localised pathogen
  infection, the signal molecule salicylic acid (SA) activates the SA
  pathway \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} NPR1 monomerisation \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} nuclear import \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} TGA transcription
  factor activation \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} PR (pathogenesis-related) gene expression. How
  does this confer resistance to secondary infections in distal tissues?
\end{enumerate}

\subsection*{Questions 21--30: Synthesis and
Evaluation}\label{questions-2130-synthesis-and-evaluation-26}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Questions 21--30: Synthesis and
Evaluation}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{20}
\tightlist
\item
  Evaluate the evidence for ``plant intelligence'' or ``plant
  neurobiology'' --- the concept that plant signalling networks
  (electrical action potentials, calcium waves, hormone gradients)
  constitute a form of information processing analogous to animal
  brains. Critically assess: (a) what criteria define intelligence; (b)
  whether plants satisfy any of these; (c) the boundaries of legitimate
  analogy vs anthropomorphism.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{21}
\tightlist
\item
  Design a CRISPR knockout experiment in Arabidopsis to determine
  whether the gravitropic response requires the starch-statolith
  mechanism (amyloplast sedimentation) or an alternative membrane-based
  mechanosensing pathway. What gene(s) would you knock out (PGM1 for
  starchless mutants), what phenotype would you measure, and what result
  would distinguish the two hypotheses?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{22}
\tightlist
\item
  Evaluate the molecular mechanisms of plant adaptation to flooding
  stress (waterlogging and submergence). Compare: (a) the SUB1A strategy
  in rice (quiescence --- ethylene \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} SUB1A \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} DELLA stabilisation \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
  growth arrest); (b) the SNORKEL strategy (escape --- ethylene \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
  SK1/SK2 \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} GA signalling \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} rapid internode elongation to escape
  floodwater). Under what flooding regimes is each strategy
  advantageous?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{23}
\tightlist
\item
  Climate change increases UV-B radiation at Earth's surface due to
  ozone depletion. Evaluate plant UV-B responses: (a) UVR8
  photoreceptor-mediated signalling \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} COP1-SPA \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} HY5 transcription
  factor \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} flavonoid/anthocyanin biosynthesis (sunscreen); (b) UV-B
  effects on DNA (CPD lesion formation) and repair (photolyase); (c)
  predicted impacts on crop productivity.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{24}
\tightlist
\item
  Evaluate the evolutionary arms race between plants and herbivores.
  Using the example of glucosinolate-myrosinase system in Brassicaceae
  (the ``mustard oil bomb''): (a) how the system works (glucosinolates
  are stored separately from myrosinase; upon tissue damage, they mix to
  produce toxic isothiocyanates); (b) how specialised herbivores
  (diamondback moth) detoxify isothiocyanates; (c) what countermeasure
  plant lineages have evolved (novel glucosinolates).
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{25}
\tightlist
\item
  Symbiotic nitrogen fixation (Rhizobium-legume): evaluate the molecular
  cross-talk leading to nodule formation: (a) plant-derived flavonoids \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
  bacterial NodD \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} Nod factor production \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} root hair curling \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} infection
  thread \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} nodule primordia; (b) the oxygen paradox (nitrogenase is
  O\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{2}}{2}-sensitive but Rhizobium needs aerobic respiration \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} leghaemoglobin
  O\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{2}}{2} buffering); (c) the autoregulation of nodulation (too many nodules
  are costly \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} CLE peptide negative feedback).
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{26}
\tightlist
\item
  Evaluate the role of epigenetics in plant stress memory. After a heat
  stress episode, some plants show enhanced heat tolerance for weeks
  (priming). What molecular marks (H3K4me3 at HSP loci, small RNA
  populations, chromatin remodelling) mediate stress memory, and does
  this memory have transgenerational stability?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{27}
\tightlist
\item
  Parasitic plants (Striga, Orobanche, dodder) exploit host plant
  signals to locate and attach to hosts. Evaluate: (a) how Striga seeds
  detect host-derived strigolactones as germination cues; (b) how the
  haustorium forms and penetrates host xylem/phloem; (c) why Striga is
  the most economically devastating weed in sub-Saharan Africa; (d) what
  control strategies (resistant crop varieties, suicidal germination
  stimulants) are being deployed.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{28}
\tightlist
\item
  Evaluate the potential of ``smart crops'' engineered with synthetic
  hormone signalling circuits: e.g., a crop that closes stomata in
  response to soil moisture sensors (synthetic ABA-independent
  signalling), activates JA defences primarily when herbivores are
  detected (synthetic promoter responsive to caterpillar oral
  secretions), and accelerates flowering under climate-variable
  conditions (synthetic florigen circuit). What are the engineering
  feasibility, field-validation, regulatory, and ecological risks?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{29}
\tightlist
\item
  Critically assess the claim that plant volatile communication
  represents a form of ``language'': (a) define what communication
  requires (sender, signal, receiver, response, evolved function); (b)
  evaluate whether plant VOC emission meets these criteria; (c) compare
  plant volatile signalling to animal pheromone communication; (d)
  assess the fitness benefit to the emitter (is it a true signal or an
  incidental cue exploited by neighbours?).
\end{enumerate}

\section*{Questions --- Ch 28: Circulation, Respiration, and
Homeostasis}\label{questions-ch-28-circulation-respiration-and-homeostasis}
\addcontentsline{toc}{section}{Questions --- Ch 28: Circulation,
Respiration, and Homeostasis}

\label{sec:q_unit_IX_circulation_respiration_homeostasis}

\subsection*{Instructor Use and Coverage
Notes}\label{instructor-use-and-coverage-notes-30}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Instructor Use and Coverage Notes}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{Coverage target:} Calculate a transport or feedback variable
  and explain the compensatory response.
\item
  \textbf{Model/data emphasis:} Cardiac-output, diffusion,
  oxygen-saturation, and feedback calculations.
\item
  \textbf{Assessment alignment:} Visual Representations, Statistical
  Tests and Data Analysis, Argumentation.
\item
  \textbf{Misconception probe:} Homeostasis is dynamic regulation, not
  an unchanging internal state.
\item
  \textbf{Transfer product:} Transfer homeostatic reasoning to exercise,
  altitude, hemorrhage, fever, and shock.
\item
  \textbf{Grading focus:} award full credit for mechanism, evidence,
  boundary conditions, and units when a calculation is required.
\item
  \textbf{Suggested use:} draw one recall item, one application item,
  and one synthesis item when building a short quiz from this bank.
\end{itemize}

--- review that chapter before attempting the exercises below.}

\subsection*{Questions 11--20: Application and
Analysis}\label{questions-1120-application-and-analysis-27}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Questions 11--20: Application and
Analysis}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{10}
\tightlist
\item
  During exercise, HR increases from 70 to 160 bpm and SV from 70 mL to
  120 mL. Calculate the CO at rest and during exercise. What is the
  fold-increase? What mechanisms increase HR (sympathetic \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} SA node \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
  faster depolarisation) and SV (Frank-Starling mechanism)?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{11}
\tightlist
\item
  The Bohr effect: increased CO\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{2}}{2} and H\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{+}}{+} in exercising muscle shift the
  oxygen-haemoglobin dissociation curve rightward, decreasing Hb's O\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{2}}{2}
  affinity. Explain: (a) the molecular basis (protonation of His146
  stabilising the T-state); (b) the physiological benefit (enhanced O\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{2}}{2}
  unloading in active tissues); (c) what happens at the lungs (low CO\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{2}}{2},
  high pH \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} leftward shift \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} enhanced O\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{2}}{2} loading).
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{12}
\tightlist
\item
  Ventilation-perfusion (V/Q) matching ensures that regions of the lung
  receiving airflow also receive blood flow. Explain: (a) what happens
  when V/Q is high (dead space) vs low (shunt); (b) how local hypoxic
  pulmonary vasoconstriction (HPV) diverts blood from poorly ventilated
  alveoli; (c) why chronic lung disease (COPD) causes V/Q mismatch and
  hypoxaemia.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{13}
\tightlist
\item
  Blood pressure regulation: the baroreceptor reflex senses carotid
  sinus stretch. When BP drops: (a) baroreceptor firing decreases; (b)
  medullary cardiovascular centre increases sympathetic output; (c) HR,
  contractility, and peripheral resistance increase; (d) BP is restored.
  What happens if the baroreceptor reflex fails (autonomic neuropathy)?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{14}
\tightlist
\item
  Surfactant (produced by type II alveolar cells) reduces alveolar
  surface tension. Without surfactant: (a) what happens to alveolar
  compliance (Laplace's law: P = 2T/r \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} smaller alveoli collapse into
  larger ones); (b) what condition results in premature infants (NRDS
  --- neonatal respiratory distress syndrome); (c) how is antenatal
  corticosteroid treatment used to mature fetal lungs?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{15}
\tightlist
\item
  The kidney maintains blood osmolality homeostasis. ADH (vasopressin)
  is released from the posterior pituitary in response to high blood
  osmolality. Explain: (a) how ADH regulates AQP2 insertion into the
  collecting duct apical membrane; (b) why ADH deficiency produces
  dilute, voluminous urine (diabetes insipidus); (c) how alcohol
  inhibits ADH secretion and causes diuresis.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{16}
\tightlist
\item
  Counter-current exchange in the vasa recta (renal medullary blood
  vessels) maintains the osmotic gradient established by the loop of
  Henle. Explain: (a) why the vasa recta loop parallel to the loop of
  Henle; (b) how ascending and descending limbs exchange solutes; (c)
  what would happen to medullary osmolality if the vasa recta were
  replaced by a single straight vessel.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{17}
\tightlist
\item
  During cold exposure, thermoregulation maintains core temperature at
  37°C. Trace the response: peripheral thermoreceptors \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} hypothalamus \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
  sympathetic nervous system \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} cutaneous vasoconstriction \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} reduced heat
  loss + shivering \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} increased heat production. What is the set-point
  concept, and how does fever alter the set-point?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{18}
\tightlist
\item
  The oxygen cascade describes the progressive decrease in PO\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{2}}{2} from
  atmosphere (160 mmHg) to mitochondria (about 1--3 mmHg).
  Identify each step: inspired air \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} alveolar air (104 mmHg, diluted by
  CO\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{2}}{2} and water vapour) \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} arterial blood (100 mmHg, some V/Q mismatch) \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
  capillary blood \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} tissue \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} mitochondria. At which step is the largest
  PO\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{2}}{2} drop, and what determines its magnitude?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{19}
\tightlist
\item
  Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) results in an EF
  \textless{} 40\% (normal 55--70\%). Explain: (a) why reduced
  contractility leads to fluid retention (RAAS activation); (b) why
  diuretics provide symptomatic relief but do not improve survival; (c)
  how ACE inhibitors + beta-blockers + ARNI (sacubitril/valsartan) have
  been shown to reduce mortality.
\end{enumerate}

\subsection*{Questions 21--30: Synthesis and
Evaluation}\label{questions-2130-synthesis-and-evaluation-27}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Questions 21--30: Synthesis and
Evaluation}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{20}
\tightlist
\item
  Evaluate the Frank-Starling mechanism at the molecular level:
  increased preload \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} increased sarcomere stretch \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} increased Ca\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{2}}{2}\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{+}}{+}
  sensitivity of troponin C \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} increased force production. What molecular
  mechanism converts sarcomere length into increased Ca\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{2}}{2}\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{+}}{+} sensitivity,
  and why does this relationship break down in dilated cardiomyopathy
  (DCM)?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{21}
\tightlist
\item
  Design an experiment to measure the maximal aerobic capacity (VO\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{2}}{2} max)
  of a human subject. Describe: the incremental exercise protocol
  (treadmill or cycle), the gas analysis measurements (O\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{2}}{2} consumption,
  CO\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{2}}{2} production, RER), and the criteria for reaching true VO\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{2}}{2} max. How
  does VO\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{2}}{2} max differ between trained athletes and sedentary
  individuals, and what factors (cardiac output, O\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{2}}{2} extraction, muscle
  mitochondrial density) limit performance?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{22}
\tightlist
\item
  Evaluate the roles of the sympathetic and parasympathetic nervous
  systems in cardiovascular regulation via their respective
  neurotransmitters (norepinephrine \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\beta}}{beta}\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{1}}{1} receptors \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} increased HR vs
  acetylcholine \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} M\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{2}}{2} receptors \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} decreased HR). What is ``vagal tone''
  at rest, and why does denervation of the heart (cardiac transplant
  recipients) result in a resting HR of about 100 bpm?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{23}
\tightlist
\item
  Evaluate the physiological trade-off between capillary density and
  distance-limited O\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{2}}{2} diffusion: (a) use Fick's law of diffusion (J = D
  \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\times}}{x} A \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\times}}{x} \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\Delta}}{Delta}P/d) to explain why capillary density must increase in
  metabolically active tissues; (b) calculate the maximum O\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{2}}{2} diffusion
  distance (about 100 \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\mu}}{mu}m); (c) explain why tumours develop
  necrotic cores when they grow beyond 200 \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\mu}}{mu}m without angiogenesis.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{24}
\tightlist
\item
  High altitude acclimatisation involves acute and chronic responses:
  acute (hyperventilation, increased HR); chronic (EPO \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} erythrocytosis,
  2,3-BPG increase, vascular remodelling). Evaluate: (a) how the carotid
  body senses hypoxia and triggers hyperventilation; (b) why respiratory
  alkalosis results; (c) how renal bicarbonate excretion compensates;
  (d) why chronic mountain sickness (Monge's disease) can result from
  excessive erythropoiesis.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{25}
\tightlist
\item
  Evaluate the ``oxygen paradox'' in ischaemia-reperfusion injury:
  restored oxygen supply to ischaemic tissue generates ROS (via xanthine
  oxidase and Complex I) that cause greater damage than the ischaemia
  itself. How do ROS cause injury (membrane lipid peroxidation,
  mitochondrial permeability transition pore opening), and what
  therapeutic strategies (hypothermia, ischaemic pre-conditioning)
  mitigate reperfusion injury?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{26}
\tightlist
\item
  Evaluate the hypothesis that endothermy evolved from aerobic capacity
  (the ``aerobic capacity model''): selection for sustained locomotion \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
  increased mitochondrial density \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} increased resting metabolic rate \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
  internal heat production \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} endothermy. Compare this to the ``parental
  care model'' (selection for incubation of eggs \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} endothermy). Which
  model is better supported by paleontological and comparative
  physiological evidence?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{27}
\tightlist
\item
  The lymphatic system returns interstitial fluid to the bloodstream.
  Evaluate: (a) how lymph is formed (Starling's forces \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} net filtration
  at the arterial end of capillaries); (b) what happens when lymphatic
  drainage fails (lymphoedema --- elephantiasis caused by parasitic
  nematode \emph{Wuchereria bancrofti}); (c) the dual role of lymphatics
  in immune surveillance (dendritic cell migration to lymph nodes).
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{28}
\tightlist
\item
  Diving mammals (Weddell seal, sperm whale) can hold their breath for
  \textgreater60 minutes while diving to \textgreater1,000 m. Evaluate
  four physiological adaptations: (a) bradycardia and peripheral
  vasoconstriction (dive reflex); (b) elevated myoglobin content (O\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{2}}{2}
  storage); (c) splenic contraction (autotransfusion of O\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{2}}{2}-carrying
  RBCs); (d) tolerance of lactate (anaerobic metabolism during deep
  dives). How do these adaptations differ between pinnipeds and
  cetaceans?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{29}
\tightlist
\item
  Critically evaluate the concept of ``physiological reserve'' --- the
  excess capacity of organ systems beyond what is needed at rest (e.g.,
  cardiac output can increase 5\texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\times}}{x} during exercise, kidneys can maintain
  GFR with a single kidney). How does ageing erode physiological
  reserve, and at what threshold does age-related reserve depletion
  produce clinical disease? Apply the concept to explain why the elderly
  are disproportionately vulnerable to COVID-19, heat waves, and
  surgical stress. Then transfer the same homeostatic-reserve logic to a
  salty high-protein meal with low water intake: predict plasma
  osmolality, ADH/aldosterone direction, hepatic urea production, urine
  concentration, and why desert mammals and freshwater fish handle
  nitrogen differently.
\end{enumerate}

\subsection*{Questions 11--20: Application and
Analysis}\label{questions-1120-application-and-analysis-28}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Questions 11--20: Application and
Analysis}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{10}
\tightlist
\item
  The Goldman equation predicts resting membrane potential from the
  relative permeabilities of Na\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{+}}{+}, K\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{+}}{+}, and Cl\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{-}}{-}. If a mutation doubles Na\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{+}}{+}
  permeability at rest (P\_Na increases 2\texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\times}}{x}), predict the new resting
  potential direction (depolarisation toward E\_Na = +60 mV). Calculate
  using simplified Goldman equation.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{11}
\tightlist
\item
  Multiple sclerosis (MS) destroys myelin in the CNS. Predict: (a) the
  effect on conduction velocity; (b) which neuronal functions are
  impaired first; (c) why remyelination therapies are being
  investigated; (d) why the PNS is relatively spared (different
  myelinating cells).
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{12}
\tightlist
\item
  Local anaesthetics (lidocaine) block voltage-gated Na\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{+}}{+} channels.
  Explain: (a) why this prevents action potential generation; (b) why
  pain fibres (small, unmyelinated C fibres) are blocked before motor
  fibres (large, myelinated A\texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\alpha}}{alpha} fibres); (c) is this use-dependent block
  (more block with higher firing frequency)?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{13}
\tightlist
\item
  The patellar (knee-jerk) reflex involves a monosynaptic stretch reflex
  arc. Trace the pathway: muscle spindle \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} Ia afferent \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} spinal cord
  (monosynaptic excitation of \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\alpha}}{alpha}-motor neuron) \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} quadriceps contraction.
  Explain: (a) why the reflex is monosynaptic (no interneuron); (b) the
  role of reciprocal inhibition of the hamstring (via an inhibitory
  interneuron).
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{14}
\tightlist
\item
  Sensory adaptation: olfactory receptors rapidly adapt to constant
  odour exposure (within minutes). Explain: (a) the molecular mechanism
  (cAMP \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} Ca\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{2}}{2}\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{+}}{+} \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} calmodulin \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} reduced CNG channel sensitivity); (b) the
  difference between phasic (rapidly adapting) and tonic (slowly
  adapting) receptors; (c) one example of a tonic receptor.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{15}
\tightlist
\item
  The blood-brain barrier (BBB) restricts drug entry into the CNS.
  Explain: (a) the cellular basis (tight junctions between endothelial
  cells, pericytes, astrocyte end-feet); (b) which molecules can cross
  (small, lipophilic, MW \textless{} 400); (c) how L-DOPA (prodrug for
  dopamine) exploits amino acid transporters to bypass the BBB.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{16}
\tightlist
\item
  Neuroplasticity: after a stroke destroys the motor cortex controlling
  the right hand, the left hand often improves in dexterity over weeks.
  Explain: (a) cortical remapping (adjacent cortical areas take over);
  (b) the role of long-term potentiation (LTP) in this process; (c) why
  intensive rehabilitation (constraint-induced movement therapy)
  accelerates recovery.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{17}
\tightlist
\item
  The autonomic nervous system has sympathetic (fight-or-flight) and
  parasympathetic (rest-and-digest) divisions. Compare: (a)
  preganglionic neurotransmitter (both ACh); (b) postganglionic
  neurotransmitter (sympathetic = NE, parasympathetic = ACh); (c)
  effects on heart rate, bronchioles, and GI motility.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{18}
\tightlist
\item
  Pain processing: nociceptors detect tissue damage and transmit signals
  via A\texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\delta}}{delta} (sharp, fast) and C (dull, slow) fibres. Explain the gate
  control theory: how does activation of large-diameter A\texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\beta}}{beta} touch fibres
  ``close the gate'' in the spinal cord dorsal horn, reducing pain
  transmission to the brain?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{19}
\tightlist
\item
  Glial cells (astrocytes, oligodendrocytes, microglia) outnumber
  neurons. Describe two functional roles of astrocytes beyond structural
  support: (a) glutamate uptake at synapses (preventing excitotoxicity);
  (b) regulation of extracellular K\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{+}}{+}; (c) the ``tripartite synapse''
  concept (astrocyte modulates synaptic strength via gliotransmitters).
\end{enumerate}

\subsection*{Questions 21--30: Synthesis and
Evaluation}\label{questions-2130-synthesis-and-evaluation-28}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Questions 21--30: Synthesis and
Evaluation}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{20}
\tightlist
\item
  Evaluate the ``integrate-and-fire'' model of neuronal computation: a
  neuron summates thousands of excitatory and inhibitory postsynaptic
  potentials (EPSPs and IPSPs) and fires when threshold is reached. What
  are the limitations of this model (dendritic computation, non-linear
  integration, backpropagating APs), and how do modern computational
  neuroscience models address them?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{21}
\tightlist
\item
  Design an experiment to determine whether a newly discovered brain
  region is involved in spatial memory rather than procedural memory.
  Describe: (a) lesion studies (selective ablation); (b)
  electrophysiology (place cells, grid cells); (c) optogenetic
  activation/inhibition during a behavioural task; (d) what behavioural
  paradigms (Morris water maze, T-maze) you would use.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{22}
\tightlist
\item
  Evaluate the molecular basis of Alzheimer's disease: (a) A\texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\beta}}{beta} oligomer
  toxicity hypothesis; (b) tau hyperphosphorylation and neurofibrillary
  tangles; (c) the failure of anti-A\texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\beta}}{beta} antibody therapies (lecanemab
  showed modest benefit, 27\% slowing of decline). What does the modest
  efficacy of anti-A\texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\beta}}{beta} antibodies tell us about the ``amyloid cascade''
  as a therapeutic target?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{23}
\tightlist
\item
  Evaluate the role of adult neurogenesis in the hippocampus: (a)
  evidence that new neurons are continuously generated in the
  subgranular zone of the dentate gyrus; (b) the functional role of
  newborn neurons in pattern separation (distinguishing similar
  memories); (c) the controversial evidence for adult neurogenesis in
  humans (Spalding et al., \texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{1}}{1}\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{4}}{4}C birth-dating vs Sorrells et al.,
  immunohistochemistry showing no new neurons after age 13).
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{24}
\tightlist
\item
  Evaluate the mechanism of general anaesthesia: despite \textgreater150
  years of use, the molecular targets of volatile anaesthetics
  (sevoflurane, isoflurane) are incompletely understood. Current
  evidence implicates: (a) GABA\_A receptor potentiation; (b) NMDA
  receptor inhibition; (c) two-pore domain K\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{+}}{+} channel (TREK/TASK)
  activation. How does the combination of these effects produce
  unconsciousness, and why is the ``unitary'' theory of anaesthesia (one
  target) now rejected?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{25}
\tightlist
\item
  Evaluate the concept of ``neural oscillations'' --- rhythmic brain
  activity at specific frequency bands (delta 1--4 Hz, theta 4--8 Hz,
  alpha 8--13 Hz, beta 13--30 Hz, gamma 30--100 Hz). What cognitive
  processes are associated with each band, and what evidence from
  EEG/MEG studies supports the idea that frequency-band-specific
  synchronisation enables ``binding'' of distributed cortical
  representations into a unified percept?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{26}
\tightlist
\item
  Chronic pain involves maladaptive plasticity (central sensitisation)
  in the spinal cord dorsal horn. Evaluate: (a) the molecular mechanism
  (NMDA receptor-dependent wind-up, glial activation, BDNF release); (b)
  why opioids provide temporary relief but worsen chronic pain through
  opioid-induced hyperalgesia (OIH); (c) what non-opioid alternatives
  (gabapentinoids, SNRI antidepressants, spinal cord stimulation) target
  central sensitisation.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{27}
\tightlist
\item
  The enteric nervous system (ENS, ``second brain'') contains
  about 500 million neurons controlling GI motility, secretion,
  and blood flow independently of the CNS. Evaluate: (a) why the ENS is
  sometimes called autonomous (it functions after vagotomy); (b) the
  evidence linking ENS dysfunction to Parkinson's disease (\texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\alpha}}{alpha}-synuclein
  aggregation begins in the ENS years before brain symptoms); (c) how
  the gut-brain axis connects the ENS to cognition and mood.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{28}
\tightlist
\item
  Optogenetics uses light-activated ion channels (channelrhodopsin-2,
  halorhodopsin) to activate or inhibit specific neurons with
  millisecond precision. Evaluate: (a) the technical requirements (viral
  vector delivery of opsin gene, implanted fibre optic); (b) an
  experiment that optogenetics uniquely enables (e.g., activating and
  silencing the same neurons to confirm necessity and sufficiency for a
  behaviour); (c) the path to clinical translation (optogenetic gene
  therapy for retinitis pigmentosa).
\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\setcounter{enumi}{29}
\tightlist
\item
  Critically evaluate the ``connectome'' project --- the effort to map
  every synaptic connection in the human brain (about 86
  billion neurons, about 150 trillion synapses). Is the
  connectome sufficient to understand brain function, or is dynamic
  activity (electrophysiology, neuromodulation) equally important?
  Compare the completed \emph{C. elegans} connectome (302 neurons, fully
  mapped) to our understanding of worm behaviour --- does knowing the
  wiring diagram explain the animal's behaviour? Then apply the same
  evidence-boundary reasoning to a high-performance speech
  neuroprosthesis reported in one participant with paralysis.
\end{enumerate}

\subsection*{Questions 11--20: Application and
