\emph{cella} = small room + Gk \emph{kyklos} = circle{]} --- The ordered
sequence of events by which a cell duplicates its contents and divides:
G\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{1}}{1} \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} S (DNA synthesis) \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} G\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{2}}{2} \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} M (mitosis) \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} cytokinesis. Regulated by
cyclin-CDK complexes and checkpoint kinases. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_IV_dna_replication_and_cell_cycle}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:camkii}{\textbf{CaMKII
(Calcium/calmodulin-dependent kinase II)}} {[}L \emph{calx} = lime (Ca)
+ \emph{calmodulin} + Gk \emph{kinein} = to move{]} --- A
serine/threonine kinase activated by Ca\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{2}}{2}\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{+}}{+}/calmodulin;
autophosphorylation at T286 renders it constitutively active
(``molecular memory''). Key effector of NMDA receptor-dependent LTP:
phosphorylates AMPA receptors (increased conductance) and drives AMPA
receptor exocytosis. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} \cref{sec:unit_IX_action_potential_synapses}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:cardiac-output}{\textbf{Cardiac output
(CO)}} {[}Gk \emph{kardia} = heart + L \emph{emittere} = to send out{]}
--- The volume of blood ejected by the heart per minute: CO = heart rate
(HR) \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\times}}{x} stroke volume (SV). Normal resting CO \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\approx}}{~}5.5 L/min; can reach
20--25 L/min during maximal exercise in athletes. Regulated by the
Frank-Starling mechanism and neurohumoral factors. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_IX_circulation_respiration_homeostasis}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:cdna}{\textbf{cDNA}} {[}complementary
DNA; L \emph{complementum} = that which fills up{]} --- DNA synthesised
from an mRNA template by reverse transcriptase; lacks introns; used in
cloning, expression libraries, and RT-PCR diagnostics. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_IV_gene_expression}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:centromere}{\textbf{Centromere}} {[}Gk
\emph{kentron} = centre + \emph{meros} = part{]} --- The specialised
chromosomal region where kinetochore proteins assemble and spindle
microtubules attach during mitosis and meiosis. Required for accurate
chromosome segregation. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_IV_dna_replication_and_cell_cycle}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:chemiosmosis}{\textbf{Chemiosmosis}}
{[}Gk \emph{chemi} = chemistry + \emph{osmos} = push{]} --- The coupling
of electron transport to ATP synthesis via a proton electrochemical
gradient across a membrane (proton-motive force). Proposed by Peter
Mitchell (1961); Nobel Prize 1978. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_III_bioenergetics_and_respiration}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:chirality}{\textbf{Chirality}} {[}Gk
\emph{cheir} = hand{]} --- The property of a molecule that is
non-superimposable on its mirror image, like a hand. Biology is strongly
homochiral in its core polymers: proteins mostly use L-amino acids,
while nucleic acids and many central metabolites use D-sugars. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_I_atoms_molecules}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:chlorophyll}{\textbf{Chlorophyll}}
{[}Gk \emph{chloros} = green/yellow-green + \emph{phyllon} = leaf{]} ---
A porphyrin-ring pigment containing Mg\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{2}}{2}\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{+}}{+} at its centre; the primary
light-harvesting molecule in photosynthesis. Absorbs strongly at 430 nm
(violet/blue) and 680--700 nm (red). \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_III_photosynthesis}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:chromatin}{\textbf{Chromatin}} {[}Gk
\emph{chroma} = colour{]} --- The complex of DNA and proteins (primarily
histones) that compacts the genome within the nucleus. Exists in two
states: \textbf{euchromatin} (open, transcriptionally active) and
\textbf{heterochromatin} (compact, silenced). The fundamental unit is
the nucleosome. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} \cref{sec:unit_IV_epigenetics_and_gene_regulation}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:chromosome}{\textbf{Chromosome}} {[}Gk
\emph{chroma} = colour + \emph{soma} = body{]} --- A linear (eukaryotic)
or circular (prokaryotic) DNA molecule associated with proteins
(histones in eukaryotes) that carries the cell's hereditary information.
Humans have 46 chromosomes (23 pairs). \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_IV_dna_replication_and_cell_cycle}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:cpg-island}{\textbf{CpG island}} (C =
cytosine; p = phosphodiester bond; G = guanine) --- A genomic region
(about 500 bp--2 kb) enriched for CG dinucleotides;
observed/expected CpG ratio \textgreater{} 0.6; present at
about 70\% of vertebrate gene promoters. Normally unmethylated;
hypermethylation silences the associated promoter in cancer and
differentiation. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} \cref{sec:unit_IV_epigenetics_and_gene_regulation}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:crispr-cas}{\textbf{CRISPR-Cas}} {[}L
\emph{crispus} = clustered + \emph{repetitive} + \emph{palindromic} +
\emph{Cas} = CRISPR-associated protein{]} --- A prokaryotic adaptive
immune system (repeat-spacer arrays + Cas endonucleases) repurposed for
programmable genome editing; Cas9 guided by a synthetic sgRNA cleaves
DNA at a complementary target. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_IV_mutations_and_genomics}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:codon}{\textbf{Codon}} {[}L
\emph{codex} = block of writing{]} --- A three-nucleotide sequence in
mRNA that specifies one amino acid or a stop signal. The genetic code
has 64 codons encoding 20 amino acids (and 3 stop codons); most amino
acids have multiple synonymous codons (degeneracy). \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_IV_gene_expression}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:cortisol}{\textbf{Cortisol}} {[}L
\emph{cortex} = bark, rind{]} --- The primary glucocorticoid secreted by
the adrenal cortex (zona fasciculata) in response to ACTH; mobilises
glucose (gluconeogenesis, protein catabolism), suppresses immunity
(reduces IL-2, PGE2, and T cell activation), and regulates the stress
response. Circadian peak at 06:00--08:00. Synthetic analogues
(prednisone, dexamethasone) are widely used anti-inflammatory agents. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_IX_endocrine_and_immune}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:cohesion-tension-theory}{\textbf{Cohesion-tension
theory}} {[}L \emph{cohaerere} = to stick together + Gk \emph{teinein} =
to stretch{]} --- The mechanism by which water ascends xylem vessels in
plants: evaporation at the leaf surface creates tension (negative
pressure) transmitted through the hydrogen-bonded water column via
adhesion to cell walls. Proposed by Dixon \& Joly (1894). \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_VIII_plant_structure_and_water}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:competitive-inhibition}{\textbf{Competitive
inhibition}} {[}L \emph{competere} = to seek together{]} --- Enzyme
inhibition in which the inhibitor binds the active site and competes
with substrate. Raises apparent K\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{m}}{m} without affecting V\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{m}}{m}\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{a}}{a}\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{x}}{x}; reversed by
increasing \hyperref[s]{S}. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} \cref{sec:unit_I_enzymes_and_kinetics}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:cytoplasm}{\textbf{Cytoplasm}} {[}Gk
\emph{kytos} = cell/vessel + \emph{plasma} = something formed{]} --- The
collective cell contents between the plasma membrane and the nucleus (or
nucleoid); includes cytosol, organelles, ribosomes, and the
cytoskeleton. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} \cref{sec:unit_II_cell_structure}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:cytoskeleton}{\textbf{Cytoskeleton}}
{[}Gk \emph{kytos} = vessel + \emph{skeletos} = dried up{]} --- The
dynamic network of protein filaments --- actin microfilaments (7 nm),
intermediate filaments (10 nm), and microtubules (25 nm) --- that
maintains cell shape, enables motility, and guides intracellular
transport. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} \cref{sec:unit_II_cell_structure}

\begin{center}\rule{0.5\linewidth}{0.5pt}\end{center}

\subsection*{D}\label{d}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{D}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:diploid}{\textbf{Diploid (2n)}} {[}Gk
\emph{diplous} = double + \emph{eidos} = form{]} --- A cell or organism
with two complete sets of homologous chromosomes; one set from each
parent. Human somatic cells are diploid (2n = 46). Contrast:
\textbf{haploid} (n). \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} \cref{sec:unit_V_chromosomal_inheritance}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:dna-helicase}{\textbf{DNA helicase}}
{[}Gk \emph{helix} = spiral{]} --- An ATP-dependent enzyme that unwinds
the DNA double helix at the replication fork by breaking hydrogen bonds
between base pairs; the replicative helicase DnaB in bacteria, MCM
complex in eukaryotes. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_IV_dna_replication_and_cell_cycle}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:dna-ligase}{\textbf{DNA ligase}} {[}L
\emph{ligare} = to bind{]} --- An enzyme that forms phosphodiester bonds
between adjacent nucleotides; joins Okazaki fragments on the lagging
strand; also used in DNA repair and recombinant DNA cloning. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_IV_dna_replication_and_cell_cycle}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:dominant}{\textbf{Dominant}} {[}L
\emph{dominare} = to rule{]} --- Describing an allele whose phenotypic
effect is expressed in both homozygous and heterozygous states. The
recessive allele is masked in the heterozygote. Mendel (1866). \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_V_mendelian_genetics}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:doubling-time}{\textbf{Doubling time
(t\_d)}} {[}OE \emph{dubbel} = twice + L \emph{tempus} = time{]} --- The
time required for a population or culture to double in number;
\(t_d = \ln 2 / \mu\) where \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\mu}}{mu} is the specific growth rate. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_VII_bacteria_archaea_viruses}

\begin{center}\rule{0.5\linewidth}{0.5pt}\end{center}

\subsection*{E}\label{e}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{E}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:electronegativity}{\textbf{Electronegativity}}
{[}Gk \emph{elektron} = amber (as source of static charge) + L
\emph{negativus} = denying{]} --- The tendency of an atom to attract
bonding electrons. Pauling scale: F = 3.98; O = 3.44; N = 3.04; C =
2.55; H = 2.20. Determines bond polarity. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_I_atoms_molecules}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:endocytosis}{\textbf{Endocytosis}}
{[}Gk \emph{endon} = within + \emph{kytos} = vessel{]} --- Uptake of
extracellular material by inward budding of the plasma membrane to form
a vesicle. Subtypes: \textbf{pinocytosis} (fluid/solutes),
\textbf{phagocytosis} (large particles), \textbf{receptor-mediated
endocytosis} (specific ligands via clathrin-coated pits). Contrast:
\textbf{exocytosis}. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} \cref{sec:unit_II_membrane_transport}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:endosymbiosis}{\textbf{Endosymbiosis}}
{[}Gk \emph{endon} = within + \emph{sym} = together + \emph{bios} =
life{]} --- A relationship in which one organism lives within another
over evolutionary time, eventually becoming an organelle. The
mitochondrion (about 1.5 Ga ago) and chloroplast
(about 1.2 Ga ago) both originated by endosymbiosis of
bacterial cells (Margulis, 1967). \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} \cref{sec:unit_II_cell_theory}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:entropy}{\textbf{Entropy (S)}} {[}Gk
\emph{en} = in + \emph{trope} = transformation{]} --- A thermodynamic
state function often described as energy dispersal or the number of
accessible microstates. For spontaneous processes in an isolated system,
total entropy increases (\(\Delta S_{universe} > 0\)). Living organisms
maintain ordered internal structures by exchanging matter and energy
with surroundings. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} \cref{sec:unit_III_bioenergetics_and_respiration}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:enzyme}{\textbf{Enzyme}} {[}Gk
\emph{en} = in + \emph{zyme} = leaven/ferment{]} --- A biological
catalyst --- almost always a protein, sometimes RNA (ribozyme) --- that
accelerates a reaction by lowering the activation energy without being
consumed. Characterised by specificity, saturation kinetics
(Michaelis-Menten), and allosteric regulation. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_I_enzymes_and_kinetics}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:epigenetics}{\textbf{Epigenetics}}
{[}Gk \emph{epi} = above/upon + \emph{genet-} = birth; coined by
Waddington, 1942{]} --- Heritable changes in gene expression that do not
alter the underlying DNA sequence. Molecular carriers: CpG methylation,
histone post-translational modifications (acetylation, methylation,
phosphorylation), and non-coding RNAs (miRNA, lncRNA, piRNA). \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_IV_epigenetics_and_gene_regulation}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:epigenome}{\textbf{Epigenome}} {[}Gk
\emph{epi} = upon + \emph{genos} = origin + \emph{-ome} = total{]} ---
The complete set of epigenetic modifications across a cell's genome;
cell-type specific and environmentally modifiable, unlike the genome
sequence. Mapped by ENCODE and Roadmap Epigenomics projects. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_IV_mutations_and_genomics}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:euchromatin}{\textbf{Euchromatin}}
{[}Gk \emph{eu} = true/good + \emph{chroma} = colour{]} --- Loosely
packed chromatin associated with H3K4me3 and H3K27ac histone marks;
transcriptionally permissive. Contrast: \textbf{heterochromatin}. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_IV_epigenetics_and_gene_regulation}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:excitotoxicity}{\textbf{Excitotoxicity}}
{[}L \emph{excitare} = to rouse + Gk \emph{toxikon} = poison{]} ---
Neuronal death caused by excessive glutamate receptor activation
(especially NMDA), leading to massive Ca\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{2}}{2}\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{+}}{+} influx, mitochondrial
dysfunction, caspase activation, and necrosis/apoptosis. The primary
mechanism of neuronal death in ischaemic stroke. Target of
neuroprotective strategies. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_IX_action_potential_synapses}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:eukaryote}{\textbf{Eukaryote}} {[}Gk
\emph{eu} = true + \emph{karyon} = nucleus{]} --- An organism whose
cells contain a membrane-enclosed nucleus and membrane-bound organelles.
Includes protists, fungi, plants, and animals. Contrast:
\textbf{prokaryote}. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} \cref{sec:unit_II_cell_theory}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:exon}{\textbf{Exon}} {[}Gk \emph{exo} =
outside; coined by Gilbert, 1978{]} --- A coding sequence in a
eukaryotic gene that is retained in the mature mRNA after splicing and
is translated into protein. Contrast: \textbf{intron}. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_IV_gene_expression}

\begin{center}\rule{0.5\linewidth}{0.5pt}\end{center}

\subsection*{F}\label{f}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{F}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:fev-fvc}{\textbf{FEV\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{1}}{1}/FVC}} {[}forced
expiratory volume/forced vital capacity{]} --- The fraction of vital
capacity exhaled in the first second of a forced expiration; obstruction
is best interpreted against the age-dependent lower limit of normal,
with a fixed 0.70 threshold used as a simple COPD screening convention.
Restrictive patterns usually preserve or raise the ratio while reducing
absolute lung volumes. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_IX_circulation_respiration_homeostasis}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:fatty-acid}{\textbf{Fatty acid}} {[}ME
\emph{fat} + Gk \emph{oxys} = acid/sharp{]} --- A carboxylic acid with a
hydrocarbon chain. Saturated fatty acids pack tightly; unsaturated
\emph{cis} double bonds introduce bends that increase membrane fluidity.
\texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} \cref{sec:unit_I_macromolecules}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:fisheries}{\textbf{Fisheries}} {[}OE
\emph{fisc} = fish{]} --- Human-managed harvest systems for aquatic
populations; modern stock assessment uses age structure, recruitment,
mortality, and maximum sustainable yield models to avoid collapse. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_X_population_ecology,sec:unit_X_biomes_and_conservation}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:frank-starling-law}{\textbf{Frank-Starling
law}} {[}named for Otto Frank (1895) and Ernest Starling (1914){]} ---
The intrinsic property of cardiac muscle whereby stroke volume increases
with end-diastolic volume (preload): greater stretch of sarcomeres
increases Ca\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{2}}{2}\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{+}}{+} sensitivity of troponin C, increasing force generation.
Operates up to an optimal sarcomere length (about 2.2 \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\mu}}{mu}m);
beyond this, overlap of thick and thin filaments decreases. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_IX_circulation_respiration_homeostasis}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:facilitated-diffusion}{\textbf{Facilitated
diffusion}} {[}L \emph{facilis} = easy + \emph{diffundere} = to pour
out{]} --- Passive transport of molecules down their concentration
gradient via membrane proteins (channels or carriers); no energy
required. Contrast: \textbf{active transport}. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_II_membrane_transport}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:fitness}{\textbf{Fitness (w)}} {[}OE
\emph{gefittan} = to be suitable{]} --- In evolutionary biology, the
relative contribution of a genotype to the next generation; often
expressed as \(w = 1 - s\) where \(s\) is the selection coefficient. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_V_population_genetics}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:free-energy}{\textbf{Free energy (\texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\Delta}}{Delta}G)}}
{[}Gk \emph{eleutheros} = free{]} --- Gibbs free energy; the energy
available to do work at constant temperature and pressure:
\(\Delta G = \Delta H - T\Delta S\). Spontaneous reactions have
\(\Delta G < 0\) (exergonic). \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_III_bioenergetics_and_respiration}

\begin{center}\rule{0.5\linewidth}{0.5pt}\end{center}

\subsection*{G}\label{g}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{G}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:glp-1}{\textbf{GLP-1 (glucagon-like
peptide-1)}} {[}L \emph{glucos} = sweet + \emph{lysis} = splitting{]}
--- An incretin hormone secreted by intestinal L cells in response to
nutrient ingestion; potentiates glucose-dependent insulin secretion
(GSIS) from beta cells; suppresses glucagon; delays gastric emptying;
reduces appetite via hypothalamic signalling. GLP-1 receptor agonists
(semaglutide, tirzepatide) are transformative in treating type 2
diabetes and obesity. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} \cref{sec:unit_IX_endocrine_and_immune}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:glut4}{\textbf{GLUT4}} {[}glucose
transporter type 4{]} --- The insulin-sensitive glucose transporter
expressed in muscle and adipose tissue; stored in intracellular
vesicles; translocated to the plasma membrane within minutes of insulin
receptor activation (PI3K--Akt--AS160 cascade). Responsible for up to
90\% of post-prandial muscle glucose uptake. Impaired GLUT4 trafficking
underlies insulin resistance in type 2 diabetes. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_IX_endocrine_and_immune}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:gamete}{\textbf{Gamete}} {[}Gk
\emph{gamete} = wife; \emph{gametes} = husband; from \emph{gamein} = to
marry{]} --- A haploid reproductive cell (sperm or egg) that fuses with
another gamete during fertilisation to restore the diploid number. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_V_chromosomal_inheritance}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:gene}{\textbf{Gene}} {[}Gk \emph{genos}
= birth/origin; coined by Johannsen, 1909{]} --- A heritable unit of
information encoded in DNA that typically specifies the sequence of a
protein or functional RNA; operationally defined as a sequence occupying
a defined chromosomal locus. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_IV_epigenetics_and_gene_regulation}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:genetic-code}{\textbf{Genetic code}}
{[}Gk \emph{genos} = birth + L \emph{codex} = writing block{]} --- The
mapping from 64 mRNA codons to 20 amino acids and stop signals. It is
nearly universal, degenerate, and read by tRNA anticodons during
translation. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} \cref{sec:unit_IV_gene_expression}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:genome}{\textbf{Genome}} {[}Gk
\emph{genos} = birth + \emph{-ome} = total body of{]} --- The complete
set of genetic information in an organism, including nuclear
chromosomes, mitochondrial DNA, and in plants, chloroplast DNA. Human
haploid genome: about 3.2 Gb, about 20,000
protein-coding genes. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} \cref{sec:unit_IV_mutations_and_genomics}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:genome-wide-association-study}{\textbf{Genome-wide
association study (GWAS)}} {[}Eng \emph{genome} + \emph{wide} +
\emph{association}{]} --- A population scan correlating millions of SNP
genotypes with a trait or disease; identifies tag loci (not always
causal genes); requires large samples and correction for multiple
testing. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} \cref{sec:unit_IV_mutations_and_genomics}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:glycolysis}{\textbf{Glycolysis}} {[}Gk
\emph{glykys} = sweet + \emph{lysis} = splitting{]} --- The 10-step
cytosolic pathway that converts glucose (6C) to 2 pyruvate (3C),
yielding a net 2 ATP and 2 NADH per glucose under standard textbook
accounting. It does not require oxygen directly and is among the most
ancient and widespread central metabolic pathways, though some organisms
use modified glycolytic routes. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_III_bioenergetics_and_respiration}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:gram-stain}{\textbf{Gram stain}}
{[}named for Hans Christian Gram, Danish bacteriologist, 1884{]} --- A
differential microbiological stain that distinguishes
thick-peptidoglycan bacteria (Gram-positive: retain crystal violet,
purple) from thin-peptidoglycan + outer membrane bacteria
(Gram-negative: lose crystal violet, pink after safranin counterstain).
\texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} \cref{sec:unit_II_cell_theory}

\begin{center}\rule{0.5\linewidth}{0.5pt}\end{center}

\subsection*{H}\label{h}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{H}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:hpa-axis}{\textbf{HPA axis
(hypothalamic--pituitary--adrenal axis)}} {[}Gk \emph{hypo} = under +
\emph{thalamos} = inner chamber{]} --- The neuroendocrine stress axis:
CRH (hypothalamus) \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} ACTH (anterior pituitary) \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} cortisol (adrenal
cortex). Regulated by negative feedback at hypothalamus and pituitary.
Dysregulation implicated in depression, PTSD, and Cushing's syndrome. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_IX_endocrine_and_immune}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:hpg-axis}{\textbf{HPG axis
(hypothalamic--pituitary--gonadal axis)}} --- GnRH (hypothalamus) \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} FSH
+ LH (anterior pituitary) \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} sex steroids + gametes (gonads). Pulsatile
GnRH (every 90 min) is required for normal FSH/LH secretion; continuous
GnRH causes receptor downregulation and gonadotropin suppression. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_IX_endocrine_and_immune}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:hpt-axis}{\textbf{HPT axis
(hypothalamic--pituitary--thyroid axis)}} --- TRH (hypothalamus) \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} TSH
(anterior pituitary) \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} T4/T3 (thyroid gland). T3 is the active form;
acts on nuclear receptors to increase metabolic rate, thermogenesis, and
cardiac output. Hypothyroidism: TSH \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\uparrow}}{up}; hyperthyroidism: TSH \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\downarrow}}{down}. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_IX_endocrine_and_immune}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:haploidy}{\textbf{Haploidy (n)}} {[}Gk
\emph{haplous} = single + \emph{eidos} = form{]} --- Condition of having
one complete set of chromosomes; characteristic of gametes and the
gametophyte generation of plants. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_V_chromosomal_inheritance}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:hardy-weinberg-equilibrium}{\textbf{Hardy-Weinberg
equilibrium}} {[}named for Godfrey Hardy, mathematician, and Wilhelm
Weinberg, physician, 1908{]} --- The principle that allele and genotype
frequencies remain constant in a population absent of evolutionary
forces (no selection, drift, mutation, migration, non-random mating).
Genotype frequencies: \(p^2 + 2pq + q^2 = 1\). \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_V_population_genetics}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:heterozygous}{\textbf{Heterozygous}}
{[}Gk \emph{heteros} = different + \emph{zygotos} = yoked{]} ---
Possessing two different alleles at a given locus (e.g., \emph{Aa}).
Contrast: \textbf{homozygous} (\emph{AA} or \emph{aa}). \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_V_mendelian_genetics}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:hill-coefficient}{\textbf{Hill
coefficient (n)}} {[}named for Archibald Hill, 1910{]} --- A measure of
cooperativity in ligand binding. \(n = 1\) = no cooperativity; \(n > 1\)
= positive cooperativity (sigmoidal binding curve). Haemoglobin:
\(n \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\approx}}{~} 2.8\). \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} \cref{sec:unit_I_enzymes_and_kinetics}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:homeostasis}{\textbf{Homeostasis}}
{[}Gk \emph{homoios} = similar + \emph{stasis} = standing/state{]} ---
The maintenance of a relatively stable internal environment despite
external fluctuations; achieved by negative feedback loops with a
sensor, comparator (integrator), and effector. Coined by Walter Cannon
(1926, building on Claude Bernard). \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} \cref{sec:unit_IX_nervous_system}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:heterochromatin}{\textbf{Heterochromatin}}
{[}Gk \emph{heteros} = different + \emph{chroma} = colour{]} --- Densely
compacted chromatin bearing repressive histone marks (H3K9me3, H3K27me3)
and high DNA methylation; transcriptionally silent.
\textbf{Constitutive} heterochromatin (centromeres, telomeres) is
permanent; \textbf{facultative} heterochromatin (e.g., the inactive X
chromosome) is cell-type specific. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_IV_epigenetics_and_gene_regulation}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:histone}{\textbf{Histone}} {[}Gk
\emph{histos} = loom/web{]} --- One of five abundant nuclear proteins
(H1, H2A, H2B, H3, H4) that form the nucleosome core and linker. Tails
are post-translationally modified by acetylation, methylation,
phosphorylation, and ubiquitination to regulate gene expression (histone
code). \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} \cref{sec:unit_IV_epigenetics_and_gene_regulation}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:histone-code}{\textbf{Histone code}}
{[}Gk \emph{histos} = loom; L \emph{codex} = writing block{]} --- The
hypothesis (Strahl \& Allis, 2000) that combinations of histone
post-translational modifications specify unique chromatin states;
`written' by HATs/HMTs, `read' by bromodomains/chromodomains, `erased'
by HDACs/KDMs. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} \cref{sec:unit_IV_epigenetics_and_gene_regulation}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:holobiont}{\textbf{Holobiont}} {[}Gk
\emph{holos} = whole + \emph{bios} = life{]} --- The host plus its
persistent associated microbiota (and sometimes viruses) treated as an
integrated biological system; useful for analysing nutrition, immunity,
and niche construction. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_VII_bacteria_archaea_viruses,sec:unit_VII_microbial_ecology}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:hydrogen-bond}{\textbf{Hydrogen bond}}
{[}Gk \emph{hydor} = water + \emph{genes} = born from (as in generated
with water){]} --- A weak electrostatic attraction (2--40 kJ/mol)
between a hydrogen atom covalently bonded to an electronegative atom (N,
O, or F) and another electronegative atom. Critical for DNA
base-pairing, protein secondary structure, and water's unique
properties. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} \cref{sec:unit_I_atoms_molecules}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:hydrolysis}{\textbf{Hydrolysis}} {[}Gk
\emph{hydor} = water + \emph{lysis} = loosening{]} --- Cleavage of a
chemical bond by addition of water; central to digestion, ATP turnover,
polymer breakdown, and many enzyme-catalysed reaction mechanisms. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_I_macromolecules,sec:unit_I_enzymes_and_kinetics}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:hydrophobic-effect}{\textbf{Hydrophobic
effect}} {[}Gk \emph{hydor} = water + \emph{phobos} = fear{]} --- The
entropy-driven clustering of nonpolar surfaces in water as ordered water
cages are released. It drives membrane assembly, protein folding, and
ligand binding. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_I_water_and_life,sec:unit_I_macromolecules}

\begin{center}\rule{0.5\linewidth}{0.5pt}\end{center}

\subsection*{I}\label{i}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{I}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:insulin-receptor}{\textbf{Insulin
receptor}} {[}L \emph{insula} = island, as in islets of Langerhans{]}
--- A receptor tyrosine kinase (RTK) composed of two \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\alpha}}{alpha} and two \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\beta}}{beta}
subunits; insulin binding activates RTK, triggering autophosphorylation
and IRS-1/2 phosphorylation; downstream: PI3K--Akt (GLUT4 translocation,
glycogen synthesis) and MAPK (gene expression, cell growth). Type 2
diabetes involves insulin receptor signalling resistance. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_IX_endocrine_and_immune}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:independent-assortment}{\textbf{Independent
assortment}} {[}L \emph{independens} = not hanging upon{]} --- Mendel's
second law: genes on non-homologous chromosomes are inherited
independently of each other, producing 9:3:3:1 ratios in dihybrid
crosses. Applies only to genes on different chromosomes or far apart on
the same chromosome. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} \cref{sec:unit_V_mendelian_genetics}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:intron}{\textbf{Intron}} {[}L
\emph{intra} = within; coined by Sharp \& Roberts, 1977{]} --- A
non-coding intervening sequence within a eukaryotic gene that is
transcribed but removed from the pre-mRNA by the spliceosome before
translation. Nobel Prize 1993 (Sharp \& Roberts). \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_IV_gene_expression}

\begin{center}\rule{0.5\linewidth}{0.5pt}\end{center}

\subsection*{K}\label{k}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{K}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:keystone-species}{\textbf{Keystone
species}} {[}L \emph{lapis} = stone; \emph{clavus} = key{]} --- A
species with a disproportionately large effect on its ecosystem relative
to its biomass; its removal causes dramatic shifts in community
structure. Term coined by Robert Paine (1966) based on sea-star
(\emph{Pisaster}) removal experiments. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_X_community_ecology}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:km}{\textbf{Km (Michaelis constant)}}
{[}after Leonor Michaelis{]} --- The substrate concentration at which an
enzyme operates at half its maximum velocity (V\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{m}}{m}\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{a}}{a}\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{x}}{x}/2); reflects
enzyme-substrate affinity (lower K\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{m}}{m} = higher affinity). Units: mol/L
(M). \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} \cref{sec:unit_I_enzymes_and_kinetics}

\begin{center}\rule{0.5\linewidth}{0.5pt}\end{center}

\subsection*{L}\label{l}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{L}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:ltp}{\textbf{LTP (long-term
potentiation)}} {[}L \emph{longum} = long + \emph{tempus} = time +
\emph{potentia} = power{]} --- A persistent (hours to days) increase in
synaptic efficacy following high-frequency stimulation; requires NMDA
receptor activation \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} Ca\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{2}}{2}\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{+}}{+} influx \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} CaMKII autophosphorylation \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} AMPA
receptor insertion; the cellular model of learning and memory (Bløndell,
Lømo 1973). \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} \cref{sec:unit_IX_action_potential_synapses}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:ltd}{\textbf{LTD (long-term
depression)}} {[}L \emph{deprimere} = to press down{]} --- A persistent
decrease in synaptic efficacy; induced by low-frequency stimulation (1
Hz) or by mGluR/endocannabinoid signalling (``endocannabinoid-mediated
LTD''); involves PP1/PP2A phosphatase activation and AMPA receptor
internalisation via dynamin-clathrin endocytosis. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_IX_action_potential_synapses}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:linkage}{\textbf{Linkage}} {[}ON
\emph{hlenkr} = chain link{]} --- The tendency of genes located on the
same chromosome to be inherited together; the closer the genes, the
stronger the linkage (lower recombination frequency). \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_V_chromosomal_inheritance}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:locus}{\textbf{Locus (plural: loci)}}
{[}L \emph{locus} = place{]} --- The fixed chromosomal position occupied
by a particular gene; defined by its physical map coordinates (base pair
position) or genetic map position (centimorgans from a reference
marker). \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} \cref{sec:unit_V_chromosomal_inheritance}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:lotka-volterra-equations}{\textbf{Lotka-Volterra
equations}} {[}named for Alfred Lotka (1925) and Vito Volterra (1926){]}
--- A pair of coupled nonlinear ODEs describing predator-prey population
cycles: \(dN/dt = \alpha N - \beta NP\) (prey) and
\(dP/dt = \delta NP - \gamma P\) (predator). Produce neutrally stable
oscillatory dynamics. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} \cref{sec:unit_X_community_ecology}

\begin{center}\rule{0.5\linewidth}{0.5pt}\end{center}

\subsection*{M}\label{m}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{M}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:mrna}{\textbf{mRNA (messenger RNA)}}
{[}L \emph{nuntius} = messenger{]} --- An RNA molecule transcribed from
a gene's template strand; carries the codon sequence from the nucleus to
the ribosome for translation into protein. Processed in eukaryotes by 5'
capping, 3' polyadenylation, and splicing. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_IV_gene_expression}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:meiosis}{\textbf{Meiosis}} {[}Gk
\emph{meiosis} = lessening{]} --- Two successive cell divisions ---
Meiosis I (reductional; homologue separation) and Meiosis II
(equational; sister chromatid separation) --- that produce four haploid
gametes from one diploid cell. Sources of genetic diversity:
crossing-over and independent assortment. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_V_chromosomal_inheritance}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:membrane-potential}{\textbf{Membrane
potential (Vm)}} {[}L \emph{membrana} = thin skin + \emph{potentia} =
power{]} --- The electric potential difference across a biological
membrane; in neurons at rest, approximately \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{-}}{-}70 mV (inside negative).
Governed by the Goldman equation for multiple ion species. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_IX_circulation_respiration_homeostasis}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:michaelis-menten-kinetics}{\textbf{Michaelis-Menten
kinetics}} {[}after Leonor Michaelis \& Maud Menten, 1913{]} --- The
standard kinetic model for enzyme catalysis:
\(v = V_{max}[S]/(K_m + [S])\). Assumes rapid equilibrium or
steady-state complex formation and one substrate. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_I_enzymes_and_kinetics}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:microbiome}{\textbf{Microbiome}} {[}Gk
\emph{mikros} + \emph{bios} + \emph{-ome}{]} --- The full complement of
microorganisms (bacteria, archaea, fungi, viruses) and their genes in a
defined environment (e.g., gut, rhizosphere); often profiled by
metagenomic sequencing. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} \cref{sec:unit_VII_bacteria_archaea_viruses}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:microbiota}{\textbf{Microbiota}} {[}Gk
\emph{mikros} + \emph{bios} + \emph{-ota} collective{]} --- The
assemblage of microorganisms themselves (contrast \textbf{microbiome},
which often denotes genes and functions as well). \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_VII_bacteria_archaea_viruses}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:microrna}{\textbf{MicroRNA (miRNA)}}
{[}Gk \emph{mikros} = small{]} --- A about 22 nt
single-stranded RNA that directs post-transcriptional gene silencing;
biogenesis: Drosha (nuclear) \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} pre-miRNA \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} Dicer (cytoplasmic) \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
AGO2/RISC; partial 3'UTR complementarity causes translational repression
and mRNA decay. \textgreater{} 2,000 human miRNAs regulate
about 60\% of protein-coding genes. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_IV_epigenetics_and_gene_regulation}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:mitosis}{\textbf{Mitosis}} {[}Gk
\emph{mitos} = thread{]} --- Cell division in which one diploid cell
produces two genetically identical diploid daughter cells; consists of
prophase, metaphase, anaphase, and telophase followed by cytokinesis. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_IV_dna_replication_and_cell_cycle}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:mutation}{\textbf{Mutation}} {[}L
\emph{mutare} = to change{]} --- A heritable change in genetic sequence,
including substitutions, insertions, deletions, inversions,
duplications, and translocations. Mutation creates new sequence
variants; recombination, segregation, gene flow, and selection then
reshape how those variants are combined and distributed in populations.
\texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} \cref{sec:unit_IV_mutations_and_genomics}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:5-methylcytosine}{\textbf{5-Methylcytosine
(5mC)}} --- The ``fifth base'' of DNA; cytosine methylated at C5 by DNMT
enzymes using S-adenosylmethionine as methyl donor. Silences promoters
via MBD protein recruitment; oxidised to 5-hydroxymethylcytosine (5hmC)
by TET enzymes for active demethylation. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_IV_epigenetics_and_gene_regulation}

\begin{center}\rule{0.5\linewidth}{0.5pt}\end{center}

\subsection*{N}\label{n}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{N}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:natural-selection}{\textbf{Natural
selection}} {[}L \emph{natura} = nature; \emph{selectio} = choosing{]}
--- The process by which heritable variations that increase survival or
reproduction become more common in a population over generations.
Proposed by Darwin \& Wallace (1858). \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_V_population_genetics}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:niche}{\textbf{Niche}} {[}OFr
\emph{nicher} = to nest{]} --- The totality of an organism's role in its
environment, including physical conditions (temperature, pH, resources)
it can use and interactions with other species. \textbf{Fundamental
niche}: possible without competition. \textbf{Realised niche}: actual
range when competitors are present. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_X_community_ecology}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:nucleosome}{\textbf{Nucleosome}} {[}L
\emph{nucleus} = nut kernel + Gk \emph{soma} = body{]} --- The
fundamental repeating unit of chromatin: 147 bp of DNA wound
about 1.65 turns around a histone octamer (H2A, H2B, H3, H4 \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\times}}{x}
2); diameter 11 nm. First visualised by electron microscopy (Kornberg,
1974; Nobel Prize 2006). \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_IV_epigenetics_and_gene_regulation}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:nucleotide}{\textbf{Nucleotide}} {[}Gk
\emph{nucleus} = kernel + L \emph{nucleus} = nut kernel{]} --- The
monomer of nucleic acids: a nitrogenous base + pentose sugar + one to
three phosphate groups. Adenine, guanine (purines); cytosine, thymine,
uracil (pyrimidines). \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_IV_dna_replication_and_cell_cycle}

\begin{center}\rule{0.5\linewidth}{0.5pt}\end{center}

\subsection*{O}\label{o}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{O}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:organelle}{\textbf{Organelle}} {[}Gk
\emph{organon} = tool/instrument + \emph{ella} = diminutive suffix{]}
--- A membrane-bound (or in some definitions, functionally discrete)
structure within a eukaryotic cell, performing a specialised function.
Examples: nucleus, mitochondrion, chloroplast, Golgi apparatus,
lysosome. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} \cref{sec:unit_II_cell_structure}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:osmosis}{\textbf{Osmosis}} {[}Gk
\emph{osmos} = pushing{]} --- The movement of water across a selectively
permeable membrane from a region of lower solute concentration (higher
water potential) to a region of higher solute concentration (lower water
potential). Van 't Hoff equation: \(\pi = iCRT\). \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_II_membrane_transport}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:oxidative-phosphorylation}{\textbf{Oxidative
phosphorylation}} {[}L \emph{oxidare} = to oxidise + Gk
\emph{phosphoros} = light-bearer{]} --- The ATP-generating process
driven by electron transfer from NADH/FADH\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{2}}{2} to O\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{2}}{2} via the electron
transport chain, producing the proton-motive force used by ATP synthase.
Yields about 28 of the about 30--32 ATP per glucose. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_III_bioenergetics_and_respiration}

\begin{center}\rule{0.5\linewidth}{0.5pt}\end{center}

\subsection*{P}\label{p}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{P}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:p}{\textbf{P\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{5}}{5}\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{0}}{0}}} {[}partial pressure at
which haemoglobin is 50\% saturated{]} --- A measure of haemoglobin-O\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{2}}{2}
affinity; normal P\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{5}}{5}\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{0}}{0} = 26--27 mmHg. Rightward shifts (increased P\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{5}}{5}\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{0}}{0}) =
decreased affinity: caused by increased PCO\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{2}}{2}, H\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{+}}{+}, temperature, 2,3-BPG
(Bohr effect). Leftward shifts = increased affinity: caused by decreased
PCO\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{2}}{2}, alkalosis, hypothermia, foetal Hb. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_IX_circulation_respiration_homeostasis}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:pan-genome}{\textbf{Pan-genome}} {[}Gk
\emph{pan} = all + \emph{genome}{]} --- The union of the collective
genes found across a species or clade when many strains are sequenced;
comprises a \textbf{core} genome (shared) and \textbf{accessory} genes
(variable). Explains strain-specific virulence and metabolic
capabilities in bacteria. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} \cref{sec:unit_IV_mutations_and_genomics}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:poiseuille-s-law}{\textbf{Poiseuille's
law}} {[}named for Jean Léonard Marie Poiseuille, 1840{]} --- Laminar
flow of a viscous fluid in a cylindrical tube:
\(Q = \pi r^4 \Delta P / 8\eta L\), where \(r\) = radius, \(\Delta P\) =
pressure gradient, \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\eta}}{eta} = viscosity, \(L\) = length. The \(r^4\) dependence
explains why small changes in vessel radius (e.g., arteriolar
vasodilation) produce large changes in flow and vascular resistance. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_IX_circulation_respiration_homeostasis}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:peptide-bond}{\textbf{Peptide bond}}
{[}Gk \emph{pepsis} = digestion; peptides were initially thought to be
digestion products{]} --- The covalent bond (--CO--NH--) formed by
condensation between the carboxyl group of one amino acid and the amino
group of another during translation. Has partial double-bond character
(resonance; about 40\% double bond), conferring planarity. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_I_macromolecules}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:ph}{\textbf{pH}} {[}Danish
\emph{potenz} = power + Gk \emph{hydro} = water; coined by Sørensen,
1909{]} --- The negative common logarithm of hydrogen ion activity:
\(pH = -\log_{10}[H^+]\). Physiological range: blood plasma 7.35--7.45;
lysosomes 4.5--5.0; mitochondrial matrix 7.8--8.0. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_I_atoms_molecules}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:phenotype}{\textbf{Phenotype}} {[}Gk
\emph{phainein} = to show + \emph{typos} = impression{]} --- The
observable characteristics of an organism, determined by the interaction
of genotype with environment. Contrast: \textbf{genotype}. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_V_mendelian_genetics}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:phospholipid-bilayer}{\textbf{Phospholipid
bilayer}} {[}Gk \emph{phosphoros} = light-bearer + L \emph{lipidus} =
fat{]} --- A self-assembled membrane structure in which amphipathic
lipids orient hydrophilic heads toward aqueous environments and
hydrophobic tails inward; typical thickness is about 7--8 nm.
It is the dominant membrane architecture in bacteria and eukaryotes,
while archaeal membranes often use ether-linked isoprenoid lipids and
can form monolayers. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} \cref{sec:unit_II_membrane_transport}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:photosynthesis}{\textbf{Photosynthesis}}
{[}Gk \emph{phos/photos} = light + \emph{synthesis} = putting
together{]} --- The process by which photosynthetic organisms use light
energy to produce organic compounds from CO\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{2}}{2} and H\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{2}}{2}O; in plants: light
reactions (thylakoids; produce ATP + NADPH) + Calvin cycle (stroma; fix
CO\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{2}}{2} into G3P). \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} \cref{sec:unit_III_photosynthesis}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:plasmid}{\textbf{Plasmid}} {[}Gk
\emph{plasma} = formed thing{]} --- A small, circular, double-stranded
DNA molecule in bacteria (and some eukaryotes) that replicates
independently of the chromosome; often carries genes for antibiotic
resistance or virulence. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} \cref{sec:unit_II_cell_theory}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:polymerase-chain-reaction}{\textbf{Polymerase
chain reaction (PCR)}} {[}Gk \emph{polys} = many + L \emph{merus} =
part; Gk \emph{kyklos} = circle; coined by Kary Mullis, 1983{]} --- An
\emph{in vitro} method for amplifying a specific DNA sequence using
repeated cycles of denaturation, primer annealing, and extension by Taq
polymerase. Transformed molecular biology; Nobel Prize 1993. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_IV_mutations_and_genomics}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:promoter}{\textbf{Promoter}} {[}L
\emph{promovere} = to move forward{]} --- A DNA sequence upstream of a
gene where RNA polymerase and transcription factors bind to initiate
transcription. In prokaryotes: \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{-}}{-}10 (Pribnow box) and \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{-}}{-}35 elements; in
eukaryotes: TATA box, initiator, and Pol II general transcription
factors. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} \cref{sec:unit_IV_gene_expression}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:protein}{\textbf{Protein}} {[}Gk
\emph{proteios} = of the first quality; coined by Mulder \& Berzelius,
1838{]} --- A polymer of L-amino acids linked by peptide bonds; encoded
by the gene sequence; functional form depends on primary (1°), secondary
(2°), tertiary (3°), and quaternary (4°) structure. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_I_macromolecules}

\begin{center}\rule{0.5\linewidth}{0.5pt}\end{center}

\subsection*{R}\label{r}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{R}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:raas}{\textbf{RAAS
(renin--angiotensin--aldosterone system)}} {[}L \emph{ren} = kidney{]}
--- The hormonal blood pressure and volume regulatory cascade: low renal
perfusion \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} juxtaglomerular cells release renin \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} cleaves
angiotensinogen to angiotensin I \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} ACE (lung) converts to angiotensin II
\texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} vasoconstriction + aldosterone release (Na\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{+}}{+}/H\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{2}}{2}O retention). ACE
inhibitors (enalapril) and ARBs (losartan) are first-line
antihypertensive drugs. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_IX_circulation_respiration_homeostasis}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:recombination}{\textbf{Recombination}}
{[}L \emph{re} = again + \emph{combinare} = to combine{]} --- The
process of generating new combinations of alleles through crossing-over
between homologous chromosomes during meiosis I. Frequency (\texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\theta}}{theta}) is
proportional to genetic map distance (1 cM = 1\% recombination). \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_V_chromosomal_inheritance}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:reduction-potential}{\textbf{Reduction
potential (E°\texorpdfstring{'}{'})}} {[}L \emph{reducere} = to lead back{]} --- The
tendency of a molecule to accept electrons, measured in volts under
standard biochemical conditions (pH 7, 25°C). O\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{2}}{2}/H\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{2}}{2}O: +0.816 V;
NAD\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{+}}{+}/NADH: \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{-}}{-}0.320 V. Electrons flow from lower to higher E°\texorpdfstring{'}{'}. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_I_atoms_molecules}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:ribonucleic-acid}{\textbf{Ribonucleic
acid (RNA)}} {[}L nucleus + suffix \emph{ic}{]} --- A single-stranded
nucleic acid using ribose and uracil (instead of deoxyribose and
thymine); roles include mRNA (messenger), tRNA (transfer), rRNA
(ribosomal), and regulatory (miRNA, siRNA, snRNA). \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_IV_gene_expression}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:ribosome}{\textbf{Ribosome}} {[}named
for ribose + Gk \emph{soma} = body{]} --- The ribonucleoprotein complex
(about 2.5 MDa in eukaryotes; 80S = 40S + 60S subunits) that
catalyses peptide bond formation during translation; catalytic activity
resides in rRNA (a ribozyme). Nobel Prize 2009 (Ramakrishnan, Steitz,
Yonath). \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} \cref{sec:unit_IV_gene_expression}

\begin{center}\rule{0.5\linewidth}{0.5pt}\end{center}

\subsection*{S}\label{s}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{S}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:saltatory-conduction}{\textbf{Saltatory
conduction}} {[}L \emph{saltare} = to jump{]} --- The rapid propagation
of action potentials in myelinated axons by jumping from one node of
Ranvier to the next; velocity proportional to internodal distance; 5--70
m/s vs 0.5--2 m/s in unmyelinated C fibres. Enabled by high Na\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{+}}{+} channel
density at nodes and insulation by myelin between nodes. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_IX_action_potential_synapses}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:snare-complex}{\textbf{SNARE complex}}
{[}acronym: \textbf{S}oluble \textbf{N}-ethylmaleimide-sensitive factor
\textbf{A}ttachment protein \textbf{RE}ceptors{]} --- The core vesicle
fusion machinery: v-SNARE (synaptobrevin/VAMP-2, on vesicle) + t-SNAREs
(syntaxin-1A and SNAP-25, on target membrane) zipper together in a
four-helix bundle providing the energy for membrane fusion. Cleaved by
clostridial neurotoxins (botulinum toxin cleaves SNAP-25/VAMP; tetanus
toxin cleaves VAMP in spinal inhibitory interneurons). \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_IX_action_potential_synapses}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:surfactant}{\textbf{Surfactant}} {[}L
\emph{superficies} = surface + \emph{activus} = active{]} --- A complex
mixture of phospholipids (primarily DPPC) and proteins (SP-A, SP-B,
SP-C, SP-D) secreted by alveolar type II pneumocytes; reduces alveolar
surface tension according to Laplace's law (\(P = 2T/r\)), preventing
alveolar collapse (atelectasis) during expiration and reducing the work
of breathing. Deficiency causes neonatal respiratory distress syndrome
(RDS). \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} \cref{sec:unit_IX_circulation_respiration_homeostasis}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:synaptotagmin}{\textbf{Synaptotagmin}}
{[}Gk \emph{synapsis} = junction + \emph{tagma} = arrangement{]} --- The
Ca\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{2}}{2}\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{+}}{+} sensor for fast neurotransmitter release; C2A and C2B domains bind
3--5 Ca\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{2}}{2}\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{+}}{+} ions cooperatively (Hill coefficient n\texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\approx}}{~}4), explaining Ca\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{2}}{2}\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{+}}{+}
cooperativity of neurotransmitter release. Synaptotagmin-1 drives
synchronous fast release; synaptotagmin-7 drives asynchronous release
and facilitatory plasticity. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_IX_action_potential_synapses}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:selection-coefficient}{\textbf{Selection
coefficient (s)}} {[}see \emph{natural selection}{]} --- A quantitative
measure of the fitness disadvantage (or advantage) conferred by an
allele; \(s = 1 - w\) where \(w\) is relative fitness. Dominant lethal:
\(s = 1\); neutral: \(s = 0\). \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} \cref{sec:unit_V_population_genetics}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:speciation}{\textbf{Speciation}} {[}L
\emph{species} = appearance/kind{]} --- The evolutionary process by
which one ancestral population diverges into two or more reproductively
isolated species. Mechanisms: \textbf{allopatric} (geographic
isolation), \textbf{sympatric} (within a range; polyploidy, disruptive
selection). \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} \cref{sec:unit_VI_genetic_drift_and_speciation}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:species-area-relationship}{\textbf{Species-area
relationship}} {[}L \emph{species} = kind + \emph{area} = open space{]}
--- The empirical relationship \(S = cA^z\) between species richness
(\(S\)) and area (\(A\)); exponent \(z \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\approx}}{~} 0.25\) for continental
habitats, \(z \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\approx}}{~} 0.30\) for island habitats. MacArthur \& Wilson (1967).
\texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} \cref{sec:unit_X_biomes_and_conservation}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:surface-area-to-volume-ratio}{\textbf{Surface-area-to-volume
ratio (A/V)}} {[}L \emph{superficies} = surface{]} --- For a sphere:
\(A/V = 3/r\). As cell radius increases, \(A/V\) decreases, limiting
diffusion-based nutrient exchange; this constraint accounts for why
cells are microscopically small. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} \cref{sec:unit_II_cell_theory}

\begin{center}\rule{0.5\linewidth}{0.5pt}\end{center}

\subsection*{T}\label{t}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{T}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:thermodynamics}{\textbf{Thermodynamics}}
{[}Gk \emph{therme} = heat + \emph{dynamis} = power{]} --- The branch of
physical science concerned with heat, work, and energy transformations.
First Law: energy is conserved. Second Law: entropy increases in any
spontaneous process. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} \cref{sec:unit_III_bioenergetics_and_respiration}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:transcription}{\textbf{Transcription}}
{[}L \emph{transcribere} = to copy{]} --- The synthesis of an RNA
molecule from a DNA template by RNA polymerase; proceeds 5\texorpdfstring{'}{'} to 3\texorpdfstring{'}{'}
reading the template strand 3\texorpdfstring{'}{'} to 5\texorpdfstring{'}{'}; regulated by transcription
factors, promoters, and enhancers. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} \cref{sec:unit_IV_gene_expression}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:translation}{\textbf{Translation}} {[}L
\emph{translatio} = carrying across{]} --- The ribosome-mediated
synthesis of a polypeptide from an mRNA template; proceeds from 5\texorpdfstring{'}{'} to 3\texorpdfstring{'}{'}
(mRNA), adding amino acids from N- to C-terminus at about 15
residues/second (eukaryotes). \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} \cref{sec:unit_IV_gene_expression}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:transpiration}{\textbf{Transpiration}}
{[}L \emph{trans} = across + \emph{spirare} = to breathe{]} --- The
evaporation of water from leaf mesophyll cells and its diffusion through
stomata; drives the transpiration stream (cohesion-tension mechanism)
and enables mineral transport in xylem. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_VIII_plant_structure_and_water}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:trophic-level}{\textbf{Trophic level}}
{[}Gk \emph{trophe} = nourishment{]} --- A functional tier in a food web
defined by the number of energy-transfer steps from primary producers;
approximately 10\% of energy passes between levels (Lindeman's
trophic-dynamic theory, 1942). \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} \cref{sec:unit_X_ecosystem_ecology}

\begin{center}\rule{0.5\linewidth}{0.5pt}\end{center}

\subsection*{V}\label{v}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{V}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:van-der-waals-forces}{\textbf{Van der
Waals forces}} {[}named for Johannes Diderik van der Waals, 1873{]} ---
Weak, short-range intermolecular attractions (0.1--10 kJ/mol) arising
from transient (London dispersion), permanent-induced (Debye), or
permanent-permanent (Keesom) dipole interactions. Important for packing
of hydrophobic molecules and protein-ligand recognition. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_I_atoms_molecules}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:virulence}{\textbf{Virulence}} {[}L
\emph{virulentus} = full of poison{]} --- The capacity of a pathogen to
cause disease; quantified as the proportion of infected hosts that
develop disease or die. Virulence factors include toxins, adhesins,
capsules, and immune evasion mechanisms. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_VII_bacteria_archaea_viruses}

\begin{center}\rule{0.5\linewidth}{0.5pt}\end{center}

\subsection*{W}\label{w}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{W}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:water-potential}{\textbf{Water
potential (\texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\Psi}}{Psi})}} {[}named analogy to electrical potential{]} --- A
measure of the free energy of water in a system relative to pure water:
\(\Psi = \Psi_s + \Psi_p\) (solute + pressure components). Water moves
from high \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\Psi}}{Psi} to low \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\Psi}}{Psi} (down the gradient). Units: megapascals (MPa). \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_VIII_plant_structure_and_water}

\begin{center}\rule{0.5\linewidth}{0.5pt}\end{center}

\subsection*{X}\label{x}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{X}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:xylem}{\textbf{Xylem}} {[}Gk
\emph{xylon} = wood{]} --- The vascular tissue that conducts water and
dissolved minerals from roots to aerial organs; composed of non-living
tracheids and vessel members (dead at maturity) plus parenchyma and
fibres. Water moves by cohesion-tension mechanism. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_VIII_plant_structure_and_water}

\begin{center}\rule{0.5\linewidth}{0.5pt}\end{center}

\subsection*{Z}\label{z}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Z}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:zygote}{\textbf{Zygote}} {[}Gk
\emph{zygotos} = yoked{]} --- The diploid cell formed by the fusion of
two haploid gametes during fertilisation; the first cell of a new
organism; undergoes mitotic divisions to form the embryo. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_V_mendelian_genetics}

\begin{center}\rule{0.5\linewidth}{0.5pt}\end{center}

\emph{This glossary covers about 120 core terms.
Chapter-specific key terms are listed in each chapter's Key Terms
section. For full index, see the combined PDF output.}

\begin{center}\rule{0.5\linewidth}{0.5pt}\end{center}

\subsection*{Additional Terms (Units III --
X)}\label{additional-terms-units-iii-x}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{Additional Terms (Units III -- X)}

\subsubsection*{C (continued)}\label{c-continued}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsubsection}{C (continued)}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:carrying-capacity}{\textbf{Carrying
capacity (K)}} {[}L \emph{capax} = able to hold{]} --- The maximum
number of individuals an environment can support indefinitely,
determined by resource availability; the equilibrium of the logistic
growth model dN/dt = rN(1 \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{-}}{-} N/K). \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} \cref{sec:unit_X_population_ecology}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:chloroplast}{\textbf{Chloroplast}}
{[}Gk \emph{chloros} = green + \emph{plastos} = formed{]} --- A
double-membrane plant organelle derived from a cyanobacterial
endosymbiont; contains the thylakoid membranes (light reactions) and
stroma (Calvin cycle); its own circular genome encodes about 80
proteins. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} \cref{sec:unit_III_photosynthesis}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:coevolution}{\textbf{Coevolution}} {[}L
\emph{co-} = together + \emph{evolutio} = unrolling{]} --- The
reciprocal evolutionary change in two or more species exerting strong
selective pressure on each other; classic examples: plant-pollinator
mutualism, host-parasite arms races, flowering plant-butterfly chemical
coevolution (Ehrlich \& Raven, 1964). \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_X_community_ecology}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:competitive-exclusion}{\textbf{Competitive
exclusion}} {[}L \emph{competere} = to strive together +
\emph{excludere} = to shut out{]} --- Gause's competitive exclusion
principle (1934): two species competing for identical limiting resources
cannot coexist indefinitely at equilibrium; one will be excluded. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_X_community_ecology}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:copepod}{\textbf{Copepod}} {[}Gk
\emph{kope} = oar + \emph{pous/podos} = foot{]} --- A crustacean
subclass of small aquatic organisms forming a major component of marine
and freshwater zooplankton; primary consumers linking phytoplankton to
larger predators in ocean food webs. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_X_ecosystem_ecology}

\subsubsection*{D (continued)}\label{d-continued}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsubsection}{D (continued)}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:decomposer}{\textbf{Decomposer}} {[}L
\emph{de} = down + \emph{componere} = put together{]} --- An organism
(primarily bacteria and fungi) that breaks dead organic matter into
inorganic nutrients through enzymatic digestion; drives nutrient cycling
in every ecosystem. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} \cref{sec:unit_X_ecosystem_ecology}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:density-dependent-regulation}{\textbf{Density-dependent
regulation}} {[}L \emph{densus} = thick{]} --- A population regulatory
mechanism whose effect (per-capita birth or death rate) changes as a
function of population density; resource competition, disease, and
predation are density-dependent. Contrast: \textbf{density-independent}
factors (e.g., floods, fires). \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} \cref{sec:unit_X_population_ecology}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:depolarisation}{\textbf{Depolarisation}}
{[}L \emph{de} = away from + Gk \emph{polos} = pivot{]} --- A decrease
in magnitude of membrane potential (movement toward zero or positive
values); in neurons, caused by Na\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{+}}{+} influx through voltage-gated channels
during the rising phase of an action potential. Contrast:
\textbf{repolarisation}, \textbf{hyperpolarisation}. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_IX_nervous_system}

\subsubsection*{E (continued)}\label{e-continued}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsubsection}{E (continued)}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:effective-population-size}{\textbf{Effective
population size (N\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{e}}{e})}} {[}Gk \emph{effectivus} = productive{]} --- An
idealised census number equivalent to the actual population in terms of
rate of genetic drift; typically much smaller than the census size due
to unequal sex ratios, variance in reproductive success, and population
size fluctuations. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\sigma}}{sigma}\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{2}}{2}(\texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\Delta}}{Delta}p) = pq/2N\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{e}}{e}. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_VI_genetic_drift_and_speciation}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:epiphyte}{\textbf{Epiphyte}} {[}Gk
\emph{epi} = upon + \emph{phyton} = plant{]} --- A plant that grows on
another plant for physical support without parasitising it; absorbs
water and nutrients from rain and air; orchids, bromeliads, and ferns
are prominent epiphytes. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} \cref{sec:unit_X_biomes_and_conservation}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:eutrophication}{\textbf{Eutrophication}}
{[}Gk \emph{eutrophos} = well-nourished{]} --- Nutrient enrichment of an
aquatic body (typically N and P from agricultural runoff) triggering
algal blooms; subsequent decomposition of algal biomass depletes
dissolved oxygen, causing hypoxic dead zones. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_X_ecosystem_ecology}

\subsubsection*{F (continued)}\label{f-continued}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsubsection}{F (continued)}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:fermentation}{\textbf{Fermentation}}
{[}L \emph{fermentum} = leaven{]} --- Anaerobic metabolic process
regenerating NAD\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{+}}{+} by reducing pyruvate to lactate (lactic acid
fermentation) or to ethanol + CO\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{2}}{2} (alcoholic fermentation); net gain: 2
ATP/glucose. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} \cref{sec:unit_III_bioenergetics_and_respiration}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:founder-effect}{\textbf{Founder
effect}} {[}OE \emph{funden} = to establish{]} --- A form of genetic
drift in which allele frequencies in a new population established from a
small group of founders differ from the source population by chance; can
lead to high prevalence of otherwise rare alleles. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_VI_genetic_drift_and_speciation}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:frond}{\textbf{Frond}} {[}L
\emph{frons/frondis} = leafy branch{]} --- The large leaf of a fern or
other pteridophyte; bears sporangia on its underside (in a sorus);
anatomically equivalent to a compound leaf. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_VIII_plant_structure_and_water}

\subsubsection*{G (continued)}\label{g-continued}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsubsection}{G (continued)}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:genetic-drift}{\textbf{Genetic drift}}
{[}ON \emph{drift} = a driving of snow{]} --- Random, chance changes in
allele frequencies in a population from generation to generation due to
sampling error in finite populations; stronger effect in small
populations. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} \cref{sec:unit_VI_genetic_drift_and_speciation}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:gpp}{\textbf{GPP (gross primary
productivity)}} {[}Gk \emph{ge} = earth + \emph{protos} = first + L
\emph{producere}{]} --- The total rate of photosynthetic carbon fixation
by producers; GPP \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{-}}{-} Ra (autotrophic respiration) = NPP (net primary
productivity). \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} \cref{sec:unit_X_ecosystem_ecology}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:guard-cell}{\textbf{Guard cell}} {[}ME
\emph{garde} = protection + L \emph{cella} = small room{]} --- One of
two kidney-shaped epidermal cells flanking a stoma; changes in turgor
pressure (driven by K\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{+}}{+} and water movement) open or close the stomatal
pore to regulate gas exchange and water loss. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_VIII_plant_structure_and_water}

\subsubsection*{H (continued)}\label{h-continued}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsubsection}{H (continued)}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:herd-immunity}{\textbf{Herd immunity}}
{[}ME \emph{herd} = flock + L \emph{immunis} = exempt{]} --- Indirect
protection of susceptible individuals when a sufficiently large
proportion of the population is immune (vaccinated or recovered),
reducing pathogen transmission; threshold: p\_c = 1 \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{-}}{-} 1/R\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{0}}{0}. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_VII_bacteria_archaea_viruses}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:herbivory}{\textbf{Herbivory}} {[}L
\emph{herba} = grass + \emph{vorare} = to devour{]} --- Consumption of
plant or algal tissue by an animal or other organism; herbivores occupy
the second trophic level; plant defences (thorns, secondary metabolites,
trichomes) and herbivore counter-adaptations drive coevolution. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_X_community_ecology}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:hormone}{\textbf{Hormone}} {[}Gk
\emph{hormaein} = to set in motion{]} --- A chemical signal produced in
one part of an organism that travels (via blood in animals, phloem in
plants) to act on distant target cells bearing specific receptors; plant
hormones (phytohormones) include auxin, gibberellin, cytokinin, abscisic
acid, and ethylene. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_VIII_plant_reproduction,sec:unit_IX_endocrine_and_immune}

\subsubsection*{I (continued)}\label{i-continued}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsubsection}{I (continued)}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:innate-immunity}{\textbf{Innate
immunity}} {[}L \emph{innatus} = inborn{]} --- The non-specific,
evolutionarily ancient first-line defence against pathogens; includes
physical barriers (skin, mucous membranes), phagocytes (neutrophils,
macrophages), complement, and pattern recognition receptors (TLRs
detecting PAMPs). Acts within minutes to hours. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_IX_endocrine_and_immune}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:intrinsic-rate-of-increase}{\textbf{Intrinsic
rate of increase (r)}} {[}L \emph{intrinsecus} = inward{]} --- The
per-capita growth rate of a population under ideal (unlimited)
conditions; r = ln(\texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\lambda}}{lambda}) where \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\lambda}}{lambda} is the per-generation finite rate of
increase; positive r = growing population; r = 0 at K. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_X_population_ecology}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:island-biogeography}{\textbf{Island
biogeography}} {[}OE \emph{ealand} = island + Gk \emph{ge} = earth +
\emph{graphein} = to write{]} --- The study of factors affecting species
richness of islands (or habitat patches); key model: species richness at
equilibrium = balance between immigration rate and extinction rate;
species-area law \(S = cA^z\) (MacArthur \& Wilson, 1967). \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_X_biomes_and_conservation}

\subsubsection*{K (continued)}\label{k-continued}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsubsection}{K (continued)}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:k-strategist}{\textbf{K-strategist}}
{[}see \emph{carrying capacity} + Gk \emph{strategia} = strategy{]} ---
An organism with a life history strategy maximising competitive success
near carrying capacity: slow growth, long lifespan, large body, few
offspring with high parental investment. Contrast:
\textbf{r-strategist}. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} \cref{sec:unit_X_population_ecology}

\subsubsection*{L (continued)}\label{l-continued}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsubsection}{L (continued)}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:life-table}{\textbf{Life table}} {[}ME
\emph{lyf} + L \emph{tabula} = flat board{]} --- A tabular display of
age-specific survival (lx) and fecundity (mx) values for a cohort; used
to calculate net reproductive rate (R\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{0}}{0} = \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\Sigma}}{Sigma} lx\texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\cdot}}{.}mx) and intrinsic rate of
increase (r). \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} \cref{sec:unit_X_population_ecology}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:logistic-growth}{\textbf{Logistic
growth}} {[}Gk \emph{logistikos} = skilled in reckoning{]} ---
Population growth model dN/dt = rN(1 \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{-}}{-} N/K), producing a sigmoidal
S-shaped curve; growth decelerates as population approaches carrying
capacity K; introduced by Verhulst (1838). \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_X_population_ecology}

\subsubsection*{M (continued)}\label{m-continued}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsubsection}{M (continued)}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:minimum-viable-population}{\textbf{Minimum
viable population (MVP)}} {[}L \emph{minimus} = smallest + \emph{vita} =
life{]} --- The smallest population size with a specified probability
(e.g., 99\%) of persisting for a given period (e.g., 1,000 years);
accounts for demographic stochasticity, environmental stochasticity, and
genetic factors; used in conservation planning. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_X_biomes_and_conservation}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:molecular-clock}{\textbf{Molecular
clock}} {[}Gk \emph{molecula} + OE \emph{clokke}{]} --- The approximate
constancy of the rate of neutral nucleotide substitution in lineages;
enables dating of evolutionary divergence events: t = d/(2\texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\mu}}{mu}) where d =
sequence divergence, \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\mu}}{mu} = substitution rate per year. Calibrated using
the fossil record. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} \cref{sec:unit_VI_genetic_drift_and_speciation}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:mutualism}{\textbf{Mutualism}} {[}L
\emph{mutuus} = mutual, reciprocal{]} --- A symbiotic relationship
benefiting both participating species (+/+); examples: mycorrhizal fungi
increasing plant phosphorus uptake, nitrogen-fixing \emph{Rhizobium} in
legume root nodules, cleaner fish and reef fish. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_X_community_ecology}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:mycorrhiza}{\textbf{Mycorrhiza}} {[}Gk
\emph{mykes} = fungus + \emph{rhiza} = root{]} --- A mutualistic
association between soil fungi (Glomeromycota for arbuscular type;
Basidiomycota/Ascomycota for ectomycorrhizal type) and plant roots;
fungi receive photosynthate, plant receives water and phosphorus;
present in about 80\% of land plants. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_VIII_plant_structure_and_water}

\subsubsection*{N (continued)}\label{n-continued}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsubsection}{N (continued)}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:neuron}{\textbf{Neuron}} {[}Gk
\emph{neuron} = nerve, sinew{]} --- The basic signalling unit of the
nervous system; consists of a cell body (soma), dendrites (input), and
an axon (output); classified by function (sensory, motor, interneuron)
or morphology; communicates via electrical (action potentials) or
chemical (synaptic) signals. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} \cref{sec:unit_IX_nervous_system}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:neutral-theory}{\textbf{Neutral
theory}} {[}L \emph{neutralis} = neither + Gk \emph{theoria} = view{]}
--- Kimura's (1968) theory that the majority of molecular evolutionary
change is selectively neutral (neither advantageous nor deleterious);
neutral mutations drift to fixation at a rate equal to the mutation rate
(u), independent of population size. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_VI_genetic_drift_and_speciation}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:nitrification}{\textbf{Nitrification}}
{[}L \emph{nitrum} = saltpetre + \emph{facere} = to make{]} --- The
aerobic microbial oxidation of ammonium (NH\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{4}}{4}\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{+}}{+}) to nitrite (NO\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{2}}{2}\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{-}}{-}) by
\emph{Nitrosomonas}, then nitrite to nitrate (NO\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{3}}{3}\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{-}}{-}) by
\emph{Nitrobacter}; a key step in the nitrogen cycle making nitrogen
available to most plants. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} \cref{sec:unit_X_ecosystem_ecology}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:nitrogen-fixation}{\textbf{Nitrogen
fixation}} {[}L \emph{nitrum} + \emph{fixatio} = making firm{]} --- The
enzymatic reduction of atmospheric N\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{2}}{2} to NH\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{3}}{3} by nitrogenase; performed
by free-living bacteria (\emph{Azotobacter}, cyanobacteria) and
symbionts (\emph{Rhizobium}, \emph{Frankia}); rate about 120 Tg
N/yr globally. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} \cref{sec:unit_VII_bacteria_archaea_viruses}

\subsubsection*{O (continued)}\label{o-continued}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsubsection}{O (continued)}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:operon}{\textbf{Operon}} {[}L
\emph{opus} = work{]} --- A prokaryotic gene cluster transcribed as a
polycistronic mRNA from a single promoter; regulated by
operator/repressor interactions; the \emph{lac} operon (Jacob \& Monod,
1961) was the first characterised gene regulatory system; Nobel Prize
1965. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} \cref{sec:unit_IV_gene_expression}

\subsubsection*{P (continued)}\label{p-continued}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsubsection}{P (continued)}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:parasite}{\textbf{Parasite}} {[}Gk
\emph{parasitos} = one who eats beside another{]} --- An organism that
benefits from living in or on a host organism at the host's expense
(+/\texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{-}}{-}); parasites reduce host fitness without immediately killing the
host (unlike predators); include worms (helminths), protozoa, and many
bacteria and fungi. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} \cref{sec:unit_VII_bacteria_archaea_viruses}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:photoperiodism}{\textbf{Photoperiodism}}
{[}Gk \emph{photos} = light + L \emph{periodus} = cycle{]} --- The
response of an organism to the relative duration of day and night
(photoperiod); controls flowering (long-day vs.~short-day
vs.~day-neutral plants) via phytochrome, a red/far-red reversible
photoreceptor. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} \cref{sec:unit_VIII_plant_responses}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:phytochrome}{\textbf{Phytochrome}}
{[}Gk \emph{phyton} = plant + \emph{chroma} = colour{]} --- A plant
photoreceptor protein interconvertible between a red-light-absorbing
form (Pr, 660 nm) and a far-red-light-absorbing form (Pfr, 730 nm); Pfr
is the biologically active form; governs seed germination, shade
avoidance, and flowering. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} \cref{sec:unit_VIII_plant_responses}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:phytoplankton}{\textbf{Phytoplankton}}
{[}Gk \emph{phyton} = plant + \emph{planktos} = wandering{]} ---
