Microscopic photosynthetic organisms (cyanobacteria, diatoms,
dinoflagellates) drifting in the photic zone of aquatic ecosystems;
responsible for about 50\% of Earth's net primary productivity.
\texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} \cref{sec:unit_X_ecosystem_ecology}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:population-genetics}{\textbf{Population
genetics}} {[}L \emph{populus} = people + Gk \emph{genos} = birth +
\emph{statistike} = statecraft{]} --- The study of allele and genotype
frequency distributions and their changes in populations; mathematical
foundation provided by Hardy, Weinberg (1908), Fisher, Wright, and
Haldane (1930s). \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} \cref{sec:unit_V_population_genetics}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:primary-succession}{\textbf{Primary
succession}} {[}L \emph{primus} = first + \emph{successio} =
following{]} --- Ecological succession on a surface not previously
colonised (e.g., bare rock after a lava flow or retreating glacier);
begins with pioneer species (lichenised fungi, mosses) and proceeds
through intermediate stages to a climax community. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_X_community_ecology}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:proton-motive-force}{\textbf{Proton-motive
force (\texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\Delta}}{Delta}p)}} {[}Gk \emph{proton} = first + L \emph{movere} = to move{]}
--- The electrochemical driving force for proton movement across a
membrane, composed of a chemical gradient (\texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\Delta}}{Delta}pH) and an electrical
gradient (\texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\Delta}}{Delta}\texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\Psi}}{Psi}); \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\Delta}}{Delta}p (mV) = \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\Delta}}{Delta}\texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\Psi}}{Psi} \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{-}}{-} 59 \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\Delta}}{Delta}pH; drives ATP synthase rotation. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_III_bioenergetics_and_respiration}

\subsubsection*{R (continued)}\label{r-continued}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsubsection}{R (continued)}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:reflex-arc}{\textbf{Reflex arc}} {[}L
\emph{reflectere} = to bend back{]} --- The neural pathway of a reflex
response: stimulus \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} sensory neuron \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} integration centre (interneuron in
spinal cord or brain) \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} motor neuron \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} effector; characterised by
Sherrington (1906). \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} \cref{sec:unit_IX_nervous_system}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:reproductive-isolation}{\textbf{Reproductive
isolation}} {[}L \emph{reproducere} = to produce again + \emph{isolatus}
= set apart{]} --- The existence of biological barriers (prezygotic or
postzygotic) preventing interbreeding between populations; the
operational criterion for separate species status in the Biological
Species Concept (Mayr). \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_VI_genetic_drift_and_speciation}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:r-strategist}{\textbf{r-strategist}}
{[}see \emph{r}, rate of increase + Gk \emph{strategia}{]} --- An
organism with a life history strategy maximising reproductive rate (r):
small body, rapid maturation, large clutch sizes, little parental
investment; thrives in unstable, unpredictable environments. Contrast:
\textbf{K-strategist}. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} \cref{sec:unit_X_population_ecology}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:resting-potential}{\textbf{Resting
potential}} {[}ME \emph{resten} + L \emph{potentialis}{]} --- The stable
membrane potential of a non-stimulated neuron (about \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{-}}{-}70 mV
inside relative to outside); maintained by the sodium-potassium pump (3
Na\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{+}}{+} out, 2 K\texorpdfstring{\textsuperscript{+}}{+} in per ATP) and selective membrane permeability. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_IX_nervous_system}

\subsubsection*{S (continued)}\label{s-continued}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsubsection}{S (continued)}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:saprophyte}{\textbf{Saprophyte}} {[}Gk
\emph{sapros} = rotten + \emph{phyton} = plant{]} --- An organism that
obtains nutrients by absorbing dissolved organic compounds from dead or
decaying matter; now more precisely called saprotrophic or decomposer;
includes most fungi and many bacteria. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_X_ecosystem_ecology}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:secondary-succession}{\textbf{Secondary
succession}} {[}L \emph{secundus} = following + \emph{successio}{]} ---
Ecological succession in an area where a previous community has been
disrupted (fire, flood, deforestation) but soil and seed bank remain;
faster than primary succession; classic example: forest regeneration
after clear-cutting. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} \cref{sec:unit_X_community_ecology}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:self-organization}{\textbf{Self-organization}}
{[}OE \emph{self} + Gk \emph{organon} = tool/instrument{]} --- The
emergence of ordered pattern from local interactions without central
control; examples include biofilms, morphogen gradients, flocking, and
vegetation patching in drylands. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_I_water_and_life,sec:unit_X_population_ecology}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:shannon-diversity-index}{\textbf{Shannon
diversity index (H')}} {[}after Claude Shannon's information entropy,
1948{]} --- A measure of species diversity: H' = \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{-}}{-}\texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\Sigma}}{Sigma}p\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{i}}{i} ln p\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{i}}{i} where p\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{i}}{i} is
the relative abundance of species i; higher H' = greater diversity; H' =
0 for a monoculture; simultaneously measures species richness and
evenness. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} \cref{sec:unit_X_community_ecology}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:signal-transduction}{\textbf{Signal
transduction}} {[}L \emph{signum} = mark + \emph{transducere} = to lead
across{]} --- The process by which a receptor converts an extracellular
signal (ligand, light, mechanical force) into an intracellular
biochemical response via cascades of protein-protein interactions and
phosphorylation events. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} \cref{sec:unit_II_cell_signaling}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:snp}{\textbf{SNP (single-nucleotide
polymorphism)}} {[}genetics abbreviation{]} --- A common single-base
genomic variant, usually defined by minor allele frequency of at least
1\% in a population; used as a marker in GWAS, ancestry inference, and
risk prediction. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_IV_mutations_and_genomics,sec:unit_V_mendelian_genetics}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:stomata}{\textbf{Stomata}} (sing.
stoma) {[}Gk \emph{stoma} = mouth{]} --- Microscopic pores in the leaf
epidermis flanked by guard cells; regulate CO\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{2}}{2} entry for photosynthesis
and water vapour exit (transpiration); respond to light, CO\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{2}}{2}
concentration, and ABA. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} \cref{sec:unit_VIII_plant_structure_and_water}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:succession}{\textbf{Succession}} {[}L
\emph{successio} = a following{]} --- The directional, predictable
change in species composition of a community over time from initial
colonisation to a relatively stable climax community; driven by
facilitation, inhibition, or tolerance mechanisms. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_X_community_ecology}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:survivorship-curve}{\textbf{Survivorship
curve}} {[}L \emph{super} = beyond + \emph{vivere} = to live{]} --- A
graph of the proportion of a cohort surviving to each age; Type I (most
survive to old age; humans, large mammals); Type II (constant mortality
rate; many birds); Type III (high early mortality; marine invertebrates,
most plants). \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} \cref{sec:unit_X_population_ecology}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:sympatric-speciation}{\textbf{Sympatric
speciation}} {[}Gk \emph{sym} = together + L \emph{patria} = homeland{]}
--- Speciation occurring within a single geographic area without
physical barriers; common in plants via allopolyploidy; also documented
in cichlids and apple maggot flies. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_VI_genetic_drift_and_speciation}

\subsubsection*{T (continued)}\label{t-continued}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsubsection}{T (continued)}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:t-helper-cell}{\textbf{T helper cell
(Th)}} {[}L \emph{thymus} + ME \emph{helpen}{]} --- A CD4+ T lymphocyte
that coordinates adaptive immunity; Th1 cells activate cytotoxic T cells
and macrophages (intracellular pathogens); Th2 cells activate B cells
(antibody production, extracellular pathogens); regulatory T cells
(Treg) suppress autoimmunity. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} \cref{sec:unit_IX_endocrine_and_immune}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:telomere}{\textbf{Telomere}} {[}Gk
\emph{telos} = end + \emph{meros} = part{]} --- Repetitive non-coding
DNA sequences (TTAGGG)\texorpdfstring{\textsubscript{n}}{n} capping eukaryotic chromosome ends; protect
against exonuclease degradation, end-to-end chromosome fusions, and loss
of information-carrying DNA; shortened with each S phase
(end-replication problem) unless telomerase is expressed. Nobel Prize
2009 (Blackburn, Greider, Szostak). \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_IV_dna_replication_and_cell_cycle}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:thermoregulation}{\textbf{Thermoregulation}}
{[}Gk \emph{therme} = heat + L \emph{regulare} = to rule{]} ---
Maintenance of body temperature within a physiological range;
\textbf{endotherms} (birds, mammals) generate heat metabolically;
\textbf{ectotherms} (reptiles, fish) rely on behavioural and
environmental sources; homeostatic mechanism with hypothalamic
`thermostat'. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} \cref{sec:unit_IX_nervous_system}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:toll-like-receptor}{\textbf{Toll-like
receptor (TLR)}} {[}\emph{Toll} = German interjection of amazement; Toll
pathway discovered in \emph{Drosophila} by Christiane
Nüsslein-Volhard{]} --- A family of pattern-recognition receptors
(TLR1--10 in humans, with additional functional TLRs in other mammals)
expressed on innate immune cells; recognise conserved PAMPs and signal
via MyD88 and TRIF adaptors to activate NF-\texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\kappa}}{kappa}B and IRF3. Dysregulation
linked to sepsis and autoimmune disease. Nobel Prize 2011 (Hoffmann,
Beutler). \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} \cref{sec:unit_IX_endocrine_and_immune}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:totipotency}{\textbf{Totipotency}} {[}L
\emph{totus} = whole + \emph{potens} = powerful{]} --- The ability of a
single cell to develop into a complete organism; characterises
fertilised eggs and early-cleavage blastomeres; plant cells frequently
retain totipotency (basis of tissue culture propagation). \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_VIII_plant_structure_and_water}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:transpiration-stream}{\textbf{Transpiration
stream}} {[}L \emph{trans} + \emph{spirare} = breathe{]} --- The
continuous movement of water from soil through roots, stem, and leaves
to the atmosphere; driven by evaporation from mesophyll cell walls;
responsible for transport of dissolved minerals throughout the plant. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_VIII_plant_structure_and_water}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:trophic-cascade}{\textbf{Trophic
cascade}} {[}Gk \emph{trophe} = nourishment + L \emph{cascata} =
waterfall{]} --- Indirect predator effects on non-prey species,
transmitted down the food chain; top-down cascade: predator suppresses
herbivore \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} vegetation recovers; bottom-up cascade: primary productivity
determines higher trophic levels. Documented in Yellowstone (wolves \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
elk \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} willows \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} beaver \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} hydrology). \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_X_community_ecology}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:turgor-pressure}{\textbf{Turgor
pressure}} {[}L \emph{turgere} = to swell{]} --- The pressure exerted by
the contents of a plant cell against its cell wall when the vacuole is
filled with water; drives cell expansion during growth and maintains
tissue rigidity (wilting = loss of turgor). \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_VIII_plant_structure_and_water}

\subsubsection*{V (continued)}\label{v-continued}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsubsection}{V (continued)}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:vaccine}{\textbf{Vaccine}} {[}L
\emph{vacca} = cow; from Jenner's cowpox inoculation against smallpox,
1796{]} --- A biological preparation conferring immunity against a
specific pathogen; types include live-attenuated (MMR), inactivated
(IPV), subunit (HepB), mRNA (SARS-CoV-2 mRNA-1273, BNT162b2), and viral
vector vaccines. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} \cref{sec:unit_VII_bacteria_archaea_viruses}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:viviparity}{\textbf{Viviparity}} {[}L
\emph{vivus} = alive + \emph{parere} = to beget{]} --- Giving birth to
live young rather than laying eggs; characteristic of most mammals and
some fish, reptiles, and invertebrates; requires placentation (in
eutherian mammals) for gas and nutrient exchange. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->}
\cref{sec:unit_IX_nervous_system}

\subsubsection*{W (continued)}\label{w-continued}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsubsection}{W (continued)}

\protect\phantomsection\label{gl:watershed}{\textbf{Watershed}} {[}OE
\emph{wæter} + OE \emph{scēad} = divide{]} --- The land area draining
into a common body of water (stream, lake, or estuary); the ecological
unit for studying nutrient export, hydrology, and land-use impacts on
aquatic ecosystems; Hubbard Brook watershed experiments (Bormann \&
Likens, 1967) pioneered biogeochemical cycle measurement at watershed
scale. \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\to}}{->} \cref{sec:unit_X_ecosystem_ecology}

\textbf{Appendix G} \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\cdot}}{.} Level 1/3 \texorpdfstring{\ensuremath{\cdot}}{.} Use as reference
\end{quote}

An index of the 139 glossary terms, each with the chapter(s) where the
term is introduced, bolded, or discussed at length. Terms marked in
\textbf{bold} appear as section headings somewhere in the textbook; the
glossary entry carries the full definition.

Each entry follows the pattern:

\begin{verbatim}
**Term** (`#gl:slug`) with semantic chapter links
\end{verbatim}

The \texttt{\#gl:slug} anchor is the canonical location defined in the
master glossary (\breaktt{manuscript/glossary.md}). Full-text search for
the slug string finds every cross-reference.

ToC labels. To verify after editing \texttt{glossary.md}, run
